events.evidence:
**THE DEEPEST ANNECCHINO THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS, AND IT CAME OUT OF A MARRIAGE DOSSIER.** Item 4 of the 1860 Arienzo marriage act's document list is «*Nell'atto di morte dell'**AVO PATERNO** dello stesso*» — the groom's paternal grandfather, **named nowhere in the act itself**. He is named in the bundle, twice: the dossier holds **two copies of the same extract**, on images 30 and 31, and they agree word for word.

**Forchia, Morti 1826, act 8, 14 June 1826**: «*avanti di noi **Angelo d'Ambrosio Sindaco** … del comune di **FORCHIA**, distretto di **NOLA** … sono comparsi **DOMENICO STROFFOLINO**, di anni **quaranta**, di professione **MASSARO** … Contrada detta **MASSERIA STROFFOLINO**, e **SABATINO STROFFOLINO**, di anni **cinquanta**, di professione **bracciale** … ivi Contrada detta **MASSERIA DE' PRETI**, i quali àn dichiarato, che nel giorno stesso **quattordici** del mese di **Giugno** anno suddetto, alle ore **diciassette**, è morto nella sua propria casa **ANTONIO ANNECCHINO**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di anni **settantatre**, di professione **bracciale**, domiciliato ivi, figlio di **DOMENICO ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **ELISABETTA D'ONOFRIO defunta***».

**Seventy-three in June 1826 puts his birth about 1753** — and his own parents, dead before 1826, must belong to the 1720s or 1730s. **That is four documented generations of Annecchino above Sabbatino, and the archive had one.**

**A SABATINO STROFFOLINO of the Masseria de' Preti declared this death**, and Antonio Annecchino's grandson born the following year was called **Sabbatino**. **The act says nothing about why**, and neither does this archive.

**DATED, AND SEPARATED FROM THE OTHER CARMINE ANNECCHINO.** The marriage act said only «*CARMINE ANNECCHINO defunto*». His **death extract is document 2 of the 1860 dossier**: Forchia, act **20**, **8 August 1838**, at twelve, in his own house — **CARMINE ANNECCHINO, born in Forchia, fifty-two, colono, of the MASSERIA DE' PRETI, son of ANTONIO ANNECCHINO and MARIA GUIDA, both already dead**. Declared by **Domenico Stroffolino**, fifty, colono, and **Giovanni Lauriello**, forty, *viaticale*.

**This archive holds a SECOND Carmine Annecchino of Forchia** — the one at the head of «Carmine Annecchino & Maria Carfora», fathering children there from **1883 to 1901**. **A man dead in 1838 did not father a child in 1901**, so the two are now named apart. Neither is claimed as kin to the other; Forchia reused this name.

events.evidence:
**THE GENERATION ABOVE SABBATINO, FROM THE PAPERS HIS MARRIAGE WAS BUILT ON.** The 1860 Arienzo marriage act named him in three words — «*CARMINE ANNECCHINO defunto*» — and this archive had nothing else. **The dossier behind that act is on Antenati and free**, and document 2 is his death extract.

**Forchia, Morti 1838, act 20, 8 August 1838**: «*sono comparsi **DOMENICO STROFFOLINO**, di anni cinquanta, di professione **colono** … e **GIOVANNI LAURIELLO**, di anni quaranta, di professione **viaticale** … i quali àn dichiarato, che nel giorno stesso **otto** del mese di **Agosto** anno corrente, alle ore **dodici**, è morto nella sua propria casa **CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di anni **cinquantadue**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato ivi **Masseria de' Preti**, figlio di **ANTONIO ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **MARIA GUIDA defunta***».

**Born about 1786.** His son's 1825 birth act makes him forty in February 1825, which is 1785; the clerks guessed both. **NOT the Carmine Annecchino of «Carmine Annecchino & Maria Carfora»**, who was fathering children at Forchia in 1901.

events.evidence:
**A BROTHER FOR SABBATINO, FOUND SIX HOURS AFTER THIS HOUSEHOLD WAS CREATED — AND IN A DIFFERENT TOWN'S REGISTER.** Arienzo, Matrimoni **1856**, **act 10**, found while sweeping a marriage volume for FALCO and not for Annecchino at all:

«*Atto di solenne promessa di matrimonio — Num. d'ordine **10**. L'anno mille ottocento cinquanta**sei**, il dì **ventiquattro** di **Marzo** … avanti di Noi **ALFONSO CIOFFI secondo eletto** ed uffiziale dello Stato Civile di **Arienzo** … comparsi nella Casa Comunale **GIACOMO ANNECCHINO**, di anni **trentanove**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **in Forchia**, figlio di **CARMINE ANNECCHINO defunto**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in Forchia, e di **ROSA CEGLIA**, domiciliata in Forchia; e **GIACINTA CAI———**, di anni **trentasette**, nata in **Arienzo**, domiciliata in Arienzo*». Witnesses **ALFONSO VERDICCHIO** and **PASQUALE LAUDATO**.

**Thirty-nine in March 1856 puts his birth about 1817** — **eight years before Sabbatino**, who was born 20 February 1825 to the same two people. *His birth act has not been looked for; the Forchia births of 1817 are `an_ua29046` by the Caserta series, and this archive has never opened them.*

**A FORCHIA MAN MARRYING AN ARIENZO WOMAN AT ARIENZO — WHICH IS WHAT HIS BROTHER DID FOUR YEARS LATER.** Sabbatino married Maria Antonia Carfora at Arienzo in January 1860. **Two brothers, two Arienzo brides, four years apart**, and the archive found the second first.

**THE ACT MARKS CARMINE DEAD AND DOES NOT MARK ROSA CEGLIA.** Her death extract — Forchia, Morti 1852, act 4, **4 April 1852** — is filed in Sabbatino's own marriage dossier and is not in doubt. **This is a clerk's omission and is recorded as one, not as a contradiction.**

**His bride's surname wraps and is left unread**: «*GIACINTA **CAI=***», thirty-seven, born Arienzo about 1819. *This archive holds a GIUSEPPE CAIAZZO married at Arienzo the year before; nothing joins them.*

**THREE GIACOMO ANNECCHINO NOW STAND IN THIS ARCHIVE** — this one of about 1817, and two born at Forchia in **1887** and **1901** to the other Carmine Annecchino. **They are named apart for the same reason the two Carmine were.**

events.evidence:
**THE MARRIAGE, FOUND** — this archive held the household from its children alone. **RE-READ IN FULL FROM THE IMAGE, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58**, and the reading below replaces one that put a «fu» in front of four names the act never puts one in front of.

«*L'anno mille ottocento **sessanta**, il dì **VENTUNO** di **Gennajo**, alle ore ventitre, avanti di Noi **Stefano Sargenti**, uffiziale dello Stato Civile di **ARIENZO**, distretto di **CASERTA** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO**, di anni **trentaquattro**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **Forchia**, figlio di **CARMINE ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **ROSA CEGLIA defunta** … e **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA**, di anni **ventinove**, nata in **ARIENZO**, domiciliata in Arienzo, figlia di **VALERIO CARFORA**, di professione contadino, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **PASQUA MORGILLO defunta***».

**THREE THINGS CHANGE.** The act is of **21 January**, not the twentieth — «*il dì **ventuno***». The groom's own spelling is **SABBATINO**, with two b. And **the bride's father is not marked dead**: see his own row below — and **his forename is FRANCESCO, not what this act was first read to say**.

The church celebration followed on **22 January**, before witnesses read here as **PASQUALE LAUDATO** and **ANTONIO CRISCI** — the last surname is **Crisci**, with no descender, and was published as «Crispi». **How the three lines divide into two witnesses is not certain**: the clerk writes «*Pasquale Lau=/dato, di Antonio/ Crisci*» with no conjunction, and it may be one man «Pasquale Laudato di Antonio» and a second surnamed Crisci. **Left as it reads.**

events.evidence:
**HE WAS BORN ON 20 FEBRUARY 1825, AND THE ACT IS IN THE ARIENZO PROCESSETTI, NOT AT FORCHIA.** Document 1 of the 1860 dossier is his birth extract, issued by the **Officio dello stato civile di FORCHIA**, act **5** of 1825: «*L'anno mille ottocento **venticinque**, il dì **venti** del mese di **Febbrajo**, ad ore sedici, avanti di Noi **Giacinto Stroffolino Sindaco** … del comune di **FORCHIA**, distretto di **NOLA** … è comparso **CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, di anni **quaranta**, di professione **bracciale**, domiciliato in detto Comune **contrada detta li PRETI**, quale ci à presentato un **maschio** … lo stesso è nato da **ROSA CEGLIA sua moglie legittima**, di anni **trenta**, domiciliata con esso, e da **lui dichiarante***». Baptised the same day; the *indicazione* names the child **SABATINO ANNECCHINO** and the parish as **San Nicola**.

**It agrees with the marriage act exactly.** He is «*di anni trentaquattro*» on 21 January 1860, and a man born 20 February 1825 is thirty-four on that day, a month short of thirty-five.

events.evidence: Named in both documents as the mother — «e figlia di ARRICALE GIOVANNA, contadina». HER PARENTS ARE READ FROM THE IMAGE: FRANCESCO ARRICALE, 24, contadino, and PASQUA FALCO, 25, both of STRADA CAPODICONCA, in her own birth act — atto 114 of 1848, born 22 December 1848. Confirmed independently by the indexed marriage record of 18 Nov 1872 in the Caserta SMCV Tribunale collection (1:2:HHBF-FZWK, image 3QS7-L976-QW8C). HER MOTHER WAS A FALCO — so generation five's groom and his bride's mother shared a surname. NO KINSHIP IS CLAIMED: Arienzo holds several Pasqua Falco in these years, mothers of Maione, Majone and Loffredo children among others, and this one is not identified beyond the act. HER SIBLINGS ARE NOT FINDABLE and the index is the reason: the Caserta collection covering 1809-1866 holds 1,086 Falco records for Arienzo and effectively NO Arricale at all, so it cannot show children of this couple. Use the full-text page transcripts for Arricale, not the name index The Arricale of Arienzo are a large and steady family of VATICALI — carriers — chiefly of strada Capodiconca, and the spelling wanders between Arricale, Arrigale and Arricole in the same decade and sometimes the same hand

events.evidence:
GENERATION FIVE'S WIFE. Born at ten o'clock in her father's house, atto 114 of 1848. THE MARGIN OF HER OWN BIRTH ACT RECORDS HER MARRIAGE: «18 Novembre 1872 … Giovanna Arricale con Carmine Antonio Falco», certified at Caserta 4 June 1884 — the register confirming from itself the date found independently in the FamilySearch index

**Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — ATTO 114, IMAGE 115 RIGHT continuing on 116 LEFT.** «*è nata da **PASQUA FALCO moglie di FRANCESCO ARRICALE**, di anni **venticinque** … e da detto **FRANCESCO ARRICALE**, di anni **ventiquattro**, di professione contadino … nel giorno **ventidue** del mese di **Dicembre** … il nome di **GIOVANNA***». Declared by **ROSA MORGILLO, forty-eight, LEVATRICE** of strada San Filippo Neri — a midwife, not a parent — and witnessed by **ANTONIO SORGENTE, forty-eight**.

**AND HER OWN BIRTH ACT CARRIES HER MARRIAGE IN THE MARGIN, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD NOT TAKEN FROM IT**: «*A **18 Novembre 1872** l'Uff.le dello Stato Civ.le d'**ARIENZO** sposò **GIOVANNA ARRICOLA** con **CARMINE ANTONIO FALCO***», annotated at Caserta in 1884. **The date was already held — from the 1897 marriage dossier of her son Raffaele — and it is now held twice, from two documents that never met.** The margin spells her **ARRICOLA** where the act itself writes **ARRICALE**; the act governs.

**GIUSEPPE FALCO'S SECOND WIFE — AND SHE HAD NO ROW HERE UNTIL 22 SEPTEMBER 2026.** Her whole filiation was read from the act on 21 September and written into **his** evidence rather than given rows of her own, so **she had no person page and neither did her parents**; her name was findable on this site only because it sits inside somebody else's quotation. *Found by auditing the search index against the week's new names.*

«*e **D'ANGELA CARFORA maggiore**, di anni **cinquantanove**, nata in **Arienzo**, domiciliata **ivi strada SIGNORINDICO**, figlia del **fu ANGELO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi, e della **fu CAMILLA CRISCI**, domiciliata ivi, **VEDOVA DI GENNARO CARFORA***».

**Fifty-nine in December 1854**, so born about **1795**; **a Carfora who had married a Carfora**, widowed before she married Giuseppe Falco. **She lived on strada SIGNORINDICO** — the street of the Carfora household that work-list row 63 settled on the same day, Francesco Carfora and Pasqua Morgillo. *Whether she belongs to it is not established and is not claimed.*

**PROBABLE.** «*Antonia Carfora, **76**, contadina, **fu STEFANO CARFORA**, contadino, e **fu TERESA DI GUIDA**, moglie di **DOMENICO GIGLIO***» — act 46, read from the image in the Arienzo death register for 1828 on 8 September 2026, **eleven days before the act that names her mother's own death was found**.

**The two acts were read a year apart and neither was found by looking for the other.** This archive held the 1828 act for two weeks without a household, because a woman named only as a dead parent gives nothing to search on.

**WHY THIS IS PROBABLE AND NOT PROVEN.** The couple named is the same — *Stefano Carfora and Teresa di Guida* — and **the ages agree without being made to**: Antonia is seventy-six in September 1828, so born about **1752**; Teresa is eighty-six in March 1810, so born about **1724**, which makes her **twenty-eight** when Antonia was born. Both parents are «fu» in 1828 and Teresa was already a widow in 1810.

**What would break it:** a second Stefano Carfora married to a second Teresa di Guida. **Stefano Carfora is a recurring Arienzo name** — a *Stefano Carfora di Pietro*, born about 1796, appears as a declarant in the death registers of 1816, 1822, 1823, 1825, 1827 and 1828, and **he too had a daughter called Antonia Carfora**, who died at eight months in 1823. He is a generation younger and is not this man; but he is the reason this is not called certain. **It is the pairing of both names that carries the identification, not either name alone.**

events.evidence:
**THEIR MARRIAGE, AND BOTH SETS OF PARENTS — FOR A HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE HELD FROM ONE BIRTH ACT.** The 1827 Arienzo marriage tavola named the couple; **the act itself was then opened**, because an index is not a record. `an_ua14231`, image 17 right, foglio 195:

«*Num. d'ordine **sedici**. L'anno mille ottocento **ventisette**, il dì **diciotto** del mese di **Agosto** … avanti di Noi **Saverio Cioffi Sindaco** … del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Distretto di **Nola** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANTONIO CARFORA, maggiore**, di anni **ventuno finiti**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi **strada CAMELLARA**, figlio di **PASQUALE CARFORA DEFUNTO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **MARIA CARBO=/NA**, domiciliata ivi*».

**Twenty-one «finiti» in August 1827** — born about 1806, and the 1831 birth act makes him twenty-six, which is 1805. **His father PASQUALE CARFORA was already dead**, and the church celebration followed on **19 August 1827** at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**.

**The two witnesses are NOT kin, and this act is the proof.** «*Don **MARCANTONIO MARTINISI** e **LUIGI VERDICCHIO***» stood for this couple in August 1827 — **and the same two men stood for Francesco Carfora and Pasqua Morgillo in June 1828**, in a different Carfora household on a different street. **They are the parish's standing witnesses.** Anyone who finds them beside a third Carfora should read them as furniture.

Two Antonio Carfora in one volume.

**CHECKED AND CONFIRMED, 20 September 2026 — and the check nearly produced a false correction.** Reading the second column down as far as the usual band goes, it appeared to be nothing but the printed formula about the parish returning the *notamento*, which never names a child — and this quotation looked constructed out of the column's printed HEADING. **It is not.** Lower down the same column, past where the band stopped, the act says it in full: «*… del controscritto atto di nascita, in piè del quale ha indicato, che il **Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato a ANTONIO CARFORA** — — — nel giorno **Dieci Gennajo corrente***».

**The archive was right and the reader was wrong**, and the reason is the rule this archive already has: **a band is not a page.** The same near-miss would have retracted three true quotations in one morning.

events.evidence:
**HIS NAME IS FRANCESCO, AND THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED IT AS VALERIO.** The 1860 act writes the forename across a line break — «*figlia di **Fran-***» at the end of one line, «***cesco** Carfora*» at the start of the next — and this archive read the second half as «lerio», reasoned that no Italian forename ends in *-lerio* except one, and published **«VALERIO CARFORA»**. The reasoning was sound and the reading was wrong.

**THREE DOCUMENTS SETTLE IT, AND TWO OF THEM NEED NO HANDWRITING JUDGEMENT AT ALL.**

**One — his own consent, written out in full three weeks earlier.** Item 6 of the marriage act's document list is the bride's father's consent, and **the paper itself is in the 1860 Arienzo processetti**: «*L'anno milleottocentosessanta il giorno **primo Gennajo** in **Arienzo**. Innanzi a noi **Stefano Sargenti Sindaco** di detto comune … si è presentato **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, contadino di detto comune, il quale presta il suo pieno consenso alla sua figlia **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA** … contragga matrimonio col nominato **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO** fu **CARMINE**, e **ROSA CEGLIA**, contadino di **Forchia***». **Same town, same official, same month, the name unwrapped and unhurried.**

**Two — his daughter's birth act, which names him twice.** Arienzo, Nati 1830, act **142**: «*è comparso **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, di anni ventotto, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada **SIGNORINDICO***», and again at the foot, «*testimonj intervenuti al presente atto, e da esso **Signor FRANCESCO CARFORA** prodotti*».

**Three — his marriage, two years before that.** Arienzo, Matrimoni 1828, act **11**, 29 June 1828: **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, twenty-eight, contadino of **strada Signorindico**, son of the late Matteo Carfora and the late Grazia Zimbardo, marrying **PASQUA MORGILLO**.

**WHAT SURVIVES OF THE OLD ENTRY.** The part this archive got right is the part it argued hardest for: **the act does not mark him dead**, and **item 6 proves he consented in person**. **Francesco Carfora, contadino of strada Signorindico, was alive at Arienzo on 21 January 1860** — a man to look for, not a death to look for. Only the forename changes.

events.evidence:
**THE CARFORA HOUSE THIS ARCHIVE WAS LOOKING FOR, AND IT IS NOT ON STRADA CAMELLARA.** Row 63 was raised because the archive did not know there were Carfora at Arienzo at all; it then found three *contadino* households in the 1831 births, two of them on the Falco's own street, and assumed the answer was among them. **It was not.** This house is on **strada SIGNORINDICO**.

**Arienzo, Matrimoni 1828, act 11, 29 June 1828**, foglio 214: «*avanti di Noi **Saverio Cioffi Sindaco** … del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Distretto di **Nola** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, maggiore, di anni **ventotto**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi **strada SIGNORINDICO**, figlio di **MATTEO CARFORA DEFUNTO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, vedovo di **MARTA CRISCI**, e di **GRAZIA ZIMBARDO DEFUNTA**, domiciliata ivi*». The church celebration followed on **30 June 1828** at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**.

**«VEDOVO DI MARTA CRISCI» IS LEFT AS IT READS.** The clause sits between Matteo Carfora and Grazia Zimbardo, and the printed form gives it to neither cleanly: it may make **Francesco** a widower remarrying at twenty-eight, or **Matteo** a man twice married. **This archive holds a MARTA GRIFO, thirty, wife of a Francesco Carfora, dead at Arienzo on 6 May 1827** — act 33 of the 1827 death register, already read here, with **Giovanni Carfora, forty-five, contadino of strada Signorindio** and **Stefano Carfora** as declarants. **Grifo is not Crisci and the two are not merged**, but a Francesco Carfora of that street widowed in May 1827 and remarrying in June 1828 is the shape the act describes, and it is recorded here for whoever reads act 33 at magnification next.

**He was still alive on 1 January 1860**, when he gave his consent in person at the Casa Comunale of Arienzo for his daughter's marriage.

---

**THE FIRST WIFE, READ FROM HER OWN ACT — 22 September 2026.** The clause «*vedovo di **MARTA CRISCI***» sat here as a puzzle, with a note that this archive held a **MARTA GRIFO** dead at thirty on 6 May 1827 as the wife of *a* Francesco Carfora, and that whoever read act 33 next should magnify it. **It has been read.**

**Arienzo, Morti 1827, act 33, 6 May 1827** — «*sono comparsi **GIOVANNI CARFORA**, di anni **quarantacinque**, di professione contadino … domiciliato **ivi strada SIGNORINDICO**, **VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA**, e **STEFANO CARFORA di PIETRO**, di anni **ventuno**, contadino … ivi **strada Signorindico** … è morta nella sua propria casa **MARTA ⟨———⟩, di anni TRENTA, MOGLIE DI FRANCESCO CARFORA**, nata in **Arienzo**, di professione contadina, domiciliata ivi, **figlia di ALESSANDRO CAS——— DEFUNTO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, **e di CARMINA PORRINO**, domiciliata ivi*».

**WHAT IS SECURE.** She is **MARTA**, **thirty**, **wife of FRANCESCO CARFORA**, dead **6 May 1827** — thirteen months before he married Pasqua Morgillo — and **both declarants are Carfora of strada SIGNORINDICO**, the street this household lives on, one of them «*vicino della defunta*». **Her parents are ALESSANDRO CAS——— and CARMINA PORRINO.**

**WHAT IS NOT.** **Her own surname will not resolve and neither will her father's.** Hers is a tall looped initial over a double-f or long-s cluster — this archive has published it as **GRIFO** — and his is four or five letters beginning **CAS**, which a note of 13 September read as **CASALE**. *Neither is CRISCI.*

**SO THE 1828 ACT'S «MARTA CRISCI» IS NOT HER SURNAME.** Either the clerk of June 1828 wrote the wrong name for a woman thirteen months dead, or Francesco Carfora buried two wives called Marta in thirteen months. **The street, the trade, the husband's name and the date all say one woman**; only the surname says two, and it is the one word on the page that cannot be read. **Left as it reads, in both acts.**

**BORN 30 DECEMBER 1830 AT ARIENZO, AND READ FROM THE REGISTER ITSELF.** The 1860 dossier carries her birth extract as document 5; **the original act was then opened, because a certified copy is not the register.** Arienzo, Nati 1830, act **142**, images 145 right and 146 left:

«*L'anno mille ottocento **trenta**, il dì **trenta** del mese di **Dicembre**, ad ore **sedici**, avanti di noi **Maria Romano Sindaco** ed Uffiziale dello Stato Civile del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Distretto di **Nola** … è comparso **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, di anni **ventotto**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada SIGNORINDICO**, quale ci ha presentato una **femina** … che la stessa è nata da **PASQUA MORGILLO sua moglie legittima**, di anni **ventisei**, liata collo stesso … **nel giorno trenta del mese di Dicembre, anno corrente, alle ore SETTE, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione** … ha in oltre dichiarato di dare alla nominata il nome di **MARIANTONIA***».

Witnesses **GENNARO MORGILLO**, thirty-three, contadino of **strada Cappellotto della Porta di Sopra** — her mother's surname — and **CRESCENZO CRISCI**, thirty-five, contadino of **strada Crisci**, «*da esso Signor **FRANCESCO CARFORA** prodotti*». **The age in the marriage act fits to the week.** She is «*di anni ventinove*» on 21 January 1860, and a woman born 30 December 1830 had turned twenty-nine three weeks before.

**THIS IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THIS ARCHIVE'S MATTEO CARFORA, AND THE STREET IS WHAT SAYS SO.**

«*L'anno **milleottocentoquindici**, il giorno **ventitré** del mese di **Marzo** … è comparso **MATTEO CARFORA** d'anni **TRENTANOVE**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in detto Comune, strada **SIGNORINDICO**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato ad ore **tre** è nato nella sua propria casa, da lui dichiarante, e da **LUCIA LAUDATO** sua moglie legitima di anni **VENTI**, un **maschio** … **A cui se li è dato il nome di ANGELO.***»

**Strada Signorindico is the street of Francesco Carfora**, whose 1828 marriage act makes him «*figlio di **MATTEO CARFORA DEFUNTO** … e di **GRAZIA ZIMBARDO DEFUNTA***» and twenty-eight, so born about **1800**. **Thirty-nine in 1815 puts this man's birth about 1776** — twenty-four when that son was born.

**SO HE HAD AT LEAST TWO WIVES AND POSSIBLY THREE**, and this archive cannot yet say which:

- **GRAZIA ZIMBARDO** — mother of Francesco about 1800, dead before 1828;
- **ANGELA ZIMBARDO** — his wife when she died on **19 February 1813**, the day after their son Domenico;
- **LUCIA LAUDATO** — twenty years old and his wife by 1814, bearing **Angelo** in March 1815.

**Angela and Grazia may be one woman under two forenames**, in which case Francesco Carfora lost his mother at about thirteen and his father remarried within two years. **Or they are sisters, married in turn.** *The 1828 word was re-read at full resolution and says GRAZIA, so this is a disagreement between documents.*

**THE HOUSEHOLDS ARE STILL NOT MERGED.** What has changed is that keeping them apart is now the cautious reading rather than the obvious one.

**A CARFORA HOUSEHOLD ON STRADA CAMELLARA — THE FALCO STREET — IN 1809.**

**TWO REGISTERS TWO YEARS APART NAME THIS COUPLE AND THEY WERE FOUND SEPARATELY.** This act gives him a wife, **Maria Carbone**. events.evidence:
«*e di **Donna FAUSTINA CIMMINO Defunta**, domiciliata ivi*» — read from the image at full resolution on 20 September 2026, the capital **F** with its crossbar and the «au» that follows it.

**THE DISCREPANCY THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED DOES NOT EXIST.** This page said: «*THE ONE DISCREPANCY, AND IT IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. The 1840 act names the mother SERAFINA Cimmino; the 1842 act names her FAUSTINA Cimmino… Either a clerk misread a forename, or Stefano Scarpati married twice.*» **Both acts say FAUSTINA.** There was no second wife to wonder about and no clerk to blame: **the misreading was this archive's**, and a woman called Donna Serafina Cimmino, who never existed, had a name on this site.

**What it costs and what it buys.** It removes an invented person and an invented problem, and it **strengthens the join**: the archpriest of Arienzo and the sorora of the Conservatorio di San Filippo are now named in two acts two years apart with **the same father, the same rank, the same trade and the same mother**. Still an inference — two death acts are not a birth record — but no longer one with an objection standing against it.

**THE SURNAME IS PLAIN HERE, AND IT CONFIRMS THE 1825 CORRECTION FROM A THIRD ACT**: *C-i-o-ff-i*, with the **i between the C and the o** that a *Cossi* does not have. The 1833 act of this same household is written in a worse hand where the two cannot be separated; this one can.

**SHE IS THE SECOND ANTONIA.** The first died on **20 June 1823**. This household also buried a **Mariantonia on 23 October 1828** and another **Mariantonia on 3 December 1832** — and **that last one may be this child**, sixteen months old. *It is not claimed*: the 1832 death act has not been re-read, and a household that reuses a dead child's name three times is exactly the one where a join like that must be proved rather than assumed.

Witnessed by **SALVATORE DIGLIO**, thirty-six, and **DOMENICO SAVONE**, twenty-seven, both *contadini* of **strada Terra Murata**. Baptised at Sant'Andrea the same day.

**This archive holds an ANTONIA CIOFFI dead on 20 June 1823.** Born 30 September 1822 she would be **not quite nine months old**, which fits — and it makes sense of the **second Antonia**, born to the same parents on **8 August 1831**. *Likely, and not claimed*: the 1823 death act has not been re-read.

**AN EIGHTH CHILD FOR A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE CHILDREN KEPT DYING, AND THE FIRST RECORD IT HAS FOR 1833.** Act 85: «*L'anno mille ottocento **trentatre**, il dì **ventitre** del mese di **AGOSTO**, ad ore dodici, avanti di noi **FRANCESCO D'AMBROSIO Sindaco** … è comparso **FRANCESCO C[OSSI/CIOFFI], di anni QUARANTA, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTADUE** … nel giorno **VENTITRE** del mese di Agosto, anno corrente, **alle ore DIECI**, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione … il nome di **CLEMENTE***». Witnessed by **AGOSTINO ARRIGALE**, fifty, *vaticale* of strada Capodiconca, and **PELLEGRINO VIGLIOTTA**, thirty. The INDICAZIONE records the **Parroco di SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO** returning the notice on the **twenty-seventh of August**, so he was baptised four days after his birth.

**THE FATHER'S SURNAME IS NOT LEGIBLE ENOUGH IN THIS HAND TO TOUCH THE STANDING CORRECTION, AND IT IS NOT TOUCHED.** This archive corrected this household from *Cossi* to **CIOFFI** from the 1825 register at full resolution, and that correction stands. Read here at 3,200 pixels the surname shows a large flourished **C**, a round **o**, a doubled letter with long descenders and a final **i** — which by the letter-count test would be *Cossi*, **except that the C's own flourish could conceal the i that makes it Cioffi**. *At this resolution, in this hand, the two cannot be separated* — which is what this archive said when it first met the problem: «at plate resolution the two surnames are not distinguishable; go to the image». **Here even the image is marginal.** The household keeps the name the 1825 act gave it.

**Maria Falco is thirty-two**, which puts her birth about 1801.

**THE CITATION IS WITHDRAWN AS IMPOSSIBLE, 20 September 2026.** It read «`an_ua14329` **img47L atto84**» — Arienzo Morti 1827. **That volume has FORTY-TWO images and SIXTY-EIGHT acts.** Image 47 does not exist. Act 84 does not exist.

**And he is not in the leaves that were swept.** Images 20 to 41 were read across three contact sheets — the act numbers on every leaf, and the name line on every act from May to the end of December. events.evidence:
**THIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOW CLOSED AT BOTH ENDS, AND THE ACT WAS FOUND BY PAYING A DEBT.** On 21 September a sweep strip showed a pair of declarants read as **RAFFAELE FALCO** and **MATTEO FALCO**, coloni of contrada Camellara; the leaf was hunted twice and missed, and this archive published the reading as **owed** rather than as a record. *The margin number in this volume runs two behind the image number.* **It is image 28.**

**Arienzo, Morti 1864, act 49, 12 August 1864**: «*sono comparsi **RAFFAELE FALCO**, di anni **quarantacinque**, di professione **COLONO**, regnicolo, domiciliato in **Arienzo, Contrada CAMELLARA**, e **MATTEO FALCO**, di anni **cinquantadue**, di professione **simile**, domiciliato **ivi**, i quali han dichiarato, che nel giorno **undici** del mese di **Agosto** anno suddetto alle ore **sedici**, è morto nella sua casa **FRANCESCO CIOFFI — VEDOVO DI MARIA FALCO**, nato in **Arienzo**, di anni **SETTANTA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **Contrada CAMELLARA**, **figlio del fu GIUSEPPE**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, **e della fu MARIA PORRINO**, domiciliata ivi*».

**Seventy in August 1864**, so born about **1794**; his wife **MARIA FALCO died 1 May 1862** at sixty-seven. **He outlived her by twenty-seven months and the act calls him her widower.** This archive followed this couple through eight children's acts from 1818 to 1831 and had a date for neither of them until this week.

**AND TWO FALCO CAME TO DECLARE IT.** The act does not say they are kin — *it says «*sono comparsi*» and nothing more* — but they are the two Falco of that street, and the dead man was married to a Falco. **RAFFAELE FALCO, forty-five** (born about 1819) and **MATTEO FALCO, fifty-two** (born about 1812), **both coloni of contrada Camellara, both alive on 12 August 1864.** *No household here is claimed for either of them on this act alone.*

events.evidence:
A contadino of **STRADA CAMELLARA** — the street of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti. He is one of the two men who report **CHIARA RIVETTI'S DEATH** on 13 September 1843. **HE IS A NEIGHBOUR.** No act calls him kin to the Falco, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.

**THIS PAGE CARRIED AN AGE SERIES THAT WAS WRONG AT BOTH ENDS, AND A CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT.** It read: «*his stated age is, after the first entry, the steadiest series in these registers: FORTY in 1840, FORTY-SEVEN in August 1842, FORTY-EIGHT in September 1843. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco eleven different ages, this clerk got one right.*»

**The 1840 act gives him no age at all** — he is named in it as the dead child's father, and fathers are not aged in these acts. **The 1843 act says forty-three, not forty-eight**; this archive read that from the image on 15 September 2026 and corrected it in one file only. **So the series is forty-seven in August 1842 and forty-three in September 1843. He got younger.** The one man the archive held up as proof that a clerk could keep an age straight is another proof that they could not.

events.evidence:
**Forty-seven**, a contadino of strada Camellara — verified from the image, «*di anni quarantasette*». He is a neighbour; the act does not call him kin, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.

**THE CLAIM THAT USED TO STAND HERE WAS THE OPPOSITE OF THE TRUTH.** This page said: «*Thirteen months later, at forty-eight, the same man reports the death of CHIARA RIVETTI on the same street. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco four different ages, this one holds.*» **He is not forty-eight in that act. He is forty-three.** The archive read «quarantatre» from the image on 15 September 2026 and corrected Chiara Rivetti's act — and left the boast standing in two other files. **Forty-seven in August 1842, forty-three in September 1843: he lost four years in thirteen months, and this is one more demonstration that the ages in these registers are guessed.**

events.evidence:
**HIS BIRTH ACT — AND HE IS THE CHILD WHOSE AGE THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN DATING THIS MARRIAGE BY.** Act **68**: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **DICIANNOVE**, a' dì **SETTE** del mese di **GIUGNO**, ad ore **DIECI**, avanti di noi **ANDREA SORICE Sindaco** … è comparso **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, di anni VENTIQUATTRO**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in detto comune **strada CAMELLARA**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato **ad ore SEI** è nato nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante, **e da MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, d'anni VENTITRÉ**, un **MASCHIO** che ci ha presentato … a cui si è dato il nome di **GIUSEPPE***». Witness **ANDREA COSSI, thirty-seven, contadino, of strada COSSI**.

**THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES.** This archive held him only as a death: **25 March 1824, aged five**. **Born 7 June 1819 he was five years and nine months.** The two acts agree.

**AND IT TIGHTENS AN ARGUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS LEANED ON.** The published reasoning ran «*their son died in March 1824 aged five, so [the marriage] is no later than about 1819*». **The son's birth is now dated to the day, so the marriage is no later than 1818** — and the conclusion that it predates the Arienzo civil registers, which begin in 1809, is untouched.

**It is also the earliest sighting of this household by three years**, and it puts them on **strada CAMELLARA** in June 1819 — the street they are on in 1822, 1824, 1828, 1831 and 1833, and **not** the strada Sant'Andrea of March 1826. *Found by reading the 1819 birth register for work-list row 86 — a volume that had never been read.*

events.evidence:
**AND THIS ONE PROBABLY DATES A DEATH THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD.** Act 74: «*L'anno mille ottocento **ventinove**, il dì **CINQUE** del mese di **OTTOBRE**, ad ore ventitré … è comparso **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, di anni TRENTASEI, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legitima, di anni TRENTAQUATTRO** … nel giorno **CINQUE** del mese di Ottobre, anno corrente, **alle ore QUINDICI**, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione … il nome di **GIUSEPPE***». Witnessed by **VINCENZO DIGLIO**, thirty-five, of strada Sant'Andrea, and **LORENZO LIPARULO**, forty-five. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo the following day**.

**This archive holds a GIUSEPPE CIOFFI «the second» who died on 5 December 1830.** Born 5 October 1829 he would be **fourteen months old** at that death, which fits, and the household's first Giuseppe died on 25 March 1824. **The join is likely and is not claimed**: the 1830 death act has not been re-read.

**Maria Falco is thirty-four here, thirty-five two years later in 1831, and thirty-two four years later in 1833.** Her husband is thirty-six in 1829 and thirty-six again in 1831. The register is guessing both of them.

events.evidence:
**THE BIRTH OF A CHILD THIS ARCHIVE ONLY HAD A DEATH FOR.** Act **19**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **VENTISEI**, il dì **NOVE** del mese di **MARZO**, ad ore **VENTI** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA FALCO, di anni TRENTA**, domiciliata ivi **strada SANT'ANDREA**, e da **FRANCESCO CIOFFI marito della stessa, di anni TRENTACINQUE**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato con detta sua moglie, nel giorno **NOVE** del mese di **MARZO** … **alle ore OTTO, nella casa d'abitazione di detti conjugi** … il nome di **GIUSEPPE***». Presented by the midwife, so both parents are named; witnesses **VINCENZO OROLOGIO, twenty-eight, *pettinatore*** and **GIUSEPPE CIMMINO, thirty-five, *viaticale***, both of strada Sant'Andrea.

**IT DATES AN ACT THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD.** On **1 May 1827** **GIUSEPPE FALCO** declared, as «*vicino del defunto*», the death of a **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI, aged one, son of FRANCESCO CIOFFI**. **Born 9 March 1826, he was one year and seven weeks old.** The join is exact and the child now has both ends of his life.

**AND THE STREET IS NEW.** This household is on **strada CAMELLARA** in 1822, 1831 and 1833. **In March 1826 it is on strada SANT'ANDREA** — so either they moved twice, or the clerks recorded the quarter rather than the lane. **It is recorded, not explained.**

**HE IS THE SECOND OF THREE GIUSEPPE, AND FINDING HIM RENUMBERED THE OTHER TWO.** The first died **25 March 1824 aged five**, so he was born about 1819. **This one was born 9 March 1826 and died 1 May 1827 at one year old** — his death act names **MARIA FALCO** and is now held under this household. A **third** was born **5 October 1829** (act 74) and is probably the Giuseppe Cioffi dead **5 December 1830** at fourteen months; **this archive had been calling him «the second» and he is the third.** On /corrections.

**This household buried at least six children that this archive knows of**, and named the next one after each: three Giuseppe, two Antonia, two Mariantonia.

events.evidence:
**DEAD AT ONE YEAR OLD, AND THE ACT NAMES BOTH HIS PARENTS.** Act **30** of 1827: «*L'anno mille ottocento **VENTISETTE**, il dì **DUE** del mese di **MAGGIO**, alle ore **UNDICI**, avanti di noi **SAVERIO CIOFFI Sindaco** … sono comparsi **GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione COLONO**, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi **strada CAMELLARA**, **VICINO DEL DEFUNTO**, e **CESARE CIOFFI, di anni TRENTA**, di professione contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, **PARENTE DEL DEFUNTO**, i quali han dichiarato, che nel giorno **PRIMO** del mese di **MAGGIO** … alle ore **VENTIQUATTRO** è morto nella sua propria casa **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI DI UN ANNO**, nato in **ARIENZO** … figlio di **FRANCESCO CIOFFI**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, **e di MARIA FALCO**, domiciliata ivi*».

**THE MOTHER'S NAME IS WHAT MAKES THE JOIN.** This archive held the act only under **Giuseppe Falco**, who declared it as a neighbour; **the household of the dead child never carried it.** Read from the image on 21 September 2026, it gives **MARIA FALCO** outright, and the child is the one born **9 March 1826**, act 19 — **one year and seven weeks old**, exactly as the act says.

**And the clerk draws the distinction himself, in one sentence**: Giuseppe Falco is «*vicino del defunto*» and **CESARE CIOFFI is «*parente del defunto*»** — kin to this household, as he is again in 1828 for another of its children. *The act is dated **2 May**; this archive had been citing it as 1 May, which is the day of the death, not of the act.*

events.evidence:
**HER BIRTH, AND IT CLOSES HER LIFE FROM BOTH ENDS TO THE FORTNIGHT.** Act **28**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **VENTOTTO**, il dì **OTTO** del mese di **MARZO**, ad ore **DICIASSETTE**, avanti di noi **SAVERIO CIOFFI Sindaco** … è comparso **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, di anni TRENTA**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in questo Comune **strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTA**, domiciliata collo stesso, **e da lui dichiarante** … nel giorno **OTTO** del mese di **MARZO** … **alle ore QUINDICI, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione** … di dare alla neonata il nome di **MARIANTONIA***». Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo** the same day.

**Her death act, already held, says «*di mesi SETTE*» on 23 October 1828.** Born 8 March, she was **seven months and fifteen days**. **The arithmetic is exact**, and this household's children are now the best-documented thing about it: it buried six that this archive knows of.

Witnesses **NICOLA CIOFFI, twenty-six, *sartore*, of strada CAMELLARA**, and **ANDREA DIGLIO, twenty-one, contadino, of strada SAPONARI**. **A CIOFFI SIGNS AS SINDACO AND A CIOFFI WITNESSES** — Saverio Cioffi holds the office, Agostino Cioffi is *secondo eletto* at her death seven months later, and Cesare Cioffi is called «*parente*» at two other burials in this family. **The name runs from the town hall to the labourers' street.**

*Found by the parents-band sweep of 1828, work-list row 86 — a volume that had never been read.*

events.evidence:
**THE ACT IS 3 SEPTEMBER, NOT 3 DECEMBER, AND THE CHILD IS ONE YEAR OLD — WHICH CLOSES THE JOIN.** «*Num. d'ordine **SESSANTAQUATTRO**. L'Anno milleottocento **trentadue**, il dì **TRE** del mese di **SETTEMBRE**, alle ore undici … sono comparsi **PELLEGRINO CIOFFI**, di anni trentasei, contadino, **in strada CAMELLARA, VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA**, e **FRANCESCO LETTIERI**, di anni quaranta, contadino, **in strada CAMELLARA, VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA** … che nel giorno **TRE** del mese di **SETTEMBRE**, anno corrente, alle ore **NOVE**, è morta nella sua propria casa **MARIANTONIA CIOFFI, DI UN ANNO** … figlia di **FRANCESCO CIOFFI** … **e di MARIA FALCO***».

**This archive held her as dying 3 DECEMBER 1832, from the INDEX** (`an_ua14294`, atto 64). **The register act of that number is 3 SEPTEMBER.** **And «di un anno» settles what the index could not**: she is the **ANTONIA born 8 August 1831** to the same parents — dead at **one year and twenty-six days**. Both declarants are neighbours, not kin.

events.evidence:
«*è morta nella sua propria casa **MARTA CIOFFI d'anni SETTE***» — **seven years old**, so born about 1833. Died at eight in the morning on **6 November 1840**, in the act drawn the same day.

**THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED HER AS «D'UN MESE» — one month old — IN QUOTATION MARKS, AND THE ACT DOES NOT SAY IT.** The words «d'anni sette» are written plainly and were magnified before this was changed. **A quotation the document does not contain is the worst thing on this page**, worse than a wrong number, because a reader cannot tell it from a reading.

**The two men who declared her death were also mis-aged**: **CLEMENTE CIOFFI is thirty-six**, not thirty-four, and **VIRGILIO CIOFFI is twenty-three**, not twenty-eight. Both of strada Camellara — a fourth and fifth Cioffi on the Falco street.

events.evidence:
**THE FIRST CHILD, THE FIRST ADDRESS AND THE FIRST AGE THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS EVER HAD.** Act 77: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **ventuno**, il dì **SEDICI** del mese di **AGOSTO**, ad ore tredici, avanti di Noi **VINCENZO MORGILLO Sindaco** … è comparso **DOMENICO COSPI, di anni CINQUANTASETTE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada COSPI**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **MARGARITA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni QUARANTUNO** … nel giorno **SEDICI** del mese di Agosto, anno corrente, **alle ore NOVE**, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione … il nome di **ANNA MARIA TERESA***». Witnessed by **FABRIZIO COSPI**, twenty-seven, ***FERRARO***, and **GASPARO DIGLIO**, forty, ***CALZOLAJO***, both of strada Porta di Sopra. The INDICAZIONE has the **Parroco di Sant'Andrea Apostolo** returning the notice **the same day**, naming the child «**ANNA MARIA TERESA COSPI**».

**Before this the couple existed only in her death act of 1836 and in one line of an 1819 marriage index.** They now have a daughter, a street of their own name, and both their ages: he **fifty-seven**, born about 1764; she **forty-one**, born about 1780 — against the **sixty** her 1836 death act gives her, which implies 1776. **Four years apart, and neither is adopted.**

events.evidence:
«*è comparso **DOMENICO COSSI, di anni QUARANTACINQUE**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in detto comune, **strada COSSI***» — **b. c.1773.** **The surname and the street both read COSSI here and both were magnified.** In 1821 the same man — same wife, same age series — is **Domenico COSPI of strada COSPI**, and an 1819 marriage index makes his son a **CRISCI**. **Three spellings, three documents, one household**; this archive records the variance and does not resolve it.

**A CAUTION ON THAT READING, AND IT IS THE SAME CLERK.** Four leaves later, in **act 47 of this volume**, the same hand writes generation three's wife — **ANDREANA CRISCI**, verified word for word from the image on 20 September 2026 and given as CRISCI in eight other acts. **At 3,000 pixels that word is a flourished C, a narrow letter that will not resolve, a doubled long ſſ and a final i** — indistinguishable, at this resolution, from the *Coſſi* read here. **So this clerk's C-word is not a safe discriminator**, and the reading above is recorded as a reading, not as a correction. *The archive's own name for this household is unchanged.*

events.evidence: «*assistita da **BRIGIDA COSSI** sua madre di anni **CINQUANTASEI**, di professione **contadina**, domiciliata colla figlia*» — born about 1759, a widow giving consent for a daughter who was still a minor. **The surname is COSSI and this one is worth the space.** This archive has spent months correcting *Cossi* to *Cioffi* on strada Camellara, on a test about the descender of the doubled letter. **That test does not work in this hand**: read at twelve times, the doubled letters here descend exactly as a double f would, and so do the ones in «MASSONE» and «SANSONE», which are certainly long ſ. **What separates the two names is the letter count**: *Cioffi* carries an **i between the C and the o** and *Cossi* does not. There is no such i here, in this act or in act 21 of the same volume, where **ELISABETTA COSSI** and her father **MARINO COSSI** are written the same way. **Cossi is a real Arienzo surname**, and the Camellara correction was about one household, not about the name.

events.evidence:
**THE EARLIEST ACT THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS, AND IT SPELLS THE FATHER A THIRD WAY.** Act **9**, foglio 5: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **DICIOTTO** a' dì **DICIOTTO** del mese di **GENNARO**, ad ore **DICIANNOVE**, avanti di noi **ANDREA SORICE Sindaco** … è comparso **DOMENICO COSSI, di anni QUARANTACINQUE**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in detto comune, **strada COSSI**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato ad ore **DICIASSETTE** è nata nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante, **e da MARGARITA FALCO sua moglie legittima, d'anni QUARANTA**, una **FEMINA** … a cui si è dato il nome di **MARIA CARMELA***». Witnesses **CESARE DIGLIO, contadino of strada CAMELLARA**, and **FRANCESCO COSSI, fifty-two, *calzolajo***.

**SHE IS NEW, AND SHE IS THIS HOUSEHOLD'S THIRD DOCUMENT.** It had two: a son **ANGELO CRISCI** marrying in 1819, and a daughter **ANNA MARIA TERESA COSPI** born in 1821.

**AND THAT IS THREE SURNAMES FOR ONE HOUSEHOLD IN THREE ACTS — CRISCI, COSPI, COSSI.** This archive renamed the household from **Domenico Crisci** to **Domenico Cospi** on the strength of the 1821 act, where the declarant is «Domenico Cospi» of «strada Cospi», the leaf's margin is annotated «Cospi» and the parish notice names the child «Anna Maria Teresa **Cospi**». **This act, three years earlier, says COSSI and strada COSSI**, and the word was magnified: **a capital C running straight to an o, a doubled long ſſ, a final i — five letters, no p, and no i between the C and the o.**

**NOTHING IS RENAMED ON THIS ACCOUNT.** The household keeps the name the 1821 act gave it, and the question is published rather than answered. *What is not in doubt is the mother: **MARGARITA FALCO**, forty in January 1818 and forty-one in August 1821 — three and a half years apart and one year older, which for this office is the same woman.*

**The volume holds the year twice** — a printed slip at image 17 declares the 1817 register stock «*vale pel corrente Esercizio 1818*» — so this act appears at **image 5 right and again at image 23 right**, in two hands. **Both were read and both say COSSI.**

**A CAUTION ON THAT READING, AND IT IS THE SAME CLERK.** Four leaves later, in **act 47 of this volume**, the same hand writes generation three's wife — **ANDREANA CRISCI**, verified word for word from the image on 20 September 2026 and given as CRISCI in eight other acts. **At 3,000 pixels that word is a flourished C, a narrow letter that will not resolve, a doubled long ſſ and a final i** — indistinguishable, at this resolution, from the *Coſſi* read here. **So this clerk's C-word is not a safe discriminator**, and the reading above is recorded as a reading, not as a correction. *The archive's own name for this household is unchanged.*

events.evidence:
«*che la stessa è nata da **ALESSANDRA [surname]** sua moglie legittima, di anni **trentasei**, domiciliata collo stesso*» — born about 1810, twelve years married. **HER SURNAME IS NOT LEGIBLE ON THIS FILMING and is deliberately left unread.** The word is a single flourished capital and a tail that runs into «sua», and this is the exact trio — **Crisci, Cossi, Cioffi** — that has caught this archive three times in one week. **The identification does not need it**: a Matteo Falco of strada Camellara whose wife is called **Alessandra**, in a town where this archive holds one Matteo Falco married to an Alessandra, and whose daughter marries a **GUIDA** exactly as the family tree says. **Two hooks, neither of them the surname.**

**THE REFUSAL STANDS, AND IT IS NARROWED, 20 September 2026.** Re-read at the leaf's full resolution, the word has **a narrow shoulder where an r belongs, no round o, and no tall double ascender**. **By this archive's own three-way test — Cioffi's double-f with its long descender, Cossi's short double-s with no ascender, Crisci's narrow r and no round o — CIOFFI IS EXCLUDED and COSSI is unlikely.** What is left is **CRISCI**, which is what the household is called on other evidence. **It is not declared settled**: the archive refused this word deliberately and a marginal reading is not grounds to overrule a considered refusal. **The refusal is narrowed, not withdrawn.**

---

**HER SURNAME IS NO LONGER UNREAD — 21 September 2026.** It was left unread here **on purpose**, and that was right: at this filming the word is a single blur. **A different register, in a different hand, nineteen years later, writes it out.** Her daughter Angela's marriage act of **23 January 1865** — Arienzo, act 3 — reads «*figlia di **MATTEO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ALESSANDRA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***», and at thirteen times magnification the word is **C-r-i-ſ-c-i**: six letters, a dot over the third and the sixth, and the only descender on the long **ſ**. **Not Crispi** — a *p* would carry the descender and the fifth letter has none.

**And the 1834 marriage index said so all along**, «*CRISCI ALESSANDRA*», from a leaf whose father's forename was lost to the page-fold. **Two documents, nineteen years apart, in two hands.**

events.evidence:
**A SECOND ANDREANA CRISCI, IN THE SAME REGISTER AS THE FIRST, EIGHT LEAVES AWAY.** Act **77** of 1826: «*è nato da **ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTUNO**, domiciliata collo stesso, e da lui dichiarante*» — the declarant being **GENNARO ESPOSITELLI, thirty-four, contadino, of strada CAPODICONCA**. The child is **RAFFAELE**, born **16 October 1826 at eighteen hours** in his father's own house.

**Act 69 of the same volume names ANDREANA CRISCI, twenty-eight, of strada CAMELLARA, wife of VINCENZO FALCO** — generation three's wife, whose baptism is 30 November 1796. **The two are three years apart in stated age, on two different streets, in one register, in one clerk's hand.** Both readings were magnified and neither is in doubt.

**THIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOT CLAIMED AS KIN AND NOTHING JOINS IT TO THIS LINE.** It is published because generation three's wife is identified in this archive by her husband and her street, and **it is now documented that her name alone identifies nobody** — as this town has already proved for Giuseppe Falco, Carlantonio Morgillo, Arcangelo Crisci, Angelo Morgillo and Gennaro Morgillo.

**A CAUTION FOUND TWO DAYS' READING LATER, AND LEFT VISIBLE.** The 1828 register, act at image 113, gives a **GENNARO ESPOSITELLA of strada CIOFFI** whose wife is «*ANDREANA **VERTEGGIO**, di anni TRENTADUE*» — magnified, the word is V-e-r-t-e-gg-i-o and is not Crisci. **So within two years the name Gennaro Espositella carries a different wife on a different street.** Either there are two men of the name — which this town produces constantly — or he was widowed and remarried between October 1826 and 1828. **Nothing here decides it, and nothing needs to**: the 1826 act's own words are what this row records, and **ANDREANA CRISCI** is magnified and certain in them.

She has a son. AND SHE IS THE EARLIEST FALCO-CRISCI MARRIAGE FOUND: born about 1776, she married a Crisci a generation before Anna, Giovanna, Matteo and Francesca did **[HOUSEHOLD RENAMED 21 September 2026: the father is DOMENICO COSPI, not Domenico Crisci.** This archive published that correction from the 1836 death act of Margarita Falco, and **the household name never followed it**. events.evidence:
**THE THIRD CHILD OF THIS COUPLE, AND THE ACT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE HOUSEHOLD WAS PUBLISHED WITH.**

«*…domiciliato in questa Comune, **strada CRISCI**, e **DOMENICO CRISCI fu ALESSANDRO**, di anni **trentasette**, di professione **contadino** … vicini della defonta, quali hanno dichiarato che a detto dì **venti — 20** del mese corrente di **Settembre**, ad ore **due** della notte, **ANNA CRISCI**, **figlia di DOMENICO CRISCI fu VINCENZO, e di MARGARITA FALCO***».

**THE REGISTER NAMES TWO DOMENICO CRISCI IN ONE SENTENCE AND TELLS THEM APART BY THEIR FATHERS.** This household was published with the plain admission that the 1809 and 1810 registers held a Domenico Crisci with children by *Maddalena Albarelli* and another by *Egidia Perrotta*, and that **which of them married Margarita Falco was not established**. It is established now: **DOMENICO CRISCI, son of the late VINCENZO**. The other — *Domenico Crisci fu Alessandro*, thirty-seven — stands in the same act as a neighbour.

**Margarita Falco buried three children in five years**: Vincenzo in 1810, a second Vincenzo in January 1812, and Anna in September 1814.

events.evidence:
**A CRISCI WOMAN LIVING ON STRADA CAMELLARA, BORN ABOUT 1736 — AND HER DAUGHTER MARRIED A CARFORA.**

«*del mese di **Ottobre** dell'anno **Mille ottocento ed undeci** in persona della Signora **ANTONIA CRISCI**, di anni **SETTANTACINQUE**, di professione **FILATRICE**, domiciliata nella anzidetta Comune, e strada **CAMMELLARA**, **VEDOVA DI PRISCO CARBONE**, la quale ha lasciato **due figli**, uno per nome **FRANCESCO**, di professione **salsolajo**, di anni **quarantacinque**, e l'altra chiamata **MARIA**, di anni **quarantadue**, **maritata col detto PASQUALE CARFORA***».

**WHY A CRISCI ON THAT STREET MATTERS.** Two of the three women who married into this archive's first Falco generations were Crisci — **Francesca Crisci**, wife of Matteo Falco, and **Andreana Crisci**, wife of Vincenzo Falco — and the Falco lived on **strada Camellara**. **This archive has never been able to say where its Crisci came from.** Here is a Crisci household on that street in 1811.

**IT IS NOT CLAIMED AS THEIRS.** The 1810 register shows a whole Crisci clan on a street that carries their own name — *Domenico, Luca, Felice, Francesco, Nicola* — and **the name is the commonest in these registers after Laudato**. [[surname-ligature-test]]

events.evidence:
**AND HIS AGE HERE BEARS ON A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS KEPT OPEN FOR MONTHS.** «*ARCANGELO CRISCI, di anni **CINQUANTA**, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada CAMELLARA***» — fifty in January 1820, so **born about 1770**.

**That is the same year the 1814 marriage act gives for Andreana Crisci's father**, read from the image on 20 September 2026: «*ARCANGELO CRISCI suo padre di anni **QUARANTAQUATTRO***», which is also **born about 1770**. **Two acts, six years apart, agreeing to the year.**

**This archive keeps TWO Arcangelo Crisci apart** — one born about 1770, one about 1795 — and has said that the elder could only ALSO be Anna Falco's husband if **Sara Ruggiero had died between September 1814**, when she consented before a notary to her daughter's marriage, **and about 1818**. **The age agreement is now the strongest evidence that they are one man**, and it makes that death the thing to look for. **It is not claimed.** An age is an age, these registers guess them, and a coincidence of two guesses is not an identification. What has changed is that the two figures no longer disagree.

**He was about twenty-eight** (fifty-two in 1817) and **she about twenty-one** (forty-five in 1817); their daughter **ANDREANA CRISCI**, who married Vincenzo Falco, was baptised **30 November 1796** — three and a half years after this wedding. **The identification rests on the COUPLE, not the forename**: this archive holds a second Arcangelo Crisci, the one who married Anna Falco, and it is the pairing with Sara Ruggiero that separates them.

**ATTESTED TWICE ON ONE PAGE**: the same leaf carries the year's index line «*Archangelus Crisci e Sara Ruggiero **1793***» above the act itself. **Both readings are machine transcriptions of the parish hand and the image has not been read.**

**ANDREANA CRISCI'S INFANT SISTER, DEAD AT SEVEN DAYS, THREE MONTHS AFTER ANDREANA'S WEDDING.**

«*…i quali hanno dichiarato che a detto dì **diciassette** del mese corrente di **Gennajo**, ad ore **una** di notte, **CARMELA CRISCI**, **figlia di ARCANGELO CRISCI e SARA RUGGIERO**, **di giorni SETTE**, di professione contadina, domiciliata strada **Camellara***».

**Arcangelo Crisci and Sara Ruggiero are Andreana's own parents** — they consented to her marriage to **Vincenzo Falco on 15 October 1814**, and the act of that marriage names them both. **This child was born about 10 January 1815**, so Sara Ruggiero was carrying her through her daughter's wedding.

**AND THE MAN WHO REPORTED THE DEATH WAS A FALCO.** The second declarant is «*GIUSEPPE FALCO di anni trenta, massaro di campagna, strada Camellara, **vicini della defunta***» — **a neighbour, not a relative**, and not this household's Vincenzo. *The act says «vicini». It does not say «parente», and this archive has been caught before reading a neighbour as kin.* [[relationship-words-magnified]]

events.evidence:
**READ THE ARITHMETIC OF THIS ACT BEFORE USING IT.** It names **four** surviving children, aged **fifteen, twelve, ten and five**, and it makes their father **fifty-three**. A man of fifty-three whose eldest living child is fifteen either married at thirty-eight or **has older children who are not on this list** — and these acts list the children who need a tutor, which is to say the minors. **So this is not a complete list of his children and must not be read as one.**

**IT BEARS ON ALESSANDRA CRISCI.** She married **MATTEO FALCO** on 24 January 1834, and the marriage index gives her parents as «*CRISCI [forename lost to the fold shadow], [QUO]TOLO ANGELA*». This archive filed that as **a resemblance and not a fact**, because Angela Quotolo is not a rare name here and the father's forename cannot be read — **and that still stands.** What this act removes is the obvious objection to it: that Alessandra is not among his children. **She would not be, if she was already grown.** A resemblance with a hole in it is now a resemblance without one, and it is still not a fact.

**This archive held his DEATH — 24 January 1820 — and not his birth.** He was born at four in the afternoon on the twenty-second, baptised that day, and buried on the twenty-fourth. **Two days.**

events.evidence:
«*figlio di **GIOACCHINO CRISCI defunto**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi*» — named in **both** his sons' death acts, and **dead before January 1829**.

**THE SURNAME WAS PUBLISHED HERE AS CIOFFI UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** Both acts were magnified on that day and **both read CRISCI**: a capital **C**, a narrow **r** shoulder, a long **ſ** with its descender, then **ci**. **No round o, which Cossi needs; no tall double-f ligature, which Cioffi needs.** That is this archive's own three-way test, applied to the two documents this household rests on.

**It matters beyond a letter.** A Falco woman marrying a **CRISCI** joins the surname the direct line married twice — Matteo Falco to Francesca Crisci and Vincenzo Falco to Andreana Crisci. **Nothing here joins her to either, and none is claimed**; but the family she married into is not the one this archive had her in.

**A SECOND CHILD FOR A HOUSEHOLD THAT HAD ONE**, and the second document it has ever had. **He is ANIELLO's brother** — seventy-six in July 1843 gives about 1767, two years apart, the same two parents.

**He was married**: **ANTONIA MORGILLO**, another Crisci–Morgillo tie in a town where this archive keeps finding them.

**And both parents are «Defunto» and «Defunta» here**, which moves their deaths from «before 1843» to **before January 1829** — fourteen years.

**Found from the 1829 tavola and then read from the act**, which is the order this archive insists on: the index produced the candidate and the leaf produced the record. **The index spelt him neither Crisci nor Cioffi clearly; the act does.**

**This row replaces an index-only placeholder raised a few hours earlier the same day.** That one read «*C[?]ffi LUCA … [figlio di] GIOACCHINO e FALCO FRANCESCA*» from the 1829 *tavola*, was published as PROBABLE, and said in terms that the surname was in the Crisci/Cossi/Cioffi trap and that **only the act could settle it.** **The act settled it.** The placeholder is not kept beside this one, because two rows for one man is how a person gets counted twice — which this archive did to an Anna Falco and found out the same day.

events.evidence:
**A CARFORA WHO DIED A CAPUCHIN, AND THE REGISTER GIVES BOTH HIS NAMES.**

«*…**PASQUALE VERDICCHIO** — di anni **quaranta**, di professione **domestico**, domiciliato **nel Convento dè Cappuccini** di questa stessa Comune, quali hanno dichiarato che a detto dì **sei** del mese corrente di **Settembre**, ad ore **cinque** della notte, **Fratell'ANGELO D'ARIENZO**, **nel secolo chiamato VINCENZO CARFORA**, **figlio delli furono GIUSEPPE CARFORA, e DOMENICA SIMINO***».

**«Nel secolo chiamato» — «called, in the world».** A friar took a religious name and a place instead of a surname, and **without this formula he would be unfindable**: there is no Carfora in the 1813 index under Angelo d'Arienzo. The declarants are the convent's own household.

**This archive already holds a Falco who took orders** — Don Giovanni Falco, deacon — and a gentry Falco house with a nun in it. **Fra Angelo is not connected to either**; he is recorded because a Carfora in a convent is a Carfora who leaves no descendants and must not be looked for among them. [[don-giovanni-falco-deacon]]

events.evidence:
**ANTONIA DI GUIDA'S BROTHER — THE ONE WHOSE BAPTISM PROVED HER PARENTAGE — SEEN ALIVE AND KEEPING HOUSE.**

«*L'anno **milleottocento quindici**, il giorno **diciotto** del mese di **Marzo** … è comparso **ANGELANDREA DI GUIDA** d'anni **VENTICINQUE**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato in detto Comune, strada **MADDALENA**, ed ha dichiarato … da **TERESA VIGLIOTTA** sua moglie legitima di anni **venticinque**, un **maschio** … **A cui se li è dato il nome di DOMENICO.***»

**He is the hinge of this archive's whole di Guida case.** Baptised **29 November 1791** to *Giuseppe di Guida* and *Maddalena Rivetta*, he died at Arienzo on **21 October 1817** as the husband of **Teresa Vigliotta**, his civil act naming the same parents — **and it was that match, parish against civil, that proved Antonia di Guida's parentage.** [[di-guida-parents]]

**Twenty-five in March 1815 puts his birth about 1790; the parish says November 1791.** *A year out, in the same direction these clerks always err.*

**He is on STRADA MADDALENA — his father's street.**

events.evidence:
**THE CIVIL REGISTER NAMES HIS FATHER, AND IT AGREES WITH THE PARISH.** «*è comparso **ANGELANDREA DI GUIDA DI GIUSEPPE, di anni VENTISEI**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada MADDALENA***».

**This archive had his filiation from the parish baptisms alone** — baptised **29 November 1791**, a child of **GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA and MADDALENA RIVETTA**, which is what makes him **ANTONIA DI GUIDA's brother** and the founder's son's brother-in-law. **«DI GIUSEPPE» in a civil act is an independent document saying the same thing**, and **twenty-six in May 1817 against a baptism of 29 November 1791 is twenty-five and a half** — right to the half-year, which this office almost never manages.

**It is also the only act this archive has of him alive.** He dies on **21 October 1817**, and everything else it holds about him comes from that death.

events.evidence:
**ALIVE ON 15 NOVEMBER 1857 — TWELVE YEARS LATER THAN THIS ARCHIVE'S PREVIOUS LATEST SIGHTING.** «*e di **ANTONIA GUIDA**, domiciliata **ivi***», in her daughter Angela Maria's marriage act, **unmarked**.

**Her window was 2 February 1845 to 1865 and it is now 15 November 1857 to 1865** — and the Arienzo death registers cover every year of what remains, with no di Guida in them. **Work-list row 39 was raised because her old negative might not cover a moved window. The window has moved again, in the same direction, and the negative still covers it.**

*The act writes her surname **GUIDA**, without the particle, as several others do. This archive holds her as **di Guida** and keeps that spelling.*

events.evidence:
**SHE IS DEAD, AND THE WINDOW IS TWENTY-SEVEN MONTHS.** «*e di **ANTONIA GUIDA DEFUNTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — her daughter Maddalena's marriage act, **14 February 1860**, read at magnification.

**And her other daughter's marriage act of 15 NOVEMBER 1857 marks neither parent** — «*figlia di GIUSEPPE FALCO, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di ANTONIA GUIDA, domiciliata ivi*». **Two acts, twenty-seven months apart, from the same register series, about the same woman.**

**AND THE DEATH REGISTERS COVER EVERY MONTH OF THAT WINDOW.** The Arienzo civil deaths are read act by act for **1844–1858** and for **1859**; and on 21 September 2026 the **1860** register (`an_ua14362`) was opened and its acts from **1 January to 5 March** read out — **Giovanni Miglio, Maria Rivetti, Raffaele Crisci, Maria Miglio, Nicola Crisci, Maria Rosa Sartore, Andrea Esposito, Nicola Nuotolo, Paolo d'Ambrogio and five more. No Falco. No Guida.**

**SO SHE IS NOT WHERE SHE HAS TO BE.** Either **a sweep missed her** — and this register enters a married woman as «*[NAME], **moglie di** [HUSBAND]*», so a pass reading only the first name on the line would not see «moglie di GIUSEPPE FALCO» — or **she died outside Arienzo**. *The first is now the likelier and it is cheap to test: re-read the Arienzo deaths of 1858 and 1859 for her name and for her husband's.* **Work-list row 39.**

**The old window was 2 February 1845 to 1865, twenty years wide, and it is now twenty-seven months.**

events.evidence:
**HER BROTHER AND HER SISTER, FOUND ON THE SAME DAY IN TWO VOLUMES NOBODY HAD OPENED.**

- **MARCELLO DI GUIDA**, husband of **ANNA CRISCI**, died **13 February 1813**, «*figlio di Giuseppe di Guida, e della **fu** Maddalena Rivetti*» — with a son **Agostino** who died the next year.
- **MARGARITA DI GUIDA**, wife of **GIACINTO MARRA**, died **15 October 1814**, «*figlia di Giuseppe di Guida, e della Maddalena Rivetti*» — with two infant sons already recorded in this archive's 1810 and 1812 sweeps **and never attached to anybody**.

**Both are identified by BOTH parents named together**, which is what separates this couple from the other di Guida × Rivetta marriage at Arienzo. See [[di-guida-parents]].

**Marcello is not in the baptismal sibling list this archive read in September 2026**, which runs 1773–1791 and gives *Marcellina 1773*. **Whether «Marcellina» is a misreading of «Marcello» is not settled here** and would need the 1773 parish act read again.

events.evidence:
«*in costanza del suo legitimo Matrimonio con **ANTONIA DI GUIDA sua Moglie**, di professione **MASSARA DI CAMPAGNA**, di anni **VENT'OTTO***».

**TWENTY-EIGHT IN FEBRUARY 1811 PUTS HER BIRTH IN 1783 — AND THE PARISH BAPTISED HER ON 31 OCTOBER 1783.** *Not «about». Exact.*

**That matters more than one figure usually would.** Her identification rests on a parish baptism read from the image in September 2026, matched to a brother's civil death act of 1817 — and **Arienzo holds a second di Guida × Rivetta couple** whose forenames are the only thing separating them. **This is a third, independent series agreeing with the first two.** [[di-guida-parents]]

**AND SHE IS GIVEN A TRADE OF HER OWN.** «*MASSARA DI CAMPAGNA*» — not *contadina*, not *filatrice*, but the feminine of her husband's own description. **In four hundred acts read from these seven years, this archive has seen a woman given that trade twice.**

events.evidence:
«***VEDOVA DI FRANCESCO DI GUIDA***» — dead by **June 1810**, husband of a woman of seventy-eight.

**HE IS NOT THE FRANCESCO DI GUIDA THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD.** That one was a declarant on strada Cioffi in **January 1842**, aged **twenty-five**, so born about **1817** — seven years after this man was already dead. **Two men, one name, and nothing links them but the name.**

**WHY HE MATTERS.** *Antonia di Guida*, who married Giuseppe Falco and stands at the head of this archive's fourth generation, was born about **1785**. A Francesco di Guida dead by 1810 with a wife born about 1732 is of the right generation to be **her father or her uncle** — and **nothing in this act says he is either**. It is recorded so the question can be asked of the 1780s marriage registers if they are ever found.

events.evidence:
«*figlio di **GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA***» — no «fu».

**WEAK INFERENCE ONLY, AND THIS PAGE ASSERTED IT UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** It read «*no «fu», **so alive in October 1817**»** — a flat statement of fact. **On 14 September 2026 this archive DISPROVED the «quondam» signal for the parish Latin register**: Matteo Falco is «*filium Matthaei*», with no «q.», **seventeen days after his own burial**. Civil acts are a different tradition and this one is probably sound, **but it no longer carries the weight the sentence gave it.**

**The downgrade was written into `data/households.tsv` on 14 September and never into the file the site is built from**, so the site went on asserting for six days what the archive had already stopped believing. Found by reconciling the two files — work-list row 75.

events.evidence:
**HER BIRTH ACT — AND IT CLOSES A PREDICTION THIS ARCHIVE MADE FROM A NAME.** Act **50**, foglio 89: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **DICIASSETTE** a' dì **VENTICINQUE** del mese di **MAGGIO**, ad ore **DODICI** … è comparso **ANGELANDREA DI GUIDA DI GIUSEPPE, di anni VENTISEI**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada MADDALENA**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato ad ore **OTTO** è nata nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante, e da **TERESA VIGLIOTTA sua moglie legittima, d'anni VENTICINQUE**, una **FEMINA** … a cui si è dato il nome di **MADDALENA***». Witnesses **AGOSTINO MORGILLO, forty, contadino of strada Santa Lucia**, and **TOMASO DELLA SELVA, sixty-five, *serviente comunale***.

**This archive already held a MADDALENA DI GUIDA of this household**, known only from her marriage to ANGELO CILLO about 1845, with the note «**NAMED FOR HER GRANDMOTHER, Maddalena Rivetta — which is what the whole di Guida reconstruction predicts**». **Here is the birth the prediction was about**, and the grandmother's name is on the act's own street.

**Her father died five months later**, on 21 October 1817. **She was born into a marriage with twenty weeks left in it.**

events.evidence:
**ANTONIA DI GUIDA'S BROTHER.** She married Giuseppe Falco and stands at the head of this archive's fourth generation; **this is the first of her brothers this archive has found in a civil death act.**

«*…quali hanno dichiarato che a detto dì **tredici** del mese corrente di **Febraro**, ad ore **diciassette**, **MARCELLO DI GUIDA**, **MARITO DI ANNA CRISCI**, [figlio] **di GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA, e della fu MADDALENA RIVETTI***».

**WHAT MAKES HIM HERS: BOTH PARENTS, NAMED TOGETHER.** Antonia di Guida was baptised at Arienzo on **31 October 1783** to **Giuseppe di Guida**, *massaro di campagna* of strada Maddalena, and **Maddalena Rivetta**. **Arienzo holds a second di Guida × Rivetta couple** — *Filippo di Guida × Margherita Rivetta* — **and the forenames separate them**; this act gives *Giuseppe* and *Maddalena*, not *Filippo* and *Margherita*. [[di-guida-parents]]

**THE SURNAME WAS READ WRONG AT STRIP SIZE AND CORRECTED AT THE IMAGE.** It looked like «**RICCIO**», which would have made this a different household entirely. Magnified nearly three times it is **«RIVETTI»** — the same name the parish writes *Rivetta* and the 1817 civil act writes *Michedalena Rivetti*. [[the-contact-sheet-is-triage]]

**«della FU Maddalena Rivetti» — his mother was dead by February 1813**, which is the earliest bound this archive has on her death.

events.evidence: A DATE FOR A BAPTISM THIS ARCHIVE COULD NOT DATE. «*è morto nella propria casa **PASQUALE DI GUIDA d'anni CINQUANTASETTE**, marito di [forename unread], nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **SENSALE**, domiciliato ivi, **figlio di GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi, **e di MADDALENA RIVETTA Defunta**, domiciliata ivi*» — act 50 of 11 August 1836, at twenty hours. **He is a brother of ANTONIA DI GUIDA**, generation four's mother-in-law, on the same two parents the 1802 marriage act gives her. This archive held him only as a parish baptism of **31 January, year unread**; his trade, his death and a stated age are new. **THE STATED AGE DOES NOT FIT THE OBVIOUS YEAR AND IS NOT FORCED TO.** Fifty-seven in August 1836 implies about **1779** — but this household baptised a **Margherita on 14 March 1779**, six weeks after a 31 January, so the two cannot both be 1779. Either his baptism is 31 January of another year, or the register is guessing his age, which it demonstrably does. The age is recorded as the register's, not as a birth year. **And the father is NOT marked defunto while the mother is** — which this archive does not read as proof he was living, for the reason set out on /corrections.

**AN AGE AND A TRADE FOR ANTONIA DI GUIDA'S BROTHER, WHERE THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEITHER.** Act **55**, foglio 91: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **DICIASSETTE** a' dì **DICIOTTO** del mese di **GIUGNO**, ad ore **SEDICI** … è comparso **PASQUALE DI GUIDA, di anni QUARANTADUE**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in detto Comune, **strada MADDALENA**, ed ha dichiarato … è nato nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante, e da **[NICOLETTA] ESPOSITELLA sua moglie legittima, d'anni TRENTADUE**, un **MASCHIO** … il nome di **RAFFAELE***».

**Forty-two in June 1817 gives b. c.1775**, and his baptism in the Arienzo parish book is «*31 January*» with **the year unread**. **This dates it.** He died on 11 August 1836, which would make him about sixty-one.

**AND HE IS A MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA, not a bracciale.** Antonia di Guida's brother farms on his own account, as her husband **GIUSEPPE FALCO, *massaro*,** does. *The di Guida of strada Maddalena are not labourers.*

events.evidence:
**A DI GUIDA MARRIED TO A CARFORA, AND SHE WAS BORN ABOUT 1724.** Found on 22 September 2026 in the Arienzo death register for **1810** — one of the seven volumes of that decade this archive had never opened — while looking for somebody else entirely.

«*NUM. **15**. Oggi, che sono li **cinque** del mese di **Marzo** dell'anno mille ottocento **dieci** sono comparsi … **DOMENICO VIGLIO**, d'anni **sessantacinque**, bracciale … e **TOMASO MORGILLO**, d'anni **cinquantasei**, bracciale, … abitante nella strada della **Porta di Sopra** — ed hanno dichiarato, che oggi suddetto giorno ad ore **nove** è morta **TERESA DI GUIDA**, d'anni **OTTANTASEI**, di professione **MENDICA**, domiciliante in detta Università, ed abitante nella strada della **Porta di Sopra**, **VEDOVA DI STEFANO CARFORA***».

**Eighty-six in March 1810 puts her birth about 1724** — **the earliest di Guida this archive can name, by three generations** — and she died a **beggar**.

**SHE JOINS TWO OF THIS ARCHIVE'S SURNAMES A CENTURY BEFORE THEY MEET AGAIN.** A **di Guida** married a **Carfora**; four generations later **Antonia di Guida** married Giuseppe Falco, and **Maria Antonia Carfora** married into the Annecchino. **No kinship between these households is claimed** — di Guida and Carfora are both Arienzo surnames and this archive has learnt what a shared name is worth.

**Her trade differs between the two acts** — *contadino* is attached to her husband here, and in 1810 she herself is a **mendica**, a beggar. **These do not contradict each other**: she had been a widow for an unknown number of years by 1810 and died on alms.
