events.evidence:
**THE EARLIEST ACT THIS ARCHIVE HAS FOR THIS HOUSEHOLD, AND IT CARRIES HER FATHER'S SIGNATURE.** Act **52**: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **DICIANNOVE**, a' dì **VENTISETTE** del mese di **APRILE**, ad ore **UNDICI**, avanti di noi **ANDREA SORICE Sindaco** … è comparso **ALFONSO DIGLIO, di anni VENTISETTE**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in detto comune **strada CAMELLARA**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato … è nata nella sua propria casa **da lui dichiarante, e da MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, d'anni VENTISETTE**, una **FEMINA** che ci ha presentata … a cui si è dato il nome di **ALESSANDRA***». Baptised at Sant'Andrea **29 April 1819**.

**THE DATE IS PROVED BY THE REGISTER'S ORDER AND NEEDS NO HANDWRITING.** Act **51** is **22 April** and act **53** is **1 May**; act 52 falls between them, and the day word reads *ventisette*.

**HER FATHER SIGNED HIS OWN NAME.** «*…ed indi firmato da noi, **e dal dichiarante**, avendo i testimonj asserito di non sapere scrivere*» — and at the foot, in large block capitals, **«A ALFONSO DIGLIO»**. **Both witnesses could not write and he could.** This archive holds one other autograph from these streets, **Pasquale Falco's of 1814**.

Witnesses **ANDREA MARTONE, thirty-seven, *falegname*, of strada SANT'ANDREA**, and **DOMENICO LAUDATO, fifty-two, contadino, of strada SANT'ANDREA**.

**She pushes this household back three years.** It was known from **1822** onwards, with a marriage index entry of 19 November 1813 and nothing between. *Found by reading the 1819 birth register for work-list row 86 — a volume that had never been read.*

Act 78: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **ventidue**, il dì **TRE** del mese di **SETTEMBRE**, ad ore diciassette, avanti di Noi **VINCENZO MORGILLO Sindaco** … è comparso **ALFONSO DIGLIO, di anni TRENTUNO, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTUNO***», and the INDICAZIONE has the **Parroco di Sant'Andrea Apostolo** returning the notice **the same day**, naming the child **SALVATORE**.

**A child for a household this archive knew by its mother's name and little else.** She is thirty-one here, so born about 1791. **This is not the Maria Falco of Francesco Cioffi** — that couple's own daughter Antonia was born on **30 September 1822**, twenty-seven days later, on the same street, and her mother is given as **twenty-four**. Two women of one name on one street, and the register separates them by their husbands.

events.evidence:
**IN A YEAR THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED AS «NO FALCO».** Act **49**: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **DICIASSETTE** a' dì **QUINDICI** del mese di **MAGGIO**, ad ore **VENTI**, avanti di noi **ANDREA SORICE Sindaco** … è comparso **ALFONSO DIGLIO, di anni VENTOTTO**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato in detto Comune, **strada CAMELLARA**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato ad ore **DICIANNOVE** è nato nella sua propria casa **da lui dichiarante, e da MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, d'anni VENTISETTE**, un **MASCHIO** … a cui si è dato il nome di **SALVATORE***». Witnesses **CESARE DIGLIO, fifty, contadino of strada CAMELLARA**, and **NICOLA DIGLIO, thirty-eight**.

**HE IS THE FIRST SALVATORE.** This household's **SALVATORE DIGLIO born 3 September 1822** is the second — **five years and four months later**, and this family names the next child after the one it buries. *What became of the first is not recorded here and is not assumed.*

**AND HE PUSHES THE HOUSEHOLD BACK AGAIN.** With Alessandra of April 1819 this is now the earliest of its children, two years earlier still, and it puts the couple on **strada Camellara** within four years of their marriage of 19 November 1813.

*Found by reading the 1817 birth register act by act for work-list row 86 — a volume this archive had published as holding no Falco at all.*

events.evidence:
**A CHILD OF THIS HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE, AND THE LAST FALCO ACT ANTENATI CAN REACH.** Arienzo, Matrimoni **1865**, **act 3**, image 5 right — the first Falco found in the Arienzo marriage registers of **1861–1865**, which had never been read:

«*ATTO DI SOLENNE PROMESSA DI MATRIMONIO — Num. d'ord. **3**. L'anno mille ottocento **sessantacinque**, il dì **ventitre** di **Gennajo**, alle ore **quindici**, avanti di Noi **RAFFAELE VIVOTTI Sindaco** ed uffiziale dello Stato Civile di **Arienzo**, distretto di **Caserta** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **VINCENZO ABATIELLO**, di anni **quaranta**, nato in **Liveri**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi, figlio del **fu ANTONIO**, di professione simile, e di **fu ALESSANDRA ALVANESE** — ed **ANGELA FALCO**, di anni **ventotto**, nata in **Arienzo**, domiciliata in **Arienzo**, figlia di **MATTEO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ALESSANDRA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***».

**TWENTY-EIGHT IN JANUARY 1865 PUTS HER BIRTH ABOUT 1837** — between this couple's marriage in January 1834 and their daughter Domenica of September 1846. *Her birth act has not been looked for; the Arienzo births of 1837 are read and this archive should go back to them with her name.*

**THE ACT DOES TWO OTHER THINGS.** It keeps **both her parents alive on 23 January 1865**, in a sentence that marks the groom's parents dead. And it **spells her mother's surname**, which the 1846 birth act left deliberately unread.

**She marries out of the town.** Vincenzo Abatiello is forty, a *contadino* of **LIVERI**, in the Nola plain — twelve years her senior and an orphan of both parents.

events.evidence:
**A FALCO WOMAN MARRIED OUT, AND A GENERATION EARLY.** Alive in 1809, *massara*, bearing a child — so born roughly **1770–1790**.

**SHE IS NOT THE ANGELA FALCO THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS.** That one is the daughter of **Matteo Falco and Francesca Crisci**, born at Arienzo in **1822** — thirteen years after this woman is burying an infant. **Same name, and half a century between them.** [[angela-falco-1822]]

**WHAT THIS OPENS.** A Falco daughter of the 1770s or 1780s is of the generation of **Matteo Falco**, this archive's head of line. *She is a candidate for his sister and nothing in this act says she is.*

events.evidence:
**A NEW GRANDDAUGHTER OF THE FOUNDER, AND THE ACT NAMES HIM.** Act 8: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **ventidue**, il dì **DICIANNOVE** del mese di **GENNARO**, ad ore quindici, avanti di Noi **VINCENZO MORGILLO Sindaco** … è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA sua moglie legittima, di anni QUARANTA**, domiciliata collo stesso … nel giorno **DICIANNOVE** del mese di Gennaro, anno corrente, **alle ore DODICI**, nella casa sua propria di abitazione … il nome di **ANGELA MARIA***».

**Witnessed by OTTAVIO MIGLIORE**, thirty-nine, of **strada Croce dell'Ospedale**, and **GENNARO MAJONE SENIORE**, forty-three, *contadino*, of **strada Caldarola** — and the act closes naming the declarant again, «*Signor **GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO***». The INDICAZIONE has the **Parroco di Sant'Andrea Apostolo** returning the notice **the same day**, naming the child «**ANGELA MARIA FALCO**».

**«FU MATTEO» is the phrase this archive built a generation on.** It is what separates the Camellara Giuseppe — this line's own — from the Giuseppe Falco of strada Costa who married Gelsomina Vigliotta. Here it is again, in his own daughter's birth act, eight years after the notarial consent that first proved Matteo dead.

**She fills a gap.** This household's known children ran **Crescenzo, 11 October 1819**, then nothing until **Clemente, 11 March 1824**. Angela Maria sits between them. Both parents are given as **forty**, which puts them about 1782 — against Antonia's baptism of **31 October 1783**, close enough for these registers and not adopted.

**HER MARRIAGE — AND IT MOVES HER PARENTS' LAST SIGHTING BY EIGHT YEARS AND TWELVE.** Arienzo, Matrimoni **1857**, **act 26**, found on 21 September 2026 in a volume this archive had never opened:

«*Atto di solenne promessa di matrimonio — Num. d'ordine **26**. L'anno mille ottocento cinquanta**sette**, il dì **quindici** di **Novembre** … avanti di Noi **CARLO CARFORA Sindaco** ed uffiziale dello Stato Civile di **Arienzo**, distretto di **Caserta** … comparsi nella Casa Comunale **RAFFAELE MORGILLO**, di anni **trenta**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato ivi, figlio di **NICOLA MORGILLO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **MARIA MAJONE**, domiciliata ivi; ed **ANGELA MARIA FALCO**, di anni **trentacinque**, nata in **Arienzo**, domiciliata ivi, figlia di **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ANTONIA GUIDA**, domiciliata **ivi***».

**Thirty-five in November 1857 is a woman born in 1822, and her birth act is 19 January 1822.** The identification needs no argument.

**AND NEITHER OF HER PARENTS IS MARKED DEAD.** No «fu», no «defunto», no «defunta» — in a form that prints the space for them and in a register whose clerks use the words constantly. **See their own rows below.**

A NEW CHILD FOR GENERATION THREE, found through the 1826 register's own tavola. «…è nato da ANDREANA CRISCI, di anni VENTOTTO, domiciliata ivi STRADA CAMELLARA, e da VINCENZO FALCO marito della stessa, di anni TRENTADUE, di professione CONTADINO … nel giorno DODICI del mese di SETTEMBRE … alle ore ventidue, nella casa d'abitazione di detti conjugi … il nome di ANGELANDREA». NOT JOINED to the ANGELO Falco who married Maria Cimmino in 1847 or the ANDREA Falco who married Maria Carmela — this household already contains both, each known only from a marriage act, and «Angelandrea» may be either or neither

**VERIFIED WORD FOR WORD, work-list row 58 — act 69, the second half of which is on image 71 LEFT.** «*è nato da **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di anni **VENTOTTO**, domiciliata **ivi strada Camellara**, e da **VINCENZO FALCO marito della stessa**, di anni **TRENTADUE**, di professione contadino, domiciliato con detta sua moglie, nel giorno **dodici** del mese di **Settembre** … nella casa d'abitazione di detti conjugi … il nome di **ANGELANDREA***».

**THE MOTHER DECLARED THIS BIRTH HERSELF** — «*La stessa ha in oltre dichiarato di dare allo stesso il nome*» — with the father named only as «marito della stessa». **The witness is CLEMENTE SANSONE, twenty-six, contadino**, which is the surname settled from three other acts on 20 September 2026.

**With this act the couple's ages line up against their baptisms**: he is thirty-two here against a baptism of 1 February 1792 (thirty-four), she twenty-eight against 30 November 1796 (twenty-nine). **Every volume but 1816 is within two years. 1816 is out by eleven and six.**

events.evidence: THE ACT THAT LIFTS A REFUSAL THIS ARCHIVE MADE ON PURPOSE. «3. FALCO ANGELANDREA | Arienzo | FALCO VINCENZO, e CRISCI ANDREANA» ed «CIMMINO MARIA | Arienzo | CIMMINO ALESSANDRO, e SOLLI [ROSA]», the church date given as «**29 MARZO**» [1847] — READ AGAIN 20 Sep 2026 at 3,000 px, where the second digit carries a full descender loop; the act number **4** two rows above it on the same page has none. This archive published it as «24 MARZO». When Angelandrea's birth act of 12 September 1826 was published, it was DELIBERATELY NOT JOINED to «the ANGELO Falco who married Maria Cimmino in 1847 or the ANDREA Falco who married Maria Carmela», because the household held all three names and each of the other two was known only from a parish marriage act. THE CIVIL INDEX SETTLES ONE HALF: the man who married MARIA CIMMINO, daughter of Alessandro and Rosa Solli, is written ANGELANDREA — the exact name of the 1826 birth act — so ANGELO of the parish act and ANGELANDREA of the birth act are ONE MAN, married at TWENTY. The ANDREA who married Maria Carmela, daughter of Onofrio and Angela Imbimbo, REMAINS A SEPARATE SON and is still not joined to anything. DATE DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: this tavola gives the church wedding as 24 March 1847 and the parish record held here gives 17 April 1847 — the same kind of civil-versus-parish disagreement already documented for Raffaele Falco's marriage of 1844

events.evidence: **«MINORE» — AND THAT ONE WORD CONFIRMS HIS BIRTH ACT.** Act on img4r: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANGELANDREA FALCO MINORE**, di anni **venti[…]**, nato in Arienzo, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, **colono**, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, **filatrice** … e **MARIA CIMMINO maggiore** … nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Capodiconca**, figlia di **ALESSANDRO CIMMINO**, contadino*». Church **29 March 1847** at Sant'Andrea. Witnesses **Gennaro Laudato** and Francesco de Angelis. **MAJORITY WAS TWENTY-ONE**, so «minore» puts him under it — and his birth act of **12 September 1826** makes him twenty years and six months. The numeral itself carries a flourish and is not read beyond «venti[…]»; **the word «minore» is what bounds him, and it is unambiguous.** **A DATE CONFLICT, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED:** this archive also holds «Angelo Falco … m. Maria Cimmino» on **17 April 1847** from a parish ark — the same bride, three weeks later. Both are kept. **AND THE ACT'S OWN INDICAZIONE COLUMN SETTLES THE CHURCH DATE, READ 20 SEPTEMBER 2026**: «*Il Parroco di SANT'ANDREA … ha certificato, che la celebrazione del matrimonio è seguita nel giorno **VENTINOVE** del mese di MARZO anno corrente*» — the priest's own certificate, copied into the register, spelling the day out in words. **The same day as the civil promise.** The index's date was read here as «24 MARZO» and it is 29; under this system the church cannot precede the promise, so a 24 was impossible on its face. For contrast, act 20 of 1848 in the next volume has the promise on **19 August** and the church on **23 August** — four days later, which is the usual shape.

events.evidence:
**A FALCO OF STRADA CAMELLARA BORN ABOUT 1747, AND THE PARENTS HE IS GIVEN ARE A GENERATION THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT HAVE.**

«*li quali hanno sottoscritta la dichiarazione della morte seguita il dì **terza — 3** del mese di **Gennaro** dell'anno **Mille ottocento, ed undici** in persona del Signor **ANGELO FALCO**, di anni **SESSANTAQUATTRO**, di professione **BRACCIALE**, nato in **Arienzo**, domiciliato in questa stessa Comune, e strada **CAMELLARA**, **figlio dalli furono GIUSEPPE FALCO, e ROSA SPOSITO***».

**«FURONO» — PLURAL. Both his parents were already dead on 3 January 1811.**

**THE FATHER'S NAME WAS SETTLED BY A CONTROL LETTER.** «*Giuseppe*» and «*Giuseppa*» end in the same cramped glyph in this hand. The word was set beside «**Giuseppe Verdicchio**» — a man, certain, written by the same clerk six images earlier in the same volume — and **the terminal letters match**. [[surname-ligature-test]]

**HOW THIS WAS FOUND, AND WHY IT WAS NOT FOUND SOONER.** This archive read the 1811 death register on 21 September 2026 and published it as read in full. **It was not.** The volume puts **two acts on every image** — even numbers on the left page, odd on the right — and only the right pages were swept. **Angelo Falco is act 2.** He sat in the half that was never opened, in a volume this archive had already called finished. [[the-tavola-page-break]]

**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** Sixty-four in January 1811 puts his birth about **1747**, which is the generation of **Matteo Falco**, this archive's head of line, who died in 1802 — and he lived on **strada Camellara**, where Matteo's people lived. **That is a reason to look, not a reason to join them.** Nothing in this act names Matteo, and **a shared street and a shared surname have twice in this archive turned out to mean nothing**. [[two-falco-families-arienzo]]

**He is given no wife and no children.** In this register a married man is given «*marito di*» and his survivors are counted; Angelo Falco is given his parents instead. **At sixty-four that is a statement that he left none.**

«*è morta nella sua propria casa **ANNA FALCO, di mesi TREDICI**, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, domiciliata ivi, **figlia di MICHELANGELO FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, **e di MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — died **4 May 1831** at thirteen hours, thirteen months old, so born about **April 1830**. **Verified from the image, work-list row 58.**

**THE CITATION POINTED AT IMAGE 19 RIGHT, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT CHILD** — Carmina Maccaniello, ten months, daughter of Pasquale Maccaniello and Raffaela Zimbardo, dead on 28 April. **The act is on IMAGE 20 RIGHT**, found by sweeping the volume's date lines.

**AND IT SHARPENS THE QUESTION RAISED ELSEWHERE TODAY.** This archive now holds **two Anna Falco, three years apart, each «figlia di MICHELANGELO FALCO», with two different mothers**: this one **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, and the Anna of 16 March 1834 **RAFFAELA FALCO**. **A remarriage between them is excluded** if this Mariantonia Vigliotta is the woman who was still bearing children to a Michele Falco in 1834, 1836 and 1842 and whom he survived in 1850. **So either there are two Michelangelo Falco at Arienzo, or one of the two mothers is misread.** Both mothers have now been read from the image at full resolution. **Neither reading is in doubt; the identification is.**

**And the declarant is the reason this household is kin at all**: «*e **VINCENZO FALCO**, di anni **trentotto**, di professione contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, **PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA***», where **ANDREA CRISCI, fifty-eight**, beside him is only «**VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA**». **The clerk drew the distinction himself, in one sentence.** Read from the image on 20 September 2026.

**THIS CHILD IS NOT RECORDED AS THIS COUPLE'S, AND THE ROW IS LEFT STANDING RATHER THAN DELETED.** Until 20 September 2026 an **ANNA FALCO, eight days old, dead 7 March 1834** stood here as a daughter of Michelangelo Falco and **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**.

**The act was found and read.** It is act 16, image 11 left, of **16 March 1834**, and it says «*figlia di **MICHELANGELO FALCO** … e di **RAFFAELA FALCO***». **The mother is not Mariantonia Vigliotta.**

**So she is published under MICHELANGELO FALCO & RAFFAELA FALCO instead**, and whether that Michelangelo is this one — widowed and remarried — or a second man of the name is an open question this archive does not close by assuming.

events.evidence:
**HER BIRTH — AND IT IS THIS HOUSEHOLD'S FIRST CHILD, FIFTEEN MONTHS AFTER ITS WEDDING.** Act **43**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **TRENTA**, il dì **VENTIQUATTRO** del mese di **MARZO**, ad ore **TREDICI**, avanti di noi **VITO MARIA ROMANO Sindaco** … è comparsa **ROSA DELLA SELVA, di anni SETTANTANOVE**, di professione **LEVATRICE**, domiciliata in questo Comune strada Porta di Sopra, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, di anni VENTICINQUE**, domiciliata in **strada CAMELLARA**, e da **MICHELANGELO FALCO marito della stessa, di anni VENTI**, di professione **CONTADINO** … nel giorno **VENTIQUATTRO** del mese di **MARZO** … **alle ore UNDICI, nella casa d'abitazione di detti conjugi** … di dare alla neonata il nome di **ANNA***». Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo** the same day. Witnesses **MARCELLO ARRIGALE, forty-three, *viaticale*, of strada CAPODICONCA**, and **NICOLA ESPOSITELLA, forty-six, *viaticale*, of strada COSSI**.

**THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES TO THE WEEK.** Her death act, already held, says «*di mesi **TREDICI***» on **4 May 1831**. **Born 24 March 1830 she was thirteen months and ten days.**

**A MIDWIFE PRESENTED HER, WHICH IS WHY THE PARENTS BAND COULD FIND HER AT ALL** — where a midwife declares, both parents are named on the left page. **This household's whole documented life is now three acts**: the marriage of December 1828, this birth, and this death.

**AND IT MAKES THE AGE PROBLEM WORSE FOR MICHELANGELO FALCO.** He is **twenty** here in March 1830, **twenty-six** in July 1832 and **thirty-four** in September 1838 — **b. c.1810, c.1806, c.1804**. **Fourteen years of ageing in eight.** Whether the Michelangelo of strada Sant'Andrea in 1838 is this man is an open question, and these figures cannot settle it either way.

*The clerk writes the mother **ANTONIA** here and **MARIANTONIA** in 1831; this archive has published that the office uses the two indifferently.*

events.evidence:
**THE EARLIEST DATED RECORD THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS, BY FOUR YEARS — AND IT WAS FOUND LOOKING FOR SOMEBODY ELSE.** The Arienzo birth register for **1813** had never been opened here; it was opened on 22 September 2026 to test work-list row 87, and it holds **one Falco act in fifty-three and this is it**:

«*NUMERO D'ORDINE **2**. L'Anno mille ottocento **tredici** a' **dì cinque** del mese di **Gennaro**, ad ore **quindici**, avanti di noi **VINCENZO MORGILLO Sindaco** … del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Provincia di Terra di Lavoro, **è comparso GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni TRENTATRÉ, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in detto Comune, STRADA COSTA**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato ad ore **dodici** è nato nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante, e da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA sua moglie legittima, di anni VENTOTTO**, un **maschio**, che ci ha presentato. **A cui si è dato il nome di ANTONIO***».

**Both ages agree with what this archive had already inferred.** Giuseppe Falco at thirty-three in January 1813 is born about **1780**; this household says *b. c.1780*. Gelsomina Vigliotta at twenty-eight is born about **1785**; this household says *b. c.1784*. **The two were guesses from an 1816 act and they hold.**

**And the street holds too** — **strada COSTA** in 1813 as in 1816, three years before this family appears on strada Camellara.

**Nothing further is known of him.** He is not among the children this household already carries, and no Antonio Falco of this house has been found in any later act.

This Carmina is documented by a single act: she died on 19 December 1832 «di mesi SEI» — at six months old — «figlia di FRANCESCO FALCO, contadino, e di RAFFAELA FALCO», on strada Camellara. line.note: Birth record of 10 July 1850 names his father as Raffaele. Five further children recorded at Arienzo, 1873–1883. His son Raffaele's birth extract of 1873 names him «CARMINANTONIO FALCO di Raffaele, contadino, DI ANNI VENTIDUE, domiciliato in Arienzo VIA DEGLI ORTI» — corroborating a birth about 1850–51 from a document rather than from the tree, and giving the household's address. His wife appears as «GIOVANNA ARRICALE FU FRANCESCO», which spells her surname ARRICALE and names her father for the first time. A DAUGHTER IS NOW DOCUMENTED: the banns of August 1902 name «FALCO ANGELA ROSA, di anni VENTIDUE, contadina, figlia di CARMINANTONIO … e figlia di ARRICALE GIOVANNA», marrying FRANCESCO ESPOSITO, 26, colono of San Felice a Cancello, son of Paolo and the late Marta Morgillo. She was born about 1880 and named for her grandmother Angela Rosa Morgillo, who died that April. Carminantonio's own age is given as forty-six in 1897 and fifty-five in 1902 — nine years of ageing in five, which is the clerks guessing, and his recorded birth of 10 July 1850 sits between them.

line.note: Born at Arienzo, resident in the province of Benevento, died at Brisbane and buried at Nudgee Cemetery in niche CHAP-082-B2. His wife Filomena Annecchino died on 10 August 1988 and lies beside him in B1. Two of their sons, Carmine and Raffaele, married two Zampiello sisters of Arpaia and both brought their families to Brisbane. Their own arrivals were untraced for years and are now found: FILOMENA reached Australia on 5 FEBRUARY 1968 and CARMINANTONIO on 19 MAY 1969, with a second crossing by him on 24 July 1972 — three entries in the national passenger lists (NAA barcodes 9788535 p.251, 12211391 p.1711 and 12047001 p.1605), identified on the forename and the dates, with the images not yet pulled. They followed their son, who had landed at Brisbane in March 1964. AND THEY ARE DOCUMENTED IN ITALY AT LAST. Forchia, atti di morte 1937, atto 17: on the morning of 2 August 1937 «FALCO CARMINANTONIO, di anni TRENTASEI, contadino, domiciliato in Forchia» came to the Casa Comunale to report that «è morto FALCO ANIELLO, di mesi nove … da Carminantonio, contadino, e da ANNECCHINO FILOMENA, casalinga, domiciliata in Forchia», at Contrada CASE SPARSE number 68. It is THE FIRST DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS FOUND THAT NAMES FILOMENA ANNECCHINO, it corroborates Carminantonio's birth year of 1901 for the first time, and it documents a son, Aniello, born at Forchia about November 1936 and dead at nine months.

events.evidence:
THE CIVIL ACT BEHIND THE CHURCH DATE, AND IT DATES HIS BIRTH. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **CRESCENZO FALCO maggiore di anni VENTICINQUE nato in ARIENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **IVI strada Sant'Andrea**, figlio di **GIUSEPPE FALCO** di professione simile domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** di professione contadina domiciliata **ivi***» — TRANSCRIPTION CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive wrote «domiciliato **in** strada Sant'Andrea» and the act reads «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea». The dropped word matters, because «ivi» in these forms means THE COMUNE and not the street — the bride in this very act is «domiciliata **ivi strada Cappuccini**», one word and two streets. So GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA are recorded here as domiciled AT ARIENZO, and THE ACT DOES NOT GIVE THEIR STREET. Anything this archive concluded about the household leaving strada Camellara rests on a word that was never there — bride **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, 23, contadina, of strada Cappuccini, «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO** … e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE** … **defunta***». The INDICAZIONE records the church celebration: **3 February 1845**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, witnesses **Luigi Verdicchio** and **Nunzio Rivetti**. TWENTY-FIVE ON 2 FEBRUARY 1845 puts his birth between 3 February 1819 and 2 February 1820 — and his civil birth act is 11 October 1819.

**RE-READ IN FULL, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58 — and one thing in it was nearly "corrected" and is right.** The act says «**maggiore** di anni venticinque», and «maggiore di anni X» is elsewhere a statement of legal majority, not of age; on that reading the act would bound his birth on one side only and «it dates his birth» would be false. **The control is four lines below, in the same sentence: the bride is «maggiore di anni VENTITRE».** No age of majority is twenty-three. **So «maggiore» is a status and the number is the age**, for both of them, and the inference stands. Everything else verifies: act 3, «Domenico Zinelli Sindaco», Arienzo, **distretto di CASERTA**, ore ventuno; «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea»; the church celebration on **3 February** before **LUIGI VERDICCHIO** and **NUNZIO RIVETTI**.

events.evidence:
**THE MARGIN OF HER BIRTH ACT CARRIES HER WEDDING, TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER.** Written vertically down the left edge: «*(1) **a 10 Ottobre 1874** l'Uff[icial]e dello Stato Civile d'**Arienzo** sposò **DOMENICA FALCO** con **PASQUA[LE]…ANTONIO GUIDA***», and beneath it the registrar's own dating, «*Caserta **31 Luglio 1884***». **The husband's forename is cut by the binding** — «Pasqua…» on one line and «…lantonio» on the next, so **Pasqualantonio**, the Neapolitan compound — but **GUIDA is clear**, and the tree had already called her «Domenica Falco (Guida)» from nothing but family memory. **THIS IS A MARRIAGE OF 1874, IN A SERIES ANTENATI STOPS FILMING IN 1865.** The margin reaches nine years past the end of the registers.

**AND THERE IS A SECOND MARGIN ON THE SAME ACT, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD NOT READ.** In the right-hand column, below the registrar's signature: «*(1) **A 25 Marzo 1881** l'Uff.le dello Stato Civ.le d'**ARIENZO** sposò **DOMENICA FALCO** con **PASQUALE SACCAVINO*** — **Caserta 16 Giugno 1884***».

**SHE MARRIED TWICE.** The first margin, down the left edge, gives **10 October 1874** and **Pasqualantonio Guida**; this one gives **25 March 1881** and **PASQUALE SACCAVINO**, dated at Caserta seven weeks before the other. **So Pasqualantonio Guida died between October 1874 and March 1881**.

**One birth act, two marriages, both after the year Antenati stops filming the series.** The margin method reaches **thirty-five years** past the register it is written in — and the second margin was on the page the whole time this archive was quoting the first.

events.evidence:
FROM THE MARGIN OF HIS OWN BIRTH ACT, not from any marriage register: «*Con atto **6 agosto 1856** at[to] **21** in **S[?] …a Vico** il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI** [di] **Gaspare**(?)*». **THE COMUNE IS NOT ESTABLISHED.** At five times magnification the place reads «*S[?]basia a Vico*» and resolves no further. **SANTA MARIA A VICO IS THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE AND IS EXCLUDED BY ITS OWN REGISTER**: `an_ua55736`, *Matrimoni* 1856, **act 21 is Don Domenico de Lucia, 29, of San Felice, promised 14 June 1856** — no Falco, and no act of 6 August (act 31 is 3 August, act 32 is 9 August). **What is certain is the annotation itself**: a Falco of this house married a DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI on 6 August 1856, recorded as act 21 somewhere «…a Vico». The bride's father reads **Gaspare** rather than the Giuseppe first published. Note that the groom's own mother is a **VIGLIOTTA**; whether the two families are one is NOT established.

**IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS ARCHIVE USED A BIRTH-ACT MARGIN AS A SOURCE**, and the rule it produced — that a civil birth act can carry the child's later marriage, in another comune, where no local register shows it — has since found Pasqua Falco's marriage of 1880, Giovanna Arricale's of 1872 and **both** of Domenica Falco's, of 1874 and 1881.

**THE PARISH BAPTISM BESIDE THE CIVIL ACT THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD.** «*Anno D[omi]ni millesimo octingentesimo decimonono **1819**, die vero **decimaoctava 18 mensis Martii** … baptizavit infantem natum ex **JOSEPHO FALCO** e **GELSUMINA [VIGLIOTTA]** conjugibus ex sua Parochia, et vocavit … **DOMINICUS CLEMENS**. **Matrina fuit … d'Addio**. HYACINTHUS Archip. MORGILLO*».

**READ THE DATES TOGETHER AND THEY ARE HARD TO READ AT ALL.** This household buried **DOMENICO** and **ROSARIA** on **15 March 1819**, eleven hours apart. **Three days later they baptised this boy and called him Domenico.** The mother was at full term when the two elder children died.

events.evidence:
e nato nella sua propria casa... un maschio... a cui si e dato il nome di Domenico — born at four in the night

**VERIFIED WORD FOR WORD, work-list row 58** — act 116, image 60 left: «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **trentasei**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPO**, domiciliato in detto comune, **STRADA COSTA** … da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA** d'anni **trentadue**, sua moglie legittima, un **Maschio** … a cui si è dato il nome di **DOMENICO***», born at **four in the night**.

**AND THE STREET IS A WARNING.** This couple are on **strada Costa** in 1816 and on **STRADA CAMELLARA** by March 1823, when the same Giuseppe Falco — forty-two, *massaro di campagna* — declares Pasqua's birth there with the same wife. **The ages agree across both acts** (thirty-six and forty-two; thirty-two and thirty-eight).

**THE DATE WAS WRONG BY FOUR YEARS AND IS CORRECTED HERE — 21 September 2026.** This row said the street stopped telling the two Giuseppe Falco apart **«from 1823»**. **It stopped in 1819.** Act 33 of the 1819 birth register — held in this archive since before this week, on this couple's own page — reads «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **TRENTOTTO**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in detto comune **strada CAMELLARA** … e da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA** sua moglie legittima*», on **18 March 1819**. **Seven months later the other Giuseppe Falco — a *contadino* married to Antonia di Guida — declares a birth on the same street.** Two men of one name on one street in one year, told apart only by trade and by wife.

**So strada Camellara has never been a discriminator for these two households in any year this archive reads.** The 1823 date was an artefact of which acts had been read first, and it was contradicted by another row of the same household.

name: Domenico Falco (m. 1844, Santa Maria a Vico)

events.evidence:
**THIS HOUSEHOLD WAS LIVING IN A PAGE TEMPLATE.** It was named on the **which-falco** disambiguation page — which exists to keep the other Arienzo Falco apart from this line — and **it was in no data file**, so it had no person pages, no place in the search index and no way for a reader to reach it. *Found on 22 September 2026 by auditing that page's eighteen couples against the household file: three had no household and two were spelled differently in the prose than in the data.* **The facts below are the page's own; the acts behind them are named and, where they have not been re-read, said to be.**

**Married 1 July 1844 at SANTA MARIA A VICO.** The which-falco page calls him «*the son of the other Giuseppe Falco and Gelsomina Vigliotta*» — the strada Costa house, not the strada Camellara one.

**WHICH DOMENICO HE IS, IS NOT SETTLED AND IS NOT CLAIMED.** That household holds a **DOMENICO FALCO born 25 November 1816 who died on 15 March 1819**, and a **DOMENICO CLEMENTE FALCO born 18 March 1819 who married on 6 August 1856**. *A man marrying in 1844 is neither of those two as this archive currently reads them* — so either there is a third Domenico, or one of the two identifications is wrong. **The act of 1 July 1844 is at Santa Maria a Vico and has not been read here.**

events.evidence:
«figlio di **GIOACCHINO CRISCI defunto**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, E DI FRANCESCA FALCO defunta» — from the death act of her son Aniello Cioffi — **who died on 26 July 1843**, in an act drawn the following day and published here as 27 July until 20 September 2026 — verified at full resolution. Her son was seventy-six, so born about 1767, which places her marriage in the seventeen-sixties and her own birth in the seventeen-forties: the generation of MATTEO FALCO himself. NOTHING NAMES HER PARENTS and this archive does not guess at them.

**AND HER DEATH WINDOW CLOSES BY FOURTEEN YEARS.** She was «defunta» in her son ANIELLO's act of 27 July 1843; she is **already «defunta» in her son LUCA's act of 16 January 1829**, found on 20 September 2026. **She died before January 1829**, and her husband with her.

events.evidence:
**A FALCO WOMAN WHO MARRIED A CRISCI, AND SHE BORE A SON ABOUT 1765.**

**WHY THIS IS THE EARLIEST FALCO THIS ARCHIVE CAN REACH.** A woman with a son born in 1765 was herself born around **1735–1745** — a full generation above **Matteo Falco**, this archive's head of line, who died in 1802.

**AND SHE MARRIED A CRISCI.** Matteo Falco's own wife was **Francesca Crisci**; his son Vincenzo married **Andreana Crisci**. **A Falco–Crisci marriage two generations before either of those is exactly the shape this archive has been looking for** — and **this act does not connect them**. It gives a name, a husband and a son, and nothing else. [[founders-children]]

**SHE IS NOT SAID TO BE DEAD, AND THAT PROVES NOTHING.** «*figlio del **fu** Gioacchino, e di Francesca Falco*» — the «fu» attaches to the father alone. **This archive has already been wrong once by reading a missing «fu» as evidence of life.** [[quondam-not-evidence]]
events.ark: ANTENATI an_ua14311 img5 — READ FROM THE IMAGE

events.evidence:
**EIGHTY YEARS OLD. SHE IS THE EARLIEST FALCO THIS ARCHIVE CAN DATE.**

«*…quali hanno dichiarato che a detto dì **undeci** del mese corrente di **Novembre**, ad ore **nove**, **FRANCESCA FALCO**, **VEDOVA DI GIOACCHINO CRISCI**, figlia delli furono **GIUSEPPE [·····]**, e ⟨———⟩ … di anni **OTTANTA** — di professione **contadina**, domiciliata nella **strada delli CRISCI** — **è morta nella sua propria casa***».

**Eighty in November 1813 puts her birth about 1733** — a generation and a half above **Matteo Falco**, who died in 1802. Her son Francesco Crisci was born about **1765**, when she was thirty-two, which the two acts agree on without being made to.

**THE DECLARANTS ARE «PARENTI DELLA DEFONTA»** — her kin — a *bracciale* of strada delli Crisci and **ARCANGELO CRISCI**, forty-two. The act does not say how either is related.

**AND HERE THE CLERK LOST HIS PLACE, WHICH COSTS THIS ARCHIVE THE THING IT MOST WANTED.** Having just written «*vedova di Gioacchi-no **CRISCI***» across a line break, he wrote **CRISCI again** where her father's surname belonged: the act says *«figlia delli furono GIUSEPPE CRISCI»* **of a woman whose own surname is FALCO**. Then he stopped — **her mother's name was never written at all**, and a whole ruled line stands empty before the printed «di anni» resumes.

**The word was magnified four times and set beside «Falco» three lines above it. They are not the same word.** The surname in her filiation is *Crisci*, and it cannot be right.

**WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ANGELO FALCO QUESTION.** The 1811 register gives **ANGELO FALCO**, born about 1747, «*figlio dalli furono **GIUSEPPE FALCO, e ROSA SPOSITO***». Here is a Francesca Falco, born about 1733, daughter of a **GIUSEPPE**. **The forename matches and the surname is demonstrably corrupt**, so the one document that could have made them brother and sister is the one document that cannot be trusted on the point. **They are candidates. They are not joined.** [[quondam-not-evidence]]

events.evidence: Named in THREE acts, all without «fu», so alive throughout: Morti 1840 atto 50 (17 Aug 1840), Morti 1842 atto 2 (2 Jan 1842) and Morti 1843 atto 17 (10 Apr 1843). The 1840 and 1842 acts, both read at 2600–2800px, give FRANCESCA. The correction stands beside the error in the notes rather than replacing it. NO ACT NAMES HER PARENTS, and the archive does not guess at them. She is NOT the older Francesca Falco who married Gioacchino Cioffi and whose son died at seventy-six in 1843 — that woman was born in the 1740s; this one is bearing children in 1840. events.evidence:
**THE ACT BEHIND THE INDEX, OPENED 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THE INDEX WAS RIGHT.** This household rested on one line of the 1832 marriage *tavola*. The act itself:

«*ATTO Della solenne promessa di celebrare IL MATRIMONIO — Num. d'ordine **OTTO**. L'anno mille ottocento **trentadue**, il dì **sei** del mese di **Luglio** … avanti di Noi **FRANCESCO D'AMBROSIO Sindaco** … del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Distretto di **Caserta** … sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO, maggiore**, di anni **ventisei**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi strada CAMELLARA**, figlio di **PASQUALE FALCO** —, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **CHIARA RIVETTI**, di professione **contadina**, domiciliata **ivi***».

**PASQUALE, and the clerk drew a dash where «defunto» would go and left it empty.** Both his parents are alive on 6 July 1832 — and this archive holds **Pasquale Falco's death on 1 October 1834**, twenty-seven months later, which agrees.

**Twenty-six in July 1832 puts his birth about 1806.** The church celebration followed on **16 July**, before a **VERDICCHIO** and a **DI GUIDA** — the bride's own surname among the witnesses.

**AND THIS DEEPENS WORK-LIST ROW 87 INSTEAD OF CLOSING IT.** Act 20 of the 1854 register gives a **FRANCESCO FALCO**, forty-eight — **born about 1806** — *contadino* of **strada Camellara**, son of the **fu RAFFAELE** and the **fu CHIARA RIVETTI**, **widower of a RAFFAELA FALCO**. **Everything matches except the father**, and the two filiations are each internally consistent: Pasquale is alive in 1832 and died in 1834; Raffaele was dead before February 1850. **Neither act is contradicting itself. They are contradicting each other, or they are two men.**

**A SECOND SON OF THIS COUPLE, AND HE IS NEW.** Arienzo, Matrimoni 1854, **act 20**, found on 21 September 2026 in a register nobody here had swept:

«*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **FRANCESCO FALCO maggiore**, di anni **quarantotto**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **strada CAMELLARA**, figlio del **fu RAFFAELE**, di professione **simile**, domiciliato ivi, e della **fu CHIARA RIVETTI**, di professione **filatrice**, domiciliata ivi, **VEDOVO DI RAFFAELA FALCO**; e **CORNELIA SABATINO maggiore**, di anni **cinquanta**, di professione **contadina**, nata in Arienzo … figlia del **fu [MATTEO]**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, e della **fu ALBERTA VERDICCHIO**, di professione **filatrice**, domiciliata ivi, **VEDOVA DI ANTONIO LETTIERI***».

The church celebration followed on **27 August 1854** at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, before **CLEMENTE GIGLIO** and **ALFONSO VERDICCHIO**. *The civil act's own day is not resolved at this filming and is left unread.*

**Forty-eight in August 1854** puts his birth about **1806** — a year before his brother Michele, or the clerks guessed, which they do.

**HE HAD MARRIED A FALCO.** «*VEDOVO DI **RAFFAELA FALCO***». **And this archive holds a «FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO» whose wife is a RAFFAELA FALCO** — the parents of **PASQUALINA FALCO**, dead 1836 — **entered as a child of PASQUALE Falco and Chiara Rivetti, not of Raffaele.**

**THAT IS THE MICHELE-AND-MICHELANGELO PROBLEM ARRIVING A SECOND TIME, AND IT IS NOT RESOLVED HERE.** Either Francescantonio and Francesco are two men — as Michelangelo and Michele turned out to be, one son of Pasquale and one of Raffaele — or one of the two filiations this archive holds is wrong. **Both readings are left standing and the question is raised on the work list.**

**A LIFE OF FORTY-EIGHT HOURS, DOCUMENTED AT BOTH ENDS.** Act **42**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **QUARANTOTTO**, il dì **PRIMO** del mese di **GIUGNO**, ad ore **DODICI** … è comparsa **FELICIA MARTONE, di anni CINQUANTASETTE, di professione LEVATRICE, domiciliata strada SAN FILIPPO NERI**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA MORGILLO, moglie di CRESCENZO FALCO, di anni VENTICINQUE**, domiciliata **strada CAMELLARA**, e da esso **CRESCENZO FALCO, di anni VENTOTTO**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato strada Camellara, **nel giorno PRIMO del mese di GIUGNO … alle ore DIECI, nella casa di esso FALCO** … di dare al neonato il nome di **GENNARO***». Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo the same day**, the notice returned that afternoon.

**He died on 3 June**, act 35 of the death register. **Two days.**

**A MIDWIFE PRESENTED HIM, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS ACT IS FINDABLE.** Where a *levatrice* declares, **both parents are named on the left page**; where the father declares, his name never appears there. *Work-list row 43's earlier sweeps read the declarant line, which on this act says only FELICIA MARTONE.*

Witnesses **GIUSEPPE DIGLIO, fifty, contadino of strada PORTA DI SOPRA**, and **ANTONIO SORGENTE, forty, contadino of the same street** — *the same Antonio Sorgente who witnesses **GIOVANNA ARRICALE's** birth six months later in this very register, where he is given as forty-eight.*

events.event: three ages in nineteen months, and two of the acts name his wife
events.evidence:
**HE STATES HIS AGE, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS ARCHIVE HAS HEARD HIM DO IT.**

Declaring a neighbour's infant on 17 January 1815: «*e **GIUSEPPE FALCO di anni TRENTA**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada **CAMELLARA**, **vicini della defunta***».

**Thirty in January 1815 puts his birth about 1785.** His wife **Antonia di Guida was baptised 31 October 1783** and they married on **4 August 1802** — **so he was about seventeen and she eighteen.** Young, and not impossibly so.

**WHY THIS IS TAKEN AS HIM AND NOT ANOTHER GIUSEPPE FALCO.** The trade and the street both match the act of **26 February 1811**, where the father of the first Raffaele is «*di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA***» on **strada Camellara** — and *massaro di campagna* is not a common description in these registers. **This archive has nevertheless documented three men of this name in three consecutive years**, one of them a *contadino* of the same street married to Gelsomina Vigliotta. **The identification is probable, not proven**, and the age should be treated as his only while that holds. [[ages-are-guessed]]

---

**CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDING.** Within hours of publishing the above, the **1815 BIRTH register** produced **the same man on the same street at the same trade — aged THIRTY-SEVEN**:

«*18 December 1815 … è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO** d'anni **TRENTASETTE**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada **CAMELLARA** … e da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** di anni **ventinove** sua moglie legittima*».

**That act names his wife. It is certainly him.** So **«born about 1785» is withdrawn** — thirty-seven in December 1815 puts his birth about **1778**, and the two statements are **seven years apart in eleven months**.

**AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE ARGUMENT ABOVE IS SIMPLY FALSE.** It was published on the reasoning that «*massaro di campagna* is not a common description in these registers». **The 1815 birth register gives that exact trade to the OTHER Giuseppe Falco too** — «*d'anni **trentaquattro**, di professione **massaro di campagna***», 5 February 1815, husband of **Gelsomina Vigliotta** — who had been a *contadino* in the 1813 register. **The trade separates nothing.**

**THREE STATEMENTS, ONE YEAR, ONE TRADE:** thirty on **17 January** (strada Camellara, death register), thirty-four on **5 February** (strada Costa, Gelsomina Vigliotta's husband), thirty-seven on **18 December** (strada Camellara, Antonia di Guida's husband). **Only the street and the wife's name do any work at all.** [[ages-are-guessed]]

---

**AND THE CORRECTION ABOVE IS ITSELF NOW CORRECTED — IN THE OTHER DIRECTION.** The **1814 birth register**, read on 23 September 2026, holds this man's son's birth act, and it **names Antonia di Guida outright**: «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **TRENTA** … strada **CAMELLARA** … e da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** sua moglie legittima di anni **ventotto***», **26 May 1814**.

**So the series is:**

| when | his age | hers | the act |
|---|---|---|---|
| **26 May 1814** | **30** | **28** | birth of his son Raffaele — *wife named* |
| **17 Jan 1815** | **30** | — | declaring a neighbour's infant |
| **18 Dec 1815** | **37** | **29** | birth of his daughter Maria Antonia — *wife named* |

**Two acts nineteen months apart, both naming his wife, differ by SEVEN YEARS.** And her own ages — twenty-eight, then twenty-nine — move by **one** across the same nineteen months, which is very nearly right.

**WHAT THIS RESTORES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.** The January 1815 declarant at **thirty** is now corroborated by a certain act of the year before, so **identifying him as this man was right after all** — and the reasoning published for it was still wrong, because it rested on a trade that both Giuseppe Falco share. **«Born about 1778» is withdrawn in turn**: two independent acts give thirty in 1814 and 1815, so **about 1784** is the best supported reading, and **«trentasette» in December 1815 is the outlier.**

**Three published estimates of one man's birth year in two days — 1785, 1778, 1784 — off four acts, all read from the image.** *This is what these registers are worth on the point, and the archive would rather show the working than quietly settle on the last one.* [[ages-are-guessed]]

events.evidence:
**«GIUSEPPE FALCO DEL FU MATTEO» — THE EARLIEST CIVIL DOCUMENT THAT NAMES MATTEO FALCO AND CALLS HIM DEAD.**

This archive's head of line died on **18 July 1802**, and until now the earliest *document* naming him was a **notarial consent act of 8 September 1814**, in which his other son **«PASQUALE FALCO del fu MATTEO»** consented to Vincenzo Falco's marriage. **This act is three years and seven months earlier**, and it names a second son the same way.

**Two sons of Matteo Falco, each given the patronymic «del fu Matteo», in two independent instruments.** [[matteo-falco-named-1814]]

**WHAT IT DOES NOT DO.** It does not *discover* the descent — the parish register already has «*Josephum Falco **filium Matthei, e Franciscae Crisci***» at this couple's marriage of 4 August 1802. **What it does is corroborate a parish reading from the civil series**, which is the test this archive applied to Angelo Andrea di Guida and calls decisive. [[di-guida-parents]]

**AND IT GIVES HIS AGE: TWENTY-EIGHT.** Born about **1783** — which settles the argument this archive has been having with itself for two days.

| when | his age | implies | the act |
|---|---|---|---|
| **16 Feb 1811** | **28** | **1783** | birth of Raffaele — *wife named, father named* |
| **26 May 1814** | **30** | **1784** | birth of Raffaele the second — *wife named* |
| **17 Jan 1815** | **30** | **1785** | declaring a neighbour's infant |
| **18 Dec 1815** | **37** | **1778** | birth of Maria Antonia — *wife named* |

**Three of the four cluster on 1783–1785. «Trentasette» in December 1815 is the outlier and can be set aside.** *«About 1784» stands, and it now rests on four acts instead of one.*

events.evidence:
**THE EARLIEST DOCUMENT OF ANY KIND THAT NAMES MATTEO FALCO AND CALLS HIM DEAD.**

«*il Signor **GIUSEPPE FALCO DEL FU MATTEO**, di professione **massaro di campagna**, d'anni **VENT'OTTO** … strada **della CAMELLARA***» — **12 January 1810**.

**THIS ARCHIVE MOVED THAT RECORD TWICE IN ONE DAY AND IS LEAVING BOTH MOVES ON THE PAGE.** Until 23 September 2026 the earliest was a **notarial consent of 8 September 1814**. That morning the **1811** birth register gave the same patronymic on **16 February 1811** and this archive published it as the earliest. **Six hours later the 1810 volume gave it again, thirteen months earlier still.** *The lesson is not about Matteo Falco. It is that «the earliest» is a claim about what has been read, and three of this decade's seven birth volumes had never been opened.* [[wrong-negatives]]

**AND HIS AGE HAS NOT MOVED.** He is **twenty-eight** here in January 1810 and **twenty-eight** again in February 1811 — *thirteen months apart, and the clerk wrote the same number*. With thirty in May 1814 and thirty in January 1815, **four of five statements now fall in 1782–1785**, and «*trentasette*» of December 1815 stands alone. **About 1783 is the reading this archive now carries.** [[ages-are-guessed]]

events.evidence:
Joseph Falco filius Crescentii et Mariae Morgillo, aetatis paucorum dierum

**THE YEAR ON THIS ROW WAS 1818 AND IT IS 1848 — corrected 21 September 2026, and the household is right.** The parish burial reads «*Joseph Falco filius **Crescentii** et **Mariae Morgillo**, aetate paucorum dierum*», and this archive dated it **1818** from the machine transcript of the page.

**A child of CRESCENZO FALCO cannot have died in 1818: his father was born on 11 October 1819.** The date was the only thing making this row impossible, and it is wrong.

**The civil register settles it.** Arienzo *Morti* **1848**, act **34**: «*nel giorno DUE del mese di GIUGNO … è morto … **GIUSEPPE**, nato in Arienzo, **di anni UNO** … **figlio di CRESCENZO FALCO** … **e di MARIA MORGILLO***». And act **35**, the next day, is his brother **GENNARO**, two days old. **The same parish page carries a SECOND entry for the same couple** — «*[N] Falco filius Crescentii e Maria Morgillo*» — which is Gennaro. **The OCR's «Anno D.ni 1818 die vero 2 Ja[nuarii]» is «1848 … 2 Ju[nii]»**, and the page's other entries are dated across the 1840s and 1850s.

**The first weeks of January 1818 and of January 1848 were both read in the civil death registers to test this, and neither holds a Falco infant.** *The «aetate paucorum dierum» belongs to Gennaro; the civil act makes Giuseppe **one year old**, and the parish clerk has run the two brothers' ages together.*

**Both deaths are now held in this household as their own rows, read from the image.** This row is kept, with its date corrected, because it is the parish witness to the same two burials.

**HE DIED THE DAY BEFORE HIS BABY BROTHER.** Act **34**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **QUARANTOTTO**, il dì **DUE** del mese di **GIUGNO**, alle ore **VENTUNO** … sono comparsi **NICOLA COSSI, di anni CINQUANTA**, **CANTINIERE**, domiciliato **in strada CAMELLARA**, e **ANDREA DIGLIO, di anni VENTICINQUE**, contadino, di strada Camellara, i quali han dichiarato, che nel giorno **DUE** del mese di **GIUGNO** … alle ore **SEDICI** è morto nella … casa … **GIUSEPPE**, nato in **ARIENZO**, **di anni UNO** … **figlio di CRESCENZO FALCO** di professione contadino domiciliato ivi, **e di MARIA MORGILLO** domiciliata ivi*».

**A year-old boy dead on 2 June and a two-day-old baby dead on 3 June, brothers, in one house.** The same two neighbours declared both. **The likeliest reading is a confinement that killed the newborn and took the toddler with it**, and the acts say only what they say.

**One year old on 2 June 1848 puts his birth between 3 June 1846 and 2 June 1847.** *His birth act has not been found: the 1846 register has been read at the parents band and holds no Maria Morgillo, and 1847 is not yet finished. **He is named for his paternal grandfather, GIUSEPPE FALCO.***

**VERIFIED AGAINST THE IMAGE, 20 September 2026, work-list row 58 — and the act number was the folio.** This page cited **atto 47**; **47 is the figure stamped in the leaf's margin**, and the act is headed «**Num. d'ordine 91**». THE FIRST MADDALENA DIED ON 31 MAY 1825, aged seven, on strada Camellara; this one was born TWENTY-THREE MONTHS LATER and given her name.

## THE ACT ITSELF IS NOW READ — AND ITS NUMBER IS 57, NOT 52 — 21 September 2026

«*L'anno mille ottocento **VENTISETTE**, il dì **QUATTRO** del mese di **MAGGIO**, ad ore **DODICI** … **Num. d'ordine CINQUANTASETTE** … che la stessa è nata da **ANTONIA DI GUIDO, di anni QUARANTA**, domiciliata **ivi strada CAMELLARA**, e da **GIUSEPPE FALCO marito della stessa, di anni QUARANTACINQUE**, di professione **COLONO**, domiciliato con detta sua moglie, nel giorno **QUATTRO** del mese di **MAGGIO** … **alle ore UNDICI, nella casa d'abitazione di detti conjugi** … di dare alla stessa il nome di **MADDALENA***». Witnesses **GENNARO LETTIERI, thirty-two, contadino, of strada COSTA**, and **RAFFAELE COSSI**. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo** the same day.

**THE ACT NUMBER PUBLISHED HERE WAS WRONG BECAUSE IT CAME FROM THE INDEX.** The tavola's numeral was read as **52**; the act's own heading, in both columns, is **«Num. d'ordine CINQUANTASETTE»**, and the acts either side of it on images 57 and 59 are 56 and 58. **The index is not the act**, and this archive has now been caught by that twice in one week.

**Two things the act adds that the tavola could not.** The birth is on **strada CAMELLARA** — this row carried no street at all — and **GIUSEPPE FALCO is forty-five and a COLONO**, which puts b. c.1782 against the forty he was given in January 1822, **the same year of birth to within a month**. His trade slides massaro → massaro di campagna → colono across this decade without the man changing.

events.evidence:
**A NEW DAUGHTER FOR GENERATION THREE — AND THE ACT THE PARENTS BAND COULD NOT SEE.** Act **84**, «*L'anno mille ottocento **TRENTADUE**, il dì **DIECI** del mese di **OTTOBRE**, ad ore **QUINDICI**, avanti di noi **FRANCESCO D'AMBROSIO Sindaco** … è comparso **VINCENZO FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato ivi, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTASEI**, domiciliata collo stesso, **e da lui dichiarante** … nel giorno **DIECI** del mese di **OTTOBRE** anno corrente, **alle ore DODICI, nella casa sua propria** … di dare alla neonata il nome di **MARIA CARMELA***».

**«DA LUI DICHIARANTE» IS WHY SHE WAS MISSING.** The left page of the opening — the band this archive reads for parents — **never writes the father's name in this act**. It says *and by him, the declarant, of the age above, of the trade above, living as above*. **A sweep of that band sees ANDREANA CRISCI and no Falco at all.** This is the exact failure work-list row 85 was raised to describe, and it had cost this line a child.

**Both stated ages are exactly right, which is rare here.** He is **forty** and his baptism is **1 February 1792**; she is **thirty-six** and hers is **30 November 1796**. This archive has published, repeatedly, that the Arienzo clerks guessed ages by as much as five years — the same office made him thirty-two in 1826 and thirty-six in 1828. **In this one act both parents are right to the year.**

**She fills the 1830–1834 gap.** The children run Giuseppe Nunzio (1824), Angelandrea (1826), Sara (1828), Pasquale (1830, dead 1833) — **Maria Carmela (1832)** — Pasquale the second (1834, dead the same year).

**SHE IS NOT THE OTHER MARIA CARMELA FALCO OF 1832.** That one was born **15 July 1832** on the same street to **Francescantonio Falco and Maria Raffaela Falco**, and is already held here. **Two girls of one name, one surname and one street, twelve weeks apart** — this town keeps proving that a name identifies nobody.

Witnesses **PIETRO MAURO, twenty-three, *sartore*, regnicolo, of strada Porta di Sopra**, and **FILIPPO GIGLIO, twenty-six**. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo di Arienzo** on **10 October**, the notamento returned the same day. **No marginal annotation**: the act carries no later marriage, and what became of her is open.

L'anno mille ottocento cinquanta**sette**, il dì **ventisei** di **Novembre** … avanti di Noi **CARLO CARFORA Sindaco** … di **Arienzo** … comparsi nella Casa Comunale **NICOLA DI LUCIA**, di anni **ventotto**, nato in **SAN FELICE**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **in San Felice**, figlio di **GIOVANNI DI LUCIA**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **VINCENZA ZIMBARDO**, domiciliata ivi; e **MARIA CARMELA FALCO**, di anni **venticinque**, nata in **Arienzo**, domiciliata in Arienzo, figlia di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***».

**Twenty-five in November 1857 is a woman born in 1832, and her birth act is 10 October 1832.**

**TWO OF THIS HOUSEHOLD'S CHILDREN MARRIED DI LUCIA OF SAN FELICE.** **STANISLAO FALCO** married **FILOMENA DI LUCIA** at Arienzo on **19 September 1861**, four years later. *Filomena's father is **LUIGI** di Lucia and Nicola's is **GIOVANNI**; whether the two houses are one is not established and is not claimed.* **Di Lucia is a San Felice surname this archive meets repeatedly.**

**THE FIRST CHILD OF A HOUSEHOLD THAT HAD NONE — AND HER OWN MARRIAGE COMES WITH HER.** Act **111**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **QUARANTACINQUE**, il dì **VENTIDUE** del mese di **NOVEMBRE**, ad ore **SEDICI** … è comparso **CRESCENZO FALCO, di anni VENTICINQUE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **MARIA MORGILLO sua moglie legittima, di anni VENTITRE**, domiciliata collo stesso, **e da lui dichiarante** … **nel giorno VENTUNO del mese di NOVEMBRE anno corrente, alle ore DUE, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione** … di dare alla neonata il nome di **MARIA FELICE***».

**Born 21 November 1845 at two in the morning; declared the next day; baptised at Sant'Andrea Apostolo on the 23rd**, the parish notice returned the same day and copied into the INDICAZIONE column — «*il Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato a **MARIA FELICIA FALCO***».

**HER PARENTS MARRIED ON 2 FEBRUARY 1845. She was born nine months and nineteen days later.**

## AND THE MARGIN CARRIES HER WEDDING, OUT OF THE LOST YEARS

«*A **3 Febbrajo 1873** l'Uff.e dello Stato Civ.e d'**ARIENZO** sposò **MARIA FELICE FALCO** con **PASQUALE QUOTOLO** — Caserta **18 Giugno 1884***». **Arienzo's civil registers for 1866–1890 are gone**, so this margin is the only record of that marriage this archive can reach — the same shape as Pasqua Falco's of 1880, found in the margin of her own 1823 birth act.

Witnesses **CLEMENTE PORRINO, contadino of strada CAMELLARA**, and **CLEMENTE CRISPI, thirty-four, contadino of strada CRISPI**, «*testimonj … da esso **CRESCENZO FALCO** prodotti*».

**Found by re-sweeping the 1845 register at the PARENTS band for work-list row 43.** *The row's earlier pass swept images **118–135** on the declarant line; **the act is at 116–117**, just outside the window.*

Born 20 July 1832, she would be one year and ten months old at that death, which fits. **Either the 1834 act belongs to MICHELANGELO's daughter and the household assignment is wrong, or there were two Maria Rosa Falco of two men whose names and whose wives' names both nearly coincide.** The birth act says MICHELANGELO, in full, twice. **Nothing is moved on the strength of it**: the 1834 death act has not been re-read, and that is the test. events.evidence:
«*è morta nella sua propria casa **MARIA ROSA FALCO, di mesi VENTIDUE**, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, domiciliata ivi, figlia di **MICHELE FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — **IMAGE 24 RIGHT**, 30 May 1834.

**SHE WAS PUBLISHED HERE AT «d'anni SEDICI» — SIXTEEN YEARS — AND SHE WAS TWENTY-TWO MONTHS.** The act reads «*di **mesi** ventidue*», magnified. **A sixteen-year-old contadina and an infant of not quite two are not the same kind of person**: everything anyone might infer from the first — a birth about 1818, a working girl, a daughter of marriageable age — is wrong. She was born about **July 1832**.

**Her mother was not recorded either.** **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** is named in the act. **And she raises a question this archive should not settle by guessing**: the Michele Falco of Arienzo who buries a two-year-old son in 1842 is married to an **ANTONIA MIGLIORE**. Same forename, same town, same trade, eight years apart. **Either one of the two surnames is misread, or there are two Michele Falco each married to an Antonia.** Neither is asserted.

**The citation also pointed at image 23 right**, which is Carmina Zimbardo, fourteen days old, daughter of Domenico Zimbardo and Orsola Porrino.

**THIS ROW STOOD IN A HOUSEHOLD OF ITS OWN, «Michele Falco (strada Camellara)», UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** The act names her mother — **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** — and that name joins her to a household this archive already had: the **MICHELE FALCO of strada Camellara** who buried Salvatore in 1836 and Matteo in 1842 and married again in 1850 as «*vedovo di ANTONIA VIGLIOTI*». **The stub was not a family. It was a line nobody had read.**

**A NEW CHILD, AND A THIRD MOTHER FOR MICHELANGELO FALCO — RECORDED, NOT JOINED.** Act **77**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **TRENTOTTO**, il dì **QUATTRO** del mese di **SETTEMBRE** … è comparso **MICHELANGELO FALCO, di anni TRENTAQUATTRO, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in strada SANT'ANDREA**, quale ci ha presentato un **MASCHIO** … che lo stesso è nato da **MARIA MIGLIORE sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTACINQUE**, domiciliata collo stesso, **e da lui dichiarante** … nel giorno **QUATTRO** del mese di **SETTEMBRE**, **alle ore VENTI, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione** … di dare al neonato il nome di **MARINO, ALESSANDRO***».

Witnesses **BENEDETTO RIVETTI, forty, contadino, regnicolo, of strada COSTA**, and **STEFANO LETTIERI, thirty-three, contadino, regnicolo, of strada COSTA**. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo** on 4 September.

**THIS ARCHIVE NOW HOLDS A MICHELANGELO FALCO WITH THREE DIFFERENT WIVES IN SEVEN YEARS**, and this act is the third: **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** (1831, 1832, strada Camellara), **RAFFAELA FALCO** (1834, strada Camellara) and now **MARIA MIGLIORE** (1838, **strada SANT'ANDREA**). The archive had already published the first two as an open question — «*either there are two Michelangelo Falco at Arienzo, or one of the two mothers is misread*». **A third mother, on a different street, makes the misreading answer much harder to hold.** It is set down here as its own household **and joined to nothing**, because deciding which Michelangelo this is would be a claim and no document makes it.

*Not to be confused with the **MARIA MIGLIORE** who died at Arienzo on 27 February 1817, wife of **MATTEO CIMMINO** and daughter of the late Fabio Migliore and Giovanna Laudato. The name is dense in this town.*
