line.note:
Named as the father in the baptisms of at least five children at Arienzo between 1767 and 1786 — six, counting the Gioacchino of 1774 who died at three — and again in his son Giuseppe's marriage record. He appears as a witness at an Arienzo marriage in 1759, so he was an adult by then. He replaces the Agostino Falcone previously carried at the head of this line. **A third child, found in 1822, names them again — and earliest of all.** On 17 October 1822 **ANGELA FALCO**, fifty-one, widow of Crescenzo Rivetti, died on strada Capodiconca, «figlia di MATTEO FALCO Defunto, di professione Contadino, e di FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta». Born about 1771. The founding couple is now named from the death acts of THREE separate children — Angela's in 1822, Rosa's in 1830 and Pasquale's in 1834 — and Angela's is the earliest. It also resolves an act found earlier in this research: when her husband Crescenzo Rivetti died in December 1816, **Gioacchino Falco** and **Giuseppe Falco** declared it as «parenti del defunto». They were his wife's brothers — which makes **Gioacchino Falco a strong candidate for a fifth child of Matteo and Francesca**, though no record yet names his parents.

**And now he is named in his own lifetime's paperwork.** The marriage dossier of his grandson Vincenzo, found in the 1814 processetti in September 2026, contains a notarial act of **8 September 1814** before Felice Morgillo in which «li conjugi **PASQUALE FALCO del fu MATTEO**, e **CHIARA RIVETTI del fu NICOLA**» consent to their son's marriage. This is **the earliest document that names Matteo Falco, and the earliest that proves him dead** — eight years earlier than Angela's act of 1822, and from a notary's instrument rather than a register clerk's recollection. **The bracket on his death closes from [1786, Oct 1822] to [1786, 8 Sep 1814].**

**And the bracket narrows again, from a negative.** The Arienzo death INDEXES for 1809–1814 — one to five images a year, against fifty for a register — have been read, and **no Matteo Falco of this generation is in them**. He is documented dead by 8 September 1814; if he had died after civil registration began in 1809 he should appear, and he does not. **So he very probably died before 1809, which puts his death in the PARISH register and nowhere else.** 

**A warning for anyone who searches this.** A **MATTEO FALCO did die at Arienzo, on 28 August 1809** — and he is **not this one**. The index names his parents «Giuseppe, ed Antonia di [Guida]» **without «fu»**, so they were living, and the same couple bury sons in 1811 and 1815. Ours was born about 1740 and had children baptised from 1767.

**GIOACCHINO IS CONFIRMED — a record names his parents at last.** The alphabetical index bound at the front of the Arienzo death register for **1851** reads: «**7. FALCO GIOACCHINO** | Arienzo | **CONTADINO** | **FALCO MATTEO, e CRISCI FRANCESCA** | **14 Febrajo**». Read at native resolution. 

**And the act itself, found the same day, says far more than the index.** «…è morto nella sua propria casa **GIOACCHINO FALCO** marito di **VITTORIA CIMMINO**, nato in **Arienzo**, di anni **SETTANTASEI**, di professione ***COLONO***, domiciliato ivi, figlio di **MATTEO FALCO defunto** … e di **FRANCESCA CRISCI defunta**.» Seventy-six in February 1851 puts his birth about **1775** — squarely among his siblings, whose baptisms run 1767 to 1786 — and it confirms the family tree's date exactly. His trade is ***colono***, the same rank the registers give Giuseppe, Vincenzo and Matteo. His wife was **VITTORIA CIMMINO**. And he was declared by **Mariantonio Crisci**, a *calzolajo*, and **Gaspare d'Onofrio**, a *sartore* — **both of strada Camellara**, so he died on the family's own street. 

**So the founding couple's documented children are now SIX**: Angela (d. 1822), Rosa (d. 1830), Pasquale (d. 1834), Giuseppe, **GIOACCHINO (d. 14 February 1851)** — and **a FIRST GIOACCHINO, baptised 25 November 1774 and buried on 11 December 1777**, whose entry carries a drawn cross and the marginal «obiit die 11 Decembris 1777». The Gioacchino this line follows was baptised fourteen months after that burial and **carries his dead brother's name** — the second time this household has been caught doing it, after Giovanna. A child who died in 1777 never reached the civil registers at all; only the parish books hold him. The archive had suspected him since 1816, when he and Giuseppe Falco declared the death of Crescenzo Rivetti as «parenti del defunto» — Crescenzo being the husband of their sister Angela. **That reasoning is now vindicated by a document rather than resting on an inference.** 

**And note how it was found**: not by reading a register act by act, but by reading an index four images long. The question had been open for years.

**And that is now settled.** All six index volumes for 1809–1814 have been read **page for page** — 138, 80, 90, 78 and 86 deaths in the years whose totals the indexes state. **No Falco of the founder's generation dies at Arienzo in any of them.** Taken with the marriage indexes, which also begin in 1809, **both of Matteo Falco's vital events lie outside the civil series entirely**. His marriage of about 1760–66 and his death are in the parish books of Sant'Andrea or nowhere, and that is now the only front on which he can be reached.

**And the 1809 namesake is probably his own grandson.** The Matteo Falco who died at Arienzo on 28 August 1809 — «di [anni struck, **mesi** written over] **quindici**» — was a son of **Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida of strada Camellara**. Two birth acts settle that there were **two Giuseppe Falco** at Arienzo, of the same name and the same stated age, distinguished by street and wife: one on **strada Costa** with **Gelsomina Vigliotta**, one on **strada Camellara** with **Antonia di Guida**. **The Camellara Giuseppe is «GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO»** — this line's own. 

So the infant was **Matteo Falco's grandson, given his grandfather's name, and buried while the grandfather was still alive**. **And it is now PROVED, not probable.** **The parish marriage act of 4 AUGUST 1802**, read from the image itself, reads «non dum uxoratos **JOSEPHUM FALCO filium MATTHEI, e FRANCISCAE CRISCI** et **ANTONIAM DI GUIDA filiam JOSEPHI, et MAGDALENAE RIVETTA**» — Giuseppe of strada Camellara is documented as Matteo's son in the very act that marries him to Antonia. **The infant is the founder's grandson.** He is still not the founder, and the warning above stands.

**The parish books have now been opened, and they carry what the civil registers cannot.** The same leaf holds **ROSA FALCO's marriage, of 12 JULY 1802 — three weeks earlier, not the same day** — «**Carolum Antonium Morgillo** filium quondam Caroli Antonii, et Emiliae … e **ROSA FALCO filiam MATTHEI, e FRANCISCAE CRISCI**» — which the archive did not have, and which disentangles two men named Carlantonio Morgillo, father and son. It also gives **Antonia di Guida's own parents, GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA and MAGDALENA RIVETTA**, a generation never held here — and **Rivetta is a name this archive already carries**: generation three's wife is **Chiara Rivetti**. Whether the two are the same family is untested and is recorded here as a lead, not a claim. Both couples were married by **Don Luca Verdicchio, *Missionarius***, under the licence of the archpriest **Giacinto Morgillo**, who signs each act. 

**And GIOACCHINO's baptism: 2 February 1779**, «qui nominatus est JOACHIM», midwife **Cecilia Martone** — which corrects the «about 1775» this archive derived from his death act's stated age of seventy-six. He was **seventy-two**. 

***THE IMAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ.*** Film 007786827, image 366; the leaf opens the section headed «A Mense Aprilis». Both acts, both sets of parents, both dates and the celebrant are read from the handwriting, not from the machine transcription — which had rendered the year as «1902» and the bride's mother as «Pivera». What remains unread is **Emilia's surname**, the Morgillo groom's mother: the scan is 2,258 pixels across the whole leaf, and that one word does not survive the magnification. 

**AND A GRANDSON IN ORDERS.** Arienzo, Morti 1849, **atto 66**: «…è morto nella sua propria casa **DON GIOVANNI FALCO**, nato in Arienzo, **di anni VENTICINQUE**, di professione **DIACONO** … **figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO** di professione **COLONO** … **e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA**» — **26 November 1849, at ten at night**. 

**There has never been a churchman in this line before.** Every Falco the archive has found across four generations is a *bracciale*, a *contadino* or a *colono*, and most of the men who declared their deaths could not write their own names. Matteo's grandson was a **deacon**, and was buried with *Don* before his name. He was born about **1824** and died at **twenty-five**. 

The act carries two more facts. **GIUSEPPE FALCO WAS STILL ALIVE** in November 1849 — no «fu», no «defunto» — and is written down as a **colono**, at about seventy. And both declarants, **Gennaro and Francesco Cioffi**, lived **on strada CAMELLARA**. 

*The index calls him* suddiacono; *the act calls him* diacono. *Both are recorded; the archive does not know which moment each describes.* 

**AND A GRANDDAUGHTER, AND THE FOUNDER'S SON ALIVE AT SEVENTY-FOUR.** Arienzo, Morti 1854, **atto 34**: «…è morta nella sua propria casa **RAFFAELA FALCO, MOGLIE DI FRANCESCO FALCO**, nata in Arienzo, di anni **TRENTAQUATTRO**, di professione contadina, domiciliata **STRADA CAMELLARA**, **figlia di GIUSEPPE FALCO** di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, **e di ANTONIA GUIDA**» — **20 April 1854**. 

She is a child of Giuseppe and Antonia this archive did not have, born about **1820**. Their documented children are now **four**: the infant Matteo (1809), the infant Raffaele (a parish burial of 26 February, year unread), **Don Giovanni the deacon** (1849) and **Raffaela**. 

**And «figlia DI Giuseppe Falco» — no «fu».** Giuseppe Falco was **alive in April 1854**, at about **seventy-four**: five years later than the previous latest sighting. 

**Her husband was a FALCO.** And the household did not survive the next summer. Arienzo, Morti 1855: «…è morto nella sua propria casa **GIOVANNI FALCO**, nato in Arienzo, **di anni TRE** … domiciliato **STRADA CAMELLARA**, **figlio di FRANCESCO** … **e della FU RAFFAELA FALCO**» — **29 June 1855**. And the parish register gives the other son: «Anno Domini **1855**, die vero **14 Augusti**, obiit **CLEMENS FALCO filius FRANCISCI, et RAPHAELAE FALCO**, aetatis suae annorum **QUINQUE**» — and the civil act dates that death **14 August 1853**, not 1855. **Four deaths in one house on strada Camellara in five years**: Antonio at two in 1850, Clemente at five in 1853, Raffaela at thirty-four in 1854, Giovanni at three in 1855. 

**FRANCESCO FALCO LOST HIS WIFE IN APRIL 1854 AND BOTH KNOWN SONS IN THE SUMMER OF 1855**, in the house on strada Camellara. **1855 was a cholera year in the Kingdom** — Arienzo registered **111 deaths against sixty-five in 1844** — but the acts give no cause and none is claimed here. A civil act and a parish entry, found by different methods on different days, joining into one family. 

*Falco marrying Falco is not rare at Arienzo: four such couples appear in the death indexes of 1850, 1853 and 1854 alone. Whether that means cousins or two unrelated Falco stocks in one town, this archive does not know.* 

**THE FOUNDER'S SON'S FAMILY, RECONSTRUCTED — SEVEN CHILDREN.** Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida married on 4 August 1802. This archive held two of their children this morning; the Arienzo parish baptisms give five more. 

**GIOVANNA** bapt. 13 Aug 1805 · **MATTEO** b. c. May 1808, d. 28 Aug 1809 · **RAFFAELE** bapt. 16 Feb 1811 and **dead on the 26th**, ten days old · **FRANCESCA MARIA LUCIA** bapt. 27 Oct 1812 · **MADDALENA** bapt. 7 Jun 1818 · **RAFFAELA** b. c.1820, d. 20 Apr 1854 · **GIOVANNI** bapt. April 1825 — **Don Giovanni the deacon**, d. 26 Nov 1849. **Twenty years of childbearing.** 

It settles the infant Raffaele, whose parish burial of «26 February» carried **no year**: the baptism ten days earlier is on the same leaf, with the marginal «**Raphael Falco obiit die 26 Februarii 1811**». **And it makes DON GIOVANNI twenty-four, not the twenty-five his death act states** — the fifth stated age this week overturned by a baptism. 

*Five of the seven are FamilySearch machine transcription and the images have not been read; the days in particular are unverified. The two civil records are read from the images.* 

---

## **HE DIED ON 18 JULY 1802 — and the argument that put him alive in August is refuted** 

The marriage act of his son **GIOACCHINO**, read from the image: «Anno Domini Millesimo Septingentesimo **NONAGESIMO SEXTO 1796**, die vero **decima sexta 16 Maii** … **PAROCHUS D. ANGELUS SCARPATI** … in Matrimonium conjunxit non dum uxoratos **JOACHIM FALCO FILIUM MATTHEI, ET FRANCISCAE CRISCI; et VICTORIAM CIMMINO FILIAM MATTHEI, ET MARIAE MIGLIORE**» — at the collegiate church of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, by decree of the episcopal curia of **Sant'Agata de' Goti**. 

**«FILIUM MATTHEI» — no «quondam», before either name.** And **this scribe uses «quondam»**: on the 1802 leaf he writes «Carolum Antonium Morgillo filium **quondam** Caroli Antonii, et Emiliae» — father dead, mother living, the word placed exactly where it belongs. He omits it for Matteo and Francesca in **1796**, and omits it again for them in **August 1802**. 

**On that reasoning this archive published, four hours before the act was found, that «MATTEO FALCO AND FRANCESCA CRISCI WERE BOTH ALIVE ON 4 AUGUST 1802» and that he must have died between then and 1809.** 

> **HE HAD BEEN DEAD FOR SEVENTEEN DAYS.** 

The Arienzo parish death register: «**Anno Domini Millesimo octingentesimo secundo 1802, die vero decimo octavo 18 Julii, MATTHAEUS FALCO VIR FRANCISCAE CRISCI, aetatis suae annorum 55 circiter**, omnibus Sacramentis munitus … obiit, et **in Archip[resbyter]ali Coemeterio ejus cadaver humatum est**. Hyacinthus Archip[resbyte]r Morgillo» — **read from the image**, margin and cross and all. 

**AND IT DATES HIS BIRTH.** «Annorum 55 circiter» puts it about **1747**, where this archive has carried «about 1740» since the beginning on no evidence but the date of his first known child. **Fifty-five fits everything**: he fathered children from 1767 to 1786, from twenty to thirty-nine, and married by 1766 at about nineteen. 

**The scribe did not write «quondam» for a man who was dead.** The argument was careful, it carried its warrant, it was labelled evidence rather than proof — **and it was wrong at both ends.** That is the finding, not a footnote to it. 

**And it dates the summer of 1802 exactly**: his daughter **ROSA married on 12 July**, six days before he died; **he died on 18 July**; his son **GIUSEPPE married on 4 August, seventeen days after burying him**. Both marriages are on one leaf, and this archive read that leaf this morning believing he was alive at both. 

*The figure is written «55»; in this hand the two glyphs are identical and the second could be an 8. **About fifty-five, born about 1744–1747**, is what this archive will say.* 

**And Vittoria Cimmino's parents are named: MATTEO CIMMINO and MARIA MIGLIORE** — a generation this archive did not have. Both the groom's father and the bride's father were called Matteo. 

---

## **AND SHE IS FOUND TOO — FRANCESCA CRISCI, 31 DECEMBER 1805** 

«**Anno D[omi]ni 1805, die vero 31 Decembris, FRANCISCA CRISCI VIDUA MAT‑THEI FALCO, aetatis suae annorum 60 circiter**, omnibus Sacramentis munita … obiit, et **in Sodalitate S. Mariae Gratiarum** ejus cadaver humatum est. Hyacinthus Archip[resbyte]r Morgillo» — **read from the image**. The surname breaks across the line, «Vidua **Mat**- / **thei** Falco», which is why the machine rendered it «Manel». 

> **THE FOUNDING COUPLE IS CLOSED AT BOTH ENDS.** He died **18 July 1802**, about **fifty-five**, buried in the **archpriest's cemetery**. She died **31 December 1805**, about **sixty**, buried in the **confraternity of Santa Maria delle Grazie**. Born about **1747** and about **1745**. She was three and a half years a widow. 

**And every number now fits.** She bore a child in January 1786 at about **forty-one**; she was about **two years older** than her husband; their children run from 1767 to 1786, from about twenty-two to about forty-one. **Nothing about this couple is strange any more** — and that is the confirmation, because the readings that made them strange were the wrong readings.

**THE CIVIL ACT, READ 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND IT DISAGREES WITH THE PARISH BY FOURTEEN MONTHS.** This death was held from the parish alone: «*Matthaeus Falco filius Josephi e Antoniae di Guida coniugum*», a machine transcription with no age. **The civil act has now been read**, from a volume this archive had never opened:

«*NUM. **38**. Oggi, che sono li **ventotto** del mese di **Agosto** dell'anno mille ottocento **nove** sono comparsi avanti il sottoscritto Sindaco di questa Università i Signori **AGOSTINO CIOFFI**, d'anni **quarantuno**, di professione **bracciale** … abitante nella strada di **SANTO ANDREA**, e **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, d'anni **trentotto**, di professione bracciale … ed hanno dichiarato, che oggi suddetto giorno ad ore **cinque** è morto **MATTEO FALCO**, di **MESI QUATTORDICI**, di professione contadino … abitante nella strada di **SANTO ANDREA**, **figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO, ed ANTONIA DI GUIDA**, di professione **MASSARI**, domiciliati nella stessa comune, e strada*».

**FOURTEEN MONTHS PUTS HIS BIRTH ABOUT JUNE 1808. The parish baptised a MATTHEUS of this couple on 9 APRIL 1807**, which would make him **twenty-eight** months. **The two cannot both be right about one child.**

*Either the civil clerk guessed the age of an infant — which these clerks do constantly — or the 1807 Mattheus and the 1809 Matteo are two children, and this household lost two sons of that name before giving it a third time in the 1810s.* **This archive already holds one necronym here: MADDALENA, given again in 1827 after the first died in 1825.** **Nothing is decided; both records stand.**

**AND THE FAMILY IS ON STRADA SANT'ANDREA IN 1809**, where every later act — from February 1811 onward — puts them on **strada CAMELLARA**. **Both parents are «MASSARI»**, which is the word the 1811 act uses too and no act after it does.

*The declarants are **AGOSTINO** and **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, both bracciali of strada Sant'Andrea — the surname that married into this family twice.*

By **16 March 1834** he is the father of a second Anna **by RAFFAELA FALCO**. **So Antonia Vigliotti died between May 1831 and March 1834 and he married again** — and this household is his second marriage. **The Antonia Vigliotta who lived until before 1850 is a different woman, married to a different man.**

events.evidence:
THE ACT THAT JOINS TWO HOUSEHOLDS THIS ARCHIVE KEPT APART. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **MICHELE FALCO maggiore, di anni QUARANTATRE, nato in ARIENZO, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione filatrice … **VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI** … e **GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO MAGGIORE, di anni TRENOVE**, di professione contadina*». **HER AGE IS THIRTY-NINE, NOT NINETEEN** — re-read at the leaf's full 3,200 pixels on 20 September 2026. The numeral's initial is a tall ascender crossed by a diagonal, a **t**; this hand's **d**, in «CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA» four lines above it in the same pen, is a small closed bowl. «Trenove» is the clerk's contraction of *trentanove*. **And the act says so twice**: she is «MAGGIORE», of age, and no consent of her mother is taken — a nineteen-year-old would have been «MINORE», as Andreana Crisci is in 1814. So she was born about **1811**, not about 1831. **«Michele Falco & Antonia Vigliotta» and «Michele Falco & Maria Giovanna d'Ambrogio» are ONE MAN AND TWO MARRIAGES.** The d'Ambrogio household was known only by a daughter **Antonia born 19 November 1850** — nine months after this wedding.

**Verified against the image, work-list row 58 — act 6, and every word holds.** «*L'anno mille ottocento **cinquanta**, il dì **dodici** del mese di **Febrajo**, alle ore **sedici**, avanti di Noi **ARCANGELO DE FUSCO Sindaco***». **The bride's parents had never been recorded here**: **DOMENICO D'AMBROGIO defunto**, contadino, and **CARMINA MANNA**, **filatrice**, and she is of **strada Sant'Andrea**. The church celebration followed the same day at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, before **ALFONSO VERDICCHIO** and a **CLEMENTE MOR[GILLO]**.

**THE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, 20 September 2026, AND THEY ARE TWO MEN.** The 1828 marriage index was read from the image at last: «*10. **FALCO MICHELANGELO** | Arienzo | **FALCO PASQUALE, e RIVETTI CHIARA*** … ***VIGLIOTTI ANTONIA** | ivi | **VIGLIOTTI FRANCESCO, e REPETELLI VITTORIA*** … **Xbre 1828**». And the 1850 act's father was magnified for the first time: «*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO Defunto***», a capital **R**.

**MICHELANGELO FALCO is a son of PASQUALE. MICHELE FALCO is a son of RAFFAELE.** Two fathers, two men — **and both of them married a woman called ANTONIA VIGLIOTTI.** That coincidence is now documented from two marriage records rather than guessed at, and it is what had the two households tangled together.

events.evidence:
**A SECOND GIUSEPPE FALCO ON STRADA CAMELLARA, WITH A DIFFERENT WIFE, IN THE SAME REGISTER AS THE FIRST.**

«*è morto **NICOLA FALCO** — d'anni **DUE** — di professione **contadino** — domiciliante in detta Università, ed abitante nella strada **della CAMELLARA**, **figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO, ed GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA**, di professione **contadini**, domiciliati nella stessa Università, e Strada*». *The clerk writes her name «Felsomina»; Gelsomina is the name.*

**THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAD A GIUSEPPE FALCO IN THIS VOLUME.** Act 38 of 28 August 1809 buries **MATTEO FALCO, fourteen months**, «*figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO, ed ANTONIA DI GUIDA, di professione **MASSARI***», on **strada SANT'ANDREA**.

**THE TWO ACTS ARE IN ONE YEAR'S REGISTER AND THEY DISAGREE ON EVERYTHING BUT THE NAME** — different wife, different street, different trade. *Massari* held land; *contadini* worked it. **There were two Giuseppe Falco at Arienzo in 1809 and this register proves it in its own pages.** [[two-falco-families-arienzo]]

**IT WAS IN THE HALF NOBODY READ.** This volume puts two acts on every image — odd numbers on the left page, even on the right — and when this archive swept it on 21 September 2026 it read only the right pages. **The Matteo Falco act is act 38 and was found. Nicola Falco is on a left page and was not.** The volume was published as read in full; **it was half read**.

Two years old in 1809, so born about **1807**.

events.evidence:
A NEW DAUGHTER for the OTHER Giuseppe Falco, found by reading the 1823 birth register end to end. «…nata da GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTOTTO … nel giorno TRENTA del mese di MARZO … alle ore DIECI … il nome di PASQUA». Her mother's age agrees with this household's other act to within a year — thirty-two in 1816, thirty-eight in 1823. THE MARGIN RECORDS HER MARRIAGE: «A 30 Dic. 1880 l'uff. dello stato civile d'Arienzo … PASQUA FALCO con PASQUALE CARFORA», certified Caserta 27 Aug 1881. SHE IS NOT JOINED TO GIOVANNA ARRICALE'S MOTHER — but she is the ONLY Pasqua born at Arienzo in the whole window Giovanna's act implies: 1822 and 1823 were both read end to end, 239 acts, and 1822 holds no Pasqua at all. Joining them would marry the Camellara Falco to the strada Costa Falco on a forename and an age the clerks are known to have guessed by up to five years. See the corrections page

**Verified against the image, work-list row 58, and the act has a number: ATTO 38, beginning on IMAGE 40 RIGHT and continuing on 41 LEFT.** «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **QUARANTADUE**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in questo Comune **strada Camellara**, quale ci ha presentato una **Femina** … nata da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA** sua moglie legittima, di anni **trentotto** … il nome di **PASQUA***», before **VINCENZO MORGILLO Sindaco**, with **GIUSEPPE COSSI, calzolajo** of strada Camellara as witness. **And the margin is there and reads as published.**

**One more point for the age series**: Giuseppe Falco is **forty-two and a massaro di campagna in March 1823** — against forty-eight and massaro in March 1824, forty and massaro on 2 April 1825, forty-five and contadino four days later, forty-six in 1826 and fifty-six and *possidente* in 1828.

**THE PLACE FIELD SAID *strada COSTA* UNTIL 21 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THE ACT SAYS *strada CAMELLARA*** — as the quotation two paragraphs above it always did. The street was carried forward from this household's 1816 act and never corrected when the 1823 act was read. **It is the one row in the household where the field and its own evidence disagreed**, and it mattered, because this is the very act on which the archive published that *strada Camellara stopped telling the two Giuseppe Falco apart*. Found by re-reading the act at the declarant band, work-list row 85.

SHE MARRIED, AND THE ARCHIVE'S REFUSAL TO JOIN HER TO ANOTHER WOMAN IS VINDICATED. «Atto di solenne promessa di matrimonio, Num. d'ordine 29», 9 SETTEMBRE 1856: «…sono comparsi ANGELO MAJONE … figlio di FRANCESCO MAJONE DEFUNTO … e di MARTA DIGLIO DEFUNTA … e PASQUA FALCO, di anni TRENTATRE, nata in ARIENZO, domiciliata in Arienzo, figlia di GIUSEPPE FALCO di professione CONTADINO domiciliato in Arienzo, e di GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA DEFUNTA». Thirty-three in September 1856 gives b. c.1823, and her birth act of 30 March 1823 is already held. THE MARGIN CERTIFIES THE CHURCH on the thirteenth of September. SHE IS NOT CALLED A WIDOW — and that is the whole point

**Verified from the image, work-list row 58.** «*di anni **TRENTATRE**, nata in ARIENZO*» — **thirty-three in September 1856 gives about 1823, and her birth act is 30 March 1823.** Exact.

**AND HER FATHER IS NOT MARKED DEAD.** «*figlia di **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in Arienzo*» — no «defunto», in an act that writes it three times over for the groom's parents and for her own mother. **So Giuseppe Falco was living on 9 September 1856**, twenty-one months later than this archive's previous latest sighting of him, his own remarriage of 13 December 1854.

events.evidence: «sono comparsi PASQUALE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque, di professione COLONO, regnicolo, domiciliato in questo comune strada Camellara, ZIO DEL DEFUNTO, e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, ZIO DEL DEFUNTO» — atto 8. THE WORD IS «ZIO», NOT «VICINO», AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG. Re-read 16 Sep 2026 at full magnification: the word before «del defunto» is three letters, written twice, and it is not the six-letter «vicino» the same clerk writes on the 1823 and 1825 acts of this same household — those two acts are the control, and they are in this file to be checked against. So the register states in 1824 that the dead child's mother MARIA FALCO is kin to these two men, four years before the 1828 act on which this archive had rested that conclusion. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE. Read strictly, «zio del defunto» makes Maria Falco a SISTER of Pasquale (bapt. 24 October 1767) and of Giuseppe — and therefore a daughter of MATTEO FALCO and FRANCESCA CRISCI. Her own stated age forbids it: twenty-five in June 1824, born about 1799, when Francesca Crisci was bearing children by 1767. Either that age is one of this register's inventions — and this archive holds the same clerk making Giuseppe Falco forty and forty-five four days apart — or «zio» is doing the loose collateral work that «parente» does in 1828. THE WORD IS RECORDED AND THE PEDIGREE IS REFUSED. THE ONLY RECORD IN WHICH PASQUALE FALCO ACTS FOR HIMSELF, and the only document in this archive written in his own hand: the act closes «segnato da noi e da uno de' dichiaranti, avendo l'altro cioè GIUSEPPE FALCO dichiarato di non sapere scrivere per non averlo mai imparato», and beneath it, in a slow upright hand quite unlike the clerk's, stands the signature «PASCALE FALCO» — the Neapolitan form, without the qu, the way he said his own name. His brother could not sign. He is fifty-five here, one year out against his baptism of 24 October 1767 — ordinary — and his trade is COLONO, a tenant farmer, where his death act of 1834 calls him contadino.

line.name: Pasquale (Pascuale) Falco
line.note:
Baptised in the Collegiate Church of Sant'Andrea at Arienzo on 24 October 1767 — the record names his father Matteo and his mother Francesca Crisci. He married Chiara Rivetti and their children were baptised in the same church from 1789 to 1802. He died at five in the morning on 1 October 1834 at his own house on strada Camellara; the civil act, given by two neighbours, names him husband of Chiara Rivetti and son of the late Matteo Falco and the late Francesca Crisci — confirming the 1767 baptism from an entirely separate record series. It gives his age as 74, which the baptism does not support; stated ages in these registers are approximate. **A daughter found in 1820 adds a third independent sighting.** On 23 August 1820 his daughter **ANNA FALCO**, twenty-five, wife of Arcangelo Crisci, died on strada Camellara, and her act names her «figlia di PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, e di CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — **both parents WITHOUT «fu»**. So Pasquale was alive, a contadino, and on the family's street in August 1820, fourteen years before his own death act; and Chiara, whom no record but her 1843 burial had ever named, was alive beside him. Anna was born about 1795 and had buried a two-day-old son seven months earlier. **And once, in 1824, he speaks for himself.** On 25 March 1824 the register opens: «sono comparsi **PASQUALE FALCO**, di anni **cinquantacinque**, di professione **COLONO**, regnicolo, domiciliato in questo comune **strada Camellara**, **ZIO DEL DEFUNTO**, e **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, **ZIO DEL DEFUNTO**» — the two brothers together, and **not** reporting a neighbour's child dead, as this archive said until 16 September 2026. The word is **«zio»** — uncle — written twice, once for each of them, and it was transcribed «vicino». The dead five-year-old is **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, son of Francesco Cioffi and **MARIA FALCO**. Read strictly the word makes Maria their sister and so a daughter of Matteo Falco; her own stated age of twenty-five in June 1824 forbids it. **The archive records the word and refuses the pedigree.** And at the foot of the leaf, beneath a formula naming Giuseppe as the brother who could not write, stands **«PASCALE FALCO»** in his own hand. **It is the only record in which Pasquale acts rather than being named**: everywhere else somebody else is speaking of him. It gives his trade as *colono*, a tenant farmer, where his death act ten years later calls him *contadino*; and his age as fifty-five, one year out against the baptism of 1767, which is ordinary in these registers. **HER PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED BY A CIVIL ACT.** She died on 13 September 1843 at eight in the evening, in her own house, aged eighty, a *contadina*: «CHIARA RIVETTI VEDOVA DI PASQUALE FALCO … figlia di NICOLA RIVETTI defunto, di professione CONTADINO, e di ANNA DI RUGGIO defunta». The archive had carried two rival couples for her parents since 2026 — the gentry Don Nicola Rivetti and Donn'Anna Quotolo, and the labouring Nicola Rivetti and Anna di Ruggio — and had said the labouring couple was the better fit without claiming it. The act settles it: her father was a contadino.

**His first age outside a death act — and it is wrong by fourteen years.** The banns of his son Vincenzo's marriage, published at Arienzo on Sunday **11 September 1814** and again on Sunday 18 September, describe the groom as «Maggiore assistito da **Pasquale suo Padre di Anni Sessanta**, di Professione **contadino**», with «**Chiara Rivetti sua Madre, di Anni quarantasette**, domiciliata in casa di suo Marito». Sixty in September 1814 implies a birth about 1754; his baptism of 24 October 1767 makes him **forty-six**. The same two acts give his son's age and his son's bride's age correctly to the year. **The clerk was accurate about the people standing in front of him and careless about everyone else** — which is the pattern this archive has argued for volumes, here proved in both directions by a single document. Chiara's forty-seven implies 1767; her 1843 burial implied 1763 and the family tree says 1772. Three estimates that still do not converge.

**A daughter found in the 1812 index: GIOVANNA FALCO.** «[Giov]anna Falco | Arienzo | **Contadina** | **PASQUALE, e CHIARA RIVETTI** | A **15 Decembre 1812**» — the surname and both parents verified at full magnification, the forename sitting in the page gutter and reading «…anna». **A SECOND child of that name.** This archive already held a **Giovanna Falco who died on 15 September 1805**, a daughter of the same parents, from the Arienzo parish register. So the Giovanna of 1812 is not a child the archive lacked — she is **a second daughter given her dead sister's name**, which is exactly what this family did again and again: two Raffaele, two Pasquale, two Maria. The claim was first published here as «a child this archive did not have» and that was wrong; see /corrections. Found not by reading the register act by act but by reading the year's index, which is three images. 

**CHIARA RIVETTI'S OWN BAPTISM, FOUND AND READ: 14 DECEMBER 1766.** «baptizavit infantem natam ex **NICOLAO RIVETTA et ANNA DI NUZZO** … cui imposui nomen **CLARA**», godmother **Cecilia Martone**, in the Collegiata di Sant'Andrea Apostolo. **She was SEVENTY-SEVEN when she died in 1843, not eighty** — the age on the death act is one more clerk's estimate. 

**And a conflict, published as a conflict**: the parish calls her mother **ANNA DI NUZZO**, across five children's baptisms; the civil series calls her **ANNA DI RUGGIO**, twice, twenty-two years apart. Both are certain in their own document and this archive does not know which is the woman's own name. 

Her brother **CARMINE**, who died in 1821 at fifty-three, was baptised **26 May 1768** — his stated age and the baptism agree to the year. And the parish books show **both** Nicola Rivetta households existing side by side: the physician «Mag[nifi]co Don Physico D. Nicolao Rivetta» with **Anna Ruotolo**, whose children are given three and four names apiece, and the plain Nicola with Anna di Nuzzo, whose children are given one. line.name: Raffaele Falco
line.spouseBorn: 24 Feb 1818, San Felice a Cancello — Massaria delle Fosse
line.note:
Baptised at Arienzo in 1818 — “ex Vincentio Falco, e Andreana Crisci coniugibus huius Parochiae, cui imposuit nomen Raphael”, with Gelsumina Ruggiero as godmother. His death record of 21 April 1880 names his father as Vincenzo. His wife Angela Rosa Morgillo, daughter of Orazio, died six days before him. His civil birth act — Arienzo, act 47 of 10 May 1818 — has him born at three in the afternoon in his father's own house on strada Camellara, and gives both parents' ages: Vincenzo twenty-seven, Andreana Crisci twenty. It was the first record to date her at all, and this archive read it as putting her birth about 1798 and her marriage, in October 1814, **at about sixteen**. **That is now corrected.** Her baptism, found in her own marriage dossier, is **30 November 1796** — so she was **twenty-one and a half** when this act called her twenty, and she married at **eighteen**, not sixteen. The act was re-read at native resolution in September 2026 for a second reason: her surname. It says «**ANDREANA CRISCI**», plainly, which agrees with the six documents of 1814 and against the 1839 death register's «Cioffi». **The complication is now closed.** Vincenzo and Andreana had named an earlier son Raffaele on 25 April 1816, and for a time this archive could not say which of the two was generation four — the generation was carried as *disputed*. The 1817 death register settles it: on **28 October 1817** the first Raffaele was buried, «figlio di Vincenzo Falco, e d'Andreana Crisci», aged about eighteen months. The child of 10 May 1818 is the one who lived. The burial was declared by **Giuseppe Falco, 37, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara**, called a «parente» of the family — a documented son of Matteo, and so Vincenzo's uncle. One warning survives: the two birth acts give irreconcilable ages for the father, Vincenzo thirty-five in 1816 and twenty-seven in 1818.

**The father's age problem is now explained rather than merely noted.** Vincenzo Falco was baptised on 1 February 1792, so he was **24** when the 1816 act called him thirty-five and **26** when the 1818 act called him twenty-seven. The 1818 figure is right by the reckoning these clerks used; the 1816 figure is simply an error. The warning that closed this entry can be retired.

**Her own birth act has been found.** Not at Arienzo — at **San Felice a Cancello**, which this archive had recorded as unreachable and had in fact never searched. On **24 February 1818 at seven in the morning**, in the **Massaria delle Fosse**, a farmstead rather than a street: «è comparso **ORAZIO MORGILLO** di anni **ventisei**, di professione **bracciale** … è nato una bambina nella sua propria casa di esso dichiarante, e da **VINCENZA PESCE** d'anni **ventisette**, di professione **filatrice**, sua legittima moglie … a cui si è dato il nome di **ANGIOLA ROSA**». 

**This is the first primary record of her parents.** Orazio Morgillo and Vincenza Pesce were carried on the family tree and nowhere else; they are now in a register, with ages, a trade and an address. Orazio at twenty-six was born about **1792**; Vincenza at twenty-seven about **1791** — **the first date this archive has ever had for her.** And the name at the font is **Angiola Rosa**. 

**THEY MARRIED ON 5 MARCH 1844, AT SANT'AGNESE IN ARIENZO — the act is read.** «Anno Domini **1844**, die vero **5 Mensis Martii** … coram me infrascripto **Parocho S. AGNETIS TERRAE ARGENTII** … matrimonium contraxerunt in faciem Ecclesiae per verba de praesenti **RAPHAEL FALCO filius VINCENTII et ANDREANAE CRISCI**, *Archipresbyteralis Ecclesiae S. ANDREAE Apostoli*, et **mea Parochiana ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO filia HORATII et VINCENTIAE PESCE**. In quorum fidem — **Josaphat Ruggiero Parochus**.» Witnesses: **[E]usebio Lettieri son of Clemente** and **Angelo di Marzo son of Francesco**. 

**The archive had no date for this marriage at all.** The act confirms both sets of parents in the parish's own hand — including **Orazio Morgillo and Vincenza Pesce**, who were first found only days ago in Angela Rosa's 1818 birth act at San Felice. And it names the parishes: **Raffaele belongs to the collegiate church of SANT'ANDREA APOSTOLO, Angela Rosa to SANT'AGNESE**, where they married. *Which of Arienzo's parishes a household belongs to is evidence, and this archive has not been using it.* 

*The path to it ran through a parish attribution this archive got right, then wrong, then declared open, in one day. See /corrections.* 

**THEIR FIRST CHILD, AND THE FIRST PRIMARY RECORD OF THEM AS A COUPLE.** Arienzo, Morti 1847, **atto 85**: «…è morta nella sua propria casa **VINCENZA FALCO**, nata in Arienzo, **di giorni UNO** … **figlia di RAFFAELE FALCO** di professione contadino … **e di ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO**» — **21 November 1847, at four in the afternoon**. The archive held this child only from the family tree; the act confirms her to the day and adds what a tree cannot — **Raffaele was living on strada CAMELLARA**, his grandfather's and his great-grandfather's street. The declarants were two neighbours of that street, **Raffaele Cioffi** and **Angelo Zimbardo**, both unable to write. 

**And it bounds the marriage**: a child born in November 1847 means **they were married in 1846 or earlier** — which narrows the hunt for the act behind the San Felice index entry at folio 2 a tergo. THEIR CIVIL MARRIAGE ACT IS FOUND — San Felice a Cancello, 7 March 1844, atto 12: «RAFFAELE FALCO di anni ventisei, nato in ARIENZO CORPO, contadino, domiciliato strada CAMMELLARA, figlio di VINCENZO FALCO di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, e di ANDREANA CRISCI, filatrice, domiciliata ivi; e ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO di anni ventisei, contadina, nata in questo Comune, figlia di ORAZIO MORGILLO, colono, e di VINCENZA PESCE, contadina». The promise was made in the BRIDE'S comune, which is why five years of searching at Arienzo found nothing. All four parents are alive in the act. The facing column certifies the celebration on 9 March, four days after the date the parish act gives.

events.evidence:
**A COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE HAS QUOTED TWICE AND NEVER GIVEN A HOUSEHOLD.** They exist here only inside two act quotations — their son **MICHELE's** marriage of **12 February 1850** and their son **FRANCESCO's** of **August 1854** — and neither put them anywhere a reader could find them. *That is the shape this archive has already had to correct three times: the documents were harvested and the family was not held.*

«*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO Defunto**, di professione **simile**, domiciliato ivi*» — 1850, with the capital **R** magnified for the first time on 20 September 2026, which is what separated **MICHELE** (son of Raffaele) from **MICHELANGELO** (son of Pasquale).

**HE IS NOT THE RAFFAELE FALCO OF ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO**, generation four, who was declaring a birth at Arienzo in 1847. **Dead before February 1850**, a *contadino* of strada Camellara; his own parents are not named in either act.

---

## THIS HOUSEHOLD RESTS ON A READING THAT WAS OVERTURNED ON 22 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND IT IS LEFT STANDING SO THE CORRECTION CAN BE READ AGAINST IT

**It was created on 21 September**, out of two acts that call a father **RAFFAELE**: Michele Falco's marriage of **12 February 1850** and Francesco Falco's of **August 1854**. **The second of those two men has since been identified, and his father was PASQUALE.**

**The chain is three records this archive already held.** **RAFFAELA FALCO**, daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida, married **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO**, son of **PASQUALE FALCO** and Chiara Rivetti, on **6 July 1832** — read from the act. She died on **20 April 1854**, aged thirty-four, of **strada Camellara**, and the register calls her «***moglie di FRANCESCO FALCO***». **Four months later**, in August 1854, a **FRANCESCO FALCO** of strada Camellara married again as «***vedovo di RAFFAELA FALCO***».

**One Raffaela Falco, one widower, one street, four months apart.** **Francesco of 1854 is Francescantonio of 1832, and his father was Pasquale Falco.** *The same man is called FRANCESCO in his own children's death acts of 1832, 1836 and 1838 and FRANCESCANTONIO in his marriage act and his son's birth act — in the same registers, in the same years.*

**SO «FIGLIO DEL FU RAFFAELE» IN THE 1854 ACT IS WRONG**, and the 1850 act says the same thing about a **MICHELE** whose christening name the parish gives as **MICHELE ANGELO ANTONIO**. **Whether that second «Raffaele» is the same slip is not yet proved and is not claimed here.** See work-list row 87.

line.note: A farmer of Arienzo. His last recorded child, Gerardo, was born in 1913 not at Arienzo but at Arpaia, over the provincial border — the first sign of the move north. THEIR MARRIAGE DOSSIER IS OPEN. Arienzo marriage allegati 1897, fascicolo for «FALCO RAFFAELE · MAIONE COSTANZA», Registro dei Matrimoni n. 41, SIX documents. Banns published 12 and 19 September 1897. His birth extract — 1873 act 39 — says he was born «il giorno SEI corrente mese di Aprile ad ore ventidue» to «CARMINANTONIO FALCO di Raffaele, contadino, di anni VENTIDUE, domiciliato in Arienzo VIA DEGLI ORTI» and «GIOVANNA ARRICALE FU FRANCESCO»: it confirms his birth date, corroborates his father's birth about 1850, gives the mother's father as FRANCESCO ARRICALE, and shows the household living in Via degli Orti rather than on strada Camellara. A certificate of poverty of 29 August 1897 calls them «FALCO RAFFAELE di Carminantonio e MAIONE COSTANZA DI ANIELLO … sono poveri» — naming her father, and recording that they married as paupers. The banns of 26 August 1897 name the bride's parents for the first time: «MAIONE COSTANZA, di anni VENTUNO … figlia di ANIELLO, di anni CINQUANTASEI, contadino, e figlia di MARTONE ANNA, contadina», both living at Arienzo. So Costanza Maione was the daughter of ANIELLO MAIONE, born about 1841, and ANNA MARTONE.

Witnessed by **GENNARO RIVETTI**, twenty-one, of **strada Monticello de' Cappuccini**, and **AGOSTINO CIOFFI**, forty-eight, of **strada Camellara**.

**The first Rosaria died on 15 MARCH 1819.** This one is born on **15 March 1821** — the same day of the same month, two years later. *The coincidence is recorded and not explained.* This household reuses a dead child's name as a matter of course, and so does its neighbour: two Raffaele, two Pasquale, two Antonia, two Maddalena, two Giovanni are already on this site.

**WORK-LIST ROW 42 IS NOT ANSWERED BY THIS.** That row asks where the FIRST Rosaria's birth act is, and it is still in none of the registers for 1816–1819. What this act does is make the second Rosaria a documented person and confirm that the first was a distinct child.

Witnesses **PIETRO GRAZIO, fifty, contadino, regnicolo, of strada CAPODICONCA** — the family is written *Grazia* elsewhere in these registers — and **ORAZIO PORRINO, forty, contadino, regnicolo**.

**The age agrees.** His marriage act of 19 September 1861 makes him **twenty-four**, which gives about 1837; born 9 September 1838 he had turned twenty-three eleven days before it. **This is the closest fit in the register and there is no other Falco birth in 1838 to compete with it.**

**WHY IT WAS MISSING, IN THE ACT'S OWN WORDS.** The left page of the opening — the band this archive reads for parents — says «*nata da ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legittima … **E DA LUI DICHIARANTE**, di anni come sopra, di professione come sopra, domiciliato come sopra*». **The father's name is never written on it.** A parents-band sweep of 1838 reads a Crisci and no Falco, which is exactly what happened: the year stood here as **«NO FALCO — the volume was read end to end and the family is not in it»**. **THE FAMILY TREE CARRIES A «VINCENZA FALCO» AS RAFFAELE FALCO'S DAUGHTER, UNSOURCED.** This is her birth act. *An assertion this archive has been carrying as unverified is now a document.*

**SHE IS OLDER THAN GENERATION FIVE.** Her brother **CARMINE ANTONIO FALCO** was born **10 July 1850**, two years and eight months after her.

**And she is named for her paternal grandfather, VINCENZO FALCO**, who was alive and on the same street.

**Both parents' ages are right.** He is **thirty** and was born **10 May 1818**; she is **twenty-nine** and was born at San Felice a Cancello on **24 February 1818**. *Two exact readings in one act, which this office manages rarely.*

line.note:
His civil marriage act — Arienzo, act 16 of 15 October 1814, read from the image on 20 September 2026 — records him as aged 23, a contadino of strada Camellara, and “figlio maggiore di Pasquale Falco”: eldest son, and his father named without “fu”, so Pasquale was still living. His wife Andreana is “figlia di Arcangelo”. The parish record of the same marriage names his mother Chiara Rivetti and Andreana's mother Ruggiero. His death record of 15 May 1875 names Pasquale a third time. The civil death registers place his household on strada Camellara at Arienzo, the same street as his father’s, and name him with his wife Andreana Crisci. He called a son Pasquale after his father twice: the first died aged three on 22 February 1833, while the grandfather still lived; the second was born about a fortnight after the grandfather’s death and lived ten days, dying on Christmas Day 1834.

**His baptism has been found, and it settles the age series.** His marriage dossier — Arienzo processetti 1814, bundle 16 — contains the extract the archpriest **Giacinto Morgillo** copied out of the parish register on 13 September 1814, citing **liber IX baptizatorum, folio 47 a tergo**: «Anno Domini Millesimo septingentesimo nonagesimo secundo **1792**, die vero prima **1 Februarii** … baptizavi infantem natum ex **Paschale Falco**, et **Clara Rivetta** Conjugibus … cui dedi nomen **Vincentius Raphael**.» 

Two things follow. **He was born about 1 February 1792, not 1793** — the date this archive published is corrected. And **his own second name was Raffaele**, which is why he named a son Raffaele in 1816 and, when that child died, named the next one Raffaele too. 

Measured against a real date, the notorious age series stops looking like one man changing his story. The banns of September 1814 call him **23** when he was 22 years and 7 months — right, if you count the year a man is *in* rather than the years he has completed, which is how these clerks counted. The 1818 birth act calls him **27** at 26 years 3 months — right the same way. **Three of the statements are exact.** The marriage act's 21, the 1839 register's 42 and above all the 1816 act's **35** — when he was 24 — are the clerks guessing. 

**And his wife is settled too.** The same bundle holds her baptism extract: **Adriana**, baptised at Arienzo on **30 November 1796**, daughter of **Arcangelo Crisci** and **Sara Ruggiero**. Adriana is the name she was given at the font, and it is the root of every variant the registers throw up — Andreana, Andriana, Andrea. The 1839 death register was read here as «Andriana **Cioffi**», and this archive carried Crisci-vs-Cioffi as an open conflict; **six documents of 1814 now say Crisci and name her parents**, so the conflict is closed and the wrong reading stays on /corrections rather than being quietly swapped.

events.evidence: **THIRTY-NINE, A VATICALE, AND EXPLICITLY NOT THE VINCENZO OF THIS LINE.** Dead **13 September 1889**, born about 1850. *This archive's own Vincenzo Falco, generation three, was born in 1792 and was alive in December 1864; the two are separated here on purpose, because a Vincenzo Falco of Arienzo is exactly the kind of name that gets merged by accident.* **The act has not been re-read.**

events.evidence:
**THE ACT THAT FINALLY SEPARATES THE TWO GIUSEPPE FALCO OF ARIENZO, AND IT DOES IT WITH ONE WORD.**

«*Oggi che sono li **sedici — 16** del mese di **Marzo** … mille ottocento **dieci** … è comparso … il Signor **GIUSEPPE FALCO DI FRANCESCO** — di professione **BRACCIALE** — d'anni **VENTISETTE** — … abitante nella strada **della CAMELLARA** — Il medesimo ha presentata una **bambina** … **nata in costanza del suo legitimo Matrimonio con GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA sua Moglie** — La quale è nata il giorno **sedici** del mese di **Marzo**, ad ore **dieci***».

**«DI FRANCESCO» — AND THE OTHER GIUSEPPE FALCO IS «DEL FU MATTEO».** Nine weeks earlier, in this same volume, «*GIUSEPPE FALCO **DEL FU MATTEO**, massaro di campagna, d'anni vent'otto*» declared a son on **the same street**.

**TWO MEN OF ONE NAME, ONE YEAR APART IN AGE, ON ONE STREET, BOTH DECLARING CHILDREN IN THE SAME REGISTER.** This archive has spent two days trying to tell them apart by trade — which fails, because both are called *massaro di campagna* by 1815 — and by street, which fails here. **The patronymic is the only clean discriminator, and the wife's name is the other.** [[which-falco]]

**HIS FATHER IS «DI», NOT «DEL FU» — FRANCESCO FALCO WAS ALIVE IN MARCH 1810.** *This archive has published that a missing «fu» proves nothing about life; a present «di» against a «del fu» in the same clerk's hand nine weeks apart is a different thing.* [[quondam-not-evidence]]

**The child's given name falls below the band read and is not recorded here.**

Thirty-two, a contadino of strada Camellara. **HIS SURNAME WAS PUBLISHED HERE AS «CIOFFI» UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 AND IT IS NOT CIOFFI.** The control is two lines below it in the same act: **GIOVANNI CIOFFI**, written with the unmistakable double-f ligature and its long descender. **This word has no such ligature.** It reads **«Gasparo»** — a capital with a descending loop, «a», a long ſ, then «aro».

events.evidence:
**THE BIRTH ACT OF ANTONIA DI GUIDA'S NEPHEW, AND IT PAIRS WITH THE DEATH ACT THIS ARCHIVE READ FIRST AND COULD NOT PLACE.**

«*Oggi che sono li **trenta** del mese di **Ottobre** … mille ottocento **dieci**, ad ore **quattordici**, è comparso … il Signor **GIACINTO MARRA DI PASQUALE** — di professione **BRACCIALE** — d'anni **VENTOTTO** — … abitante nella strada **della PORTA DI SOPRA** — Il medesimo ha presentato un **bambino** … **nato in costanza del suo legitimo Matrimonio con MARGARITA DI GUIDA sua Moglie** — Il quale è nato il giorno **suddetto trenta** del mese di **Ottobre**, ad ore **dieci***».

**Born 30 October 1810; the death register buries a PASQUALE ANTONIO MARRA of twenty-five days on strada Porta di Sopra**, which puts that burial in late November. **Same street, same parents, and the arithmetic closes.**

**He was named for his father's father.** The act calls Giacinto Marra «*DI PASQUALE*» — *di*, not *del fu*, **so Pasquale Marra was alive when his grandson was named for him.**

**AND THE STRIP READ THIS AS «GIACINTO SANSONE».** It was magnified only because this archive had published a household for Giacinto Marra hours earlier and the surname had to be right. [[the-contact-sheet-is-triage]]

events.evidence:
**HER BIRTH ACT, FOUND AND READ — AND IT MAKES HER A YEAR YOUNGER THAN HER OWN MARRIAGE DOES.** The 1845 dossier carries a certified copy of it as document 2; **the register was then opened at the act it names**, because a copy is not a record.

**Arienzo, Nati 1822, act 66**, images 68 right and 69 left: «*L'Anno mille ottocento **ventidue**, il dì **due** del mese di **Agosto**, ad ore **ventuno**, avanti di Noi **VINCENZO MORGILLO Sindaco** ed Ufiziale dello Stato Civile del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Distretto di **Nola** … è comparso **GENNARO MORGILLO**, di anni **trentasei**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada VALLONE**, quale ci ha presentato una **femina** … che la stessa è nata da **MARIA FELICE SAN=/SONE sua moglie legittima**, di anni **trentaquattro** … nel giorno **due** del mese di **Agosto** anno corrente, alle ore **diciassette**, nella sua propria di abitazione*». The *indicazione*: baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo** the same day, «*il Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato ad **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO***».

**SHE WAS TWENTY-TWO WHEN SHE MARRIED, NOT TWENTY-THREE.** Born 2 August 1822, she was twenty-two and six months on 2 February 1845. **The certified copy of the promise in the dossier says «di anni VENTIDUE» and the register's own act 3 says «VENTITRE».** The birth act decides between them, and it decides for the copy. *Nothing turns on the year; it is recorded because this archive has twice found a clerk's age to be a guess and here it can watch one being made.*

**Her father is a MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA here and a COLONO in 1843 and 1845** — a man who kept a farm and ended a labourer on it, or two words for the same work. **The street changes too**: strada Vallone in 1822, strada Cappuccini by 1845.

**Witnessed by VINCENZO VERDICCHIO, seventy, *contadino*, and OTTAVIO MIGLIORE, thirty-nine, *BARBIERE*, both of strada Croce dell'Ospedale.** The same Ottavio Migliore, at the same stated age, witnessed **Angela Maria Falco's** birth act fourteen months earlier, on 19 January 1822 — **and this act gives the trade that one did not**: he is a barber.

events.evidence:
NAMED ONLY BY HIS DAUGHTER'S MARRIAGE, and already dead when it happened: «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO**, di professione **colono***». Not claimed as kin — recorded because the Falco married the Morgillo repeatedly and this archive cannot yet tell those Morgillo houses apart.

**A CANDIDATE FOR HIS DEATH ACT, FOUND ON 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 IN THE ARCHIVE'S OWN FILES.** Arienzo Morti 1843, act 33 — `an_ua14345` img24R — records **GENNARO MORGILLO, fifty-three, COLONO of strada Camellara, «vedovo di Felicia S___», son of ANGELO MORGILLO defunto, colono**, dead **4 August 1843**. That is eighteen months before this marriage, it agrees on the trade, on the wife's forename and on her being dead first, and the bride's **strada Cappuccini** is the hill where that Angelo Morgillo's house stood. **It is graded PROBABLE and no more**, because Morgillo is the commonest surname in these registers. **AND THE WIFE'S SURNAME NOW AGREES TOO.** The 1843 word was published as «Sompone» and read on 20 September as **«Sanſone»** — SANSONE — against a control on the same street: Arienzo Morti 1826 act 22, declared by **ANGELO SANSONE** of strada Camellara, whose surname is written in the same hand-shape, long ſ and all. **What this archive had taken for a «p» is a long s.** So the mother named here is the woman named there. **The 1845 processetto would settle it in one line**, by quoting the death act's number.

---

**PROVED, 21 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THE PROCESSETTO DID EXACTLY WHAT THIS ENTRY SAID IT WOULD.** The last line above reads «*The 1845 processetto would settle it in one line, by quoting the death act's number*». **It quotes the act itself.** Bundle 3 of `an_ua14190` — the Arienzo *processetti* for 1845, on Antenati and free — holds, twice over on images 31 and 32, a certified copy headed «*MUNICIPALITÀ DI **ARIENZO** — **Estratto di Morte del 1843** — Num. d'ordine **TRENTATRE***», ending «*Valga per uso di **matrimonio**. Rilasciato in Arienzo il dì **ventidue** del mese di **Novembre** … **1844***», signed by the Sindaco and by the Cancelliere Archivario **FELICE MORGILLO**.

**ACT 33 OF 1843 IS THE ACT THIS MARRIAGE WAS BUILT ON.** The grade moves from *probable* to **proved**: the man who died a widower on **strada Camellara on 4 August 1843**, son of the late **ANGELO MORGILLO**, colono of the Monticello de' Cappuccini, **is Angela Maria Morgillo's father**, and the Falco of strada Camellara are joined to the Morgillo of the hill by a document instead of by four agreeing details.

events.evidence:
«GENNARO MORGILLO, vedovo di Felicia SANSONE, nato in Arienzo, di anni cinquantatré, di professione COLONO, domiciliato STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di ANGELO MORGILLO defunto, di professione COLONO» — born about 1790. A THIRD SON of the colono Angelo, and the one who left the hill: he lived on strada Camellara, the Falco street. HIS DEATH WAS DECLARED BY GIUSEPPE FALCO, colono of the same street. (Dated 14 August here until 20 September 2026; the act reads «il dì quattro del mese di Agosto», and the acts either side of it are 3 August and 10 August.)

**THIS ARCHIVE SAID, UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, THAT THE ACT WAS «THE CLOSEST THE RECORD COMES TO THE FALCO-MORGILLO MARRIAGE THAT WAS STILL THIRTY YEARS AWAY». THAT WAS WRONG BY TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS, AND THE ARCHIVE'S OWN FILES SAID SO.** Eighteen months after this act, on **2 February 1845**, **CRESCENZO FALCO** — Giuseppe's son, of this same strada Camellara — married **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, twenty-three, of **strada Cappuccini**, «*figlia di GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO, di professione colono, e di MARIA FELICIA SANSONE … defunta*».

**PROBABLE, NOT PROVEN: the Gennaro Morgillo who died here is very likely her father.** Four things agree — the forename and surname; the trade, *colono*, in both acts; the wife, a **Felicia** already dead when he died a widower in 1843 and «defunta» in 1845; and the street, since the bride lived on **strada Cappuccini** and this Gennaro's father Angelo was the colono of the **Monticello de' Cappuccini**, the hill that street climbs. **And the wife's surname, which could not be read on 20 September, was read the same day.** The word in the 1843 act is **«Sanſone»** — SANSONE — with the long ſ that this archive published as a «p» when it wrote «Sompone». The control is in the next volume it checked: Arienzo Morti 1826 act 22 is declared by **ANGELO SANSONE** of this same strada Camellara, and the two words are the same shape, letter for letter. **So the 1845 act's MARIA FELICIA SANSONE and the 1843 act's FELICIA SANSONE are one name**, s and z being interchangeable in these registers.

**Five things now agree, and one of them is a whole second name.** What is still missing is a document that says so. Morgillo is the commonest surname on these pages and this archive already holds two distinct Angelo Morgillo. **What would settle it is the marriage's own dossier**: the *processetto* for Arienzo 1845 must contain Gennaro Morgillo's death certificate, and that certificate will carry an act number. If it is 33 of 1843, this is him.

---

**RE-READ AT 3,200 PIXELS, 21 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND FOUR THINGS IN THE SWEEP'S ROW WERE WRONG.**

**The act is of 4 AUGUST, not 14 August** — «*nel giorno **quattro** del mese di **Agosto** anno corrente, alle ore **diciassette***».

**Giuseppe Falco is «di anni CINQUANTOTTO», not fifty-five.** That removes a puzzle this archive recorded about a man who was «56 in May and 55 in August».

**The second declarant is NOT a Cioffi.** «*e **GIOVANNI CRIS[P/C]I**, di anni **quarantotto**, di professione **contadino**, regnicolo, domiciliato in **strada Camellara***» — the surname's second letter is a zigzag *r*, not a round *o*, and there is no double-f ascender anywhere in it. **C-r-i and then a long descender.** Whether it ends *-spi* or *-sci* this archive has already had to leave open once, and leaves open here.

**AND THE ACT NAMES HIS MOTHER, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAD NOT RECORDED.** «*figlio di **ANGELO MORGILLO defunto**, di professione colono, domiciliato ivi, **e di MARIA G———, defunta**, domiciliata ivi*». **The surname will not resolve** — a looped G, six or seven letters, at the limit of this filming — and it is left unread rather than guessed. **It is Angelo Morgillo's wife**, and this household has never had one.

**The identification is now PROVED, not probable**: the 1845 marriage dossier quotes this act by number. See work-list row 73.

events.evidence:
«*figlia di **GIOVANNI MORGILLO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi*» — and **the act does not mark him dead**, where it marks both of the groom's parents dead in the same sentence. **Living at Arienzo in June 1828.** A **GENNARO MORGILLO**, thirty-three, of strada Cappellotto della Porta di Sopra, witnessed his granddaughter's birth in 1830; **the act does not say he is kin and this archive does not say so either**.

---

**HE DIED ON 10 NOVEMBER 1864, AGED EIGHTY-TWO — AND THE ACT GIVES HIS OWN PARENTS.** Found on 22 September 2026 while reading the Arienzo death registers for somebody else entirely. **Arienzo, Morti 1864, act 73** (`an_ua14366` img 40R):

«*L'anno mille ottocento **sessantaquattro**, il dì **undici** del mese di **Novembre**, alle ore **venti**, avanti di noi **RAFFAELE RIVETTI Sindaco** … sono comparsi **RAFFAELE GUIDA**, di anni **quarantotto**, di professione **COLONO**, regnicolo, domiciliato in **Arienzo, Villaggio CRISCI**, ed **ALESSANDRO CRISCI**, di anni **trentadue** … i quali han dichiarato, che nel giorno **dieci** del mese di **Novembre** anno suddetto alle ore **tre d'Italia** è morto nella sua casa **GIOVANNI MORGILLO — VEDOVO DI DOMENICA CRISCI**, nato in **Arienzo**, di anni **OTTANTADUE**, di professione **COLONO**, domiciliato **nel Villaggio CRISCI**, **figlio del fu PASQUALE**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, **e della fu MARIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*».

**THE IDENTIFICATION RESTS ON HIS WIFE'S NAME, NOT HIS OWN.** Morgillo is among the four commonest surnames in these registers and Giovanni is a common forename; **what settles it is «VEDOVO DI DOMENICA CRISCI»**, which is exactly the woman the 1828 marriage act names as Pasqua Morgillo's mother — and the **villaggio Crisci** is the **strada Crisci** the bride lived on in 1828.

**Eighty-two in November 1864 puts his birth about 1782.** He outlived his daughter Pasqua, dead before January 1860, and he was alive at her marriage thirty-six years earlier.

events.evidence:
**A FOURTH CHILD FOR ROSA FALCO, AND THE ACT THAT DATES THIS HOUSEHOLD'S MOVE.** Act **139**: «*L'anno mille ottocento **VENTISETTE**, il dì **VENTI** del mese di **DECEMBRE**, ad ore **VENTI** … è comparso **CARLANTONIO MORGILLO, di anni QUARANTADUE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **ROSA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni QUARANTA**, domiciliata collo stesso, **e da lui dichiarante** … nel giorno **VENTI** del mese di **DECEMBRE** … alle ore **QUATTRO E MEZZA, nella casa sua propria d'abitazione** … il nome di **MARIA CARMELA***». Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo** the same day; witness **ORAZIO PORRINO, thirty, contadino, of strada CAMELLARA**.

**ROSA FALCO IS A DAUGHTER OF THE FOUNDERS** — her death act of 16 October 1830 calls her «*figlia di **MATTEO FALCO, defunto**, e di **FRANCESCA CRISCI***» — so this is **a granddaughter of Matteo Falco**, and the fourth child this archive has for the household: Giovanna (1817), Giuditta (1820), Angela (1823), **Maria Carmela (1827)**.

**AND IT DATES THE MOVE.** This household is on **strada MADDALENA** in 1817, 1820 and 1823, and on **strada CAMELLARA** when Rosa Falco dies in 1830. **This act puts them on Camellara already in December 1827**, which narrows the move to between **March 1823 and December 1827**.

**Her mother's age holds**: forty in December 1827, and forty-two at her death in October 1830 — a year apart across three years, which for these clerks is close agreement.

*Found by the declarant-band sweep of 1827, work-list rows 35 and 86 — a volume that had never been read at all.*

events.evidence:
**THIRTY-TWO** in October 1828, contadino of **strada Monticello de' Cappuccini**. Husband of **MARIA MAJONE**; their **eight-year-old PASQUALE** died on 6 May (atto 14). He declares his brother's child's death as «**ZIO DELLA DEFUNTA**» (atto 56), magnified and confirmed, which makes him and Vincenzo brothers.

**TWO THINGS WERE WRONG HERE UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026.** This page said «34 in 1828» and cited atto 14 for it — **and atto 14 gives him no age at all**: he is named in it as the dead boy's father, and fathers are not aged in these acts. **The only act of 1828 that ages him is atto 56, and it says «di anni trentadue».** And the dead boy was **PASQUALE**, not Raffaele: «*è morto nella sua propria casa **PASCALE MORGILLO, d'anni otto***».

**It is the second time in one morning that an age was attached to a man from an act that never states it** — the first was Giovanni Cioffi's «forty in 1840». **Both came from reading a household into an act instead of reading the act.**

events.evidence:
**HER MARRIAGE AND HER PARENTS, FROM THE REGISTER — BUT NOT YET HER DEATH.** «*e di **PASQUA MORGILLO defunta***» gave a death window and nothing else. The **Arienzo marriage register of 1828, act 11, 29 June** now gives the rest: «***PASQUA MORGILLO**, maggiore, di anni **venticinque**, nata in **Arienzo**, domiciliata ivi **strada CRISCI**, figlia di **GIOVANNI MORGILLO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **DOMENICA CRISCI***».

So: **born at Arienzo about 1803**, of **strada Crisci**, daughter of **Giovanni Morgillo** — **living in June 1828** — and **Domenica Crisci**. Her daughter's birth act of December 1830 makes her twenty-six; the two ages differ by a year and the clerks guessed both.

**HER DEATH ACT IS STILL OWED.** It is **item 7** of the 1860 marriage act's own document list — «*Nell'atto di morte della madre della stessa*» — and it is **NOT filed in bundle 3 of the 1860 processetti**: images 25 to 42 hold four death extracts and all four are from **Forchia**, for the groom's side. **Where the Arienzo one went is not known.** The window is still 30 December 1830 to 21 January 1860.

This archive already holds, from the act, «RAFFAELE MORGILLO, 22, CONTADINO, figlio di Carlantonio Morgillo», died 9 MAY 1832. SAME DAY OF THE MONTH, DIFFERENT MONTH, DIFFERENT ENDING, DIFFERENT SEX. This is the woman named on Donna Francesca Rivetti's act of January 1816, now with her own death, her age, her father and his station.

**THE MOTHER'S SURNAME WAS «Maria d'Isteria(?)» HERE UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND «d'ISTERIA» IS EXCLUDED.** At the leaf's full resolution the word plainly ends **-ustina** — there is no **r** before the final syllable — and it begins **Di**. **The likeliest reading is DI GIUSTINA**, an attested Campanian surname; the middle letter will not separate a **g** from an **f**, so *Difustina* cannot be ruled out and the reading is **not treated as settled**. **What is settled is the negative.**

events.evidence:
«CARMINE RIVETTI di anni cinquantatre, marito di GIUSTINA MORGILLO, nato in Arienzo, di professione Contadino» — born about 1768. Declared by **MARCELLO RIVETTI, thirty-six**, contadino of **strada Monticello de' Cappuccini** — the same street as the dead man — and **GIOVANNI MORGILLO FU PASCALE, forty-five**, contadino of **strada Cioffi**, «**parente del defunto**».

**The second declarant's patronymic was published here as «fu RAFFAELE» until 20 September 2026.** The word is **PASCALE**: a long ſ in the middle and the ending **-ale**, where Raffaele has a double-f and ends **-ele**. **It is the only thing that identifies which Giovanni Morgillo this is**, and it gives his father a name.

**Note what «fu» is doing here, because this archive got it wrong elsewhere in the same week**: it is a **patronymic** — *Giovanni Morgillo, son of the late Pascale* — attached to a living declarant. **It is not the death mark in a filiation clause**, which these forms write as «Defunto» AFTER the parent's name, as they do twice in this very act for Nicola Rivetti and Anna di Ruggio.

**This closes the household at one end and opens a generation above it.** One of the two declarants is described as «*parente*» — kin — and the act does not say how.

**IT DOES NOT SETTLE THE ANGELA FALCO QUESTION.** A Saverio Rivieri, also a *massaro*, buried an infant by **ANGELA FALCO** in **1809**, on a different street. If that is this man, Angela Falco died between 1809 and 1810 — **and this archive has now read every Arienzo death act of both years and she is in neither**. So either she died away from Arienzo, or there were two Saverio Rivieri. **The two households stay apart.** [[saverio-rivieri-angela-falco]]

The archive's only previous source for this woman is the parish marriage act, whose machine transcript gives «e [ROSAE] Ruggiero» WITH THE FORENAME IN BRACKETS, the archive's own mark for a reading it did not trust. The civil index is unambiguous. AND IT EXPLAINS A NAME: the daughter born to this couple on 19 DECEMBER 1828 was called SARA — the only Sara in the household, and this archive found her only yesterday. She was named for her mother's mother. The midwife who declared that birth was GELSOMINA RUGGIERO, sixty, and a Gelsomina Ruggiero stood MATRINA at this couple's son Raffaele's baptism in 1818; the Ruggiero kinship is now MORE likely and is STILL NOT CLAIMED

events.evidence: SHE IS THE THREAD THROUGH THE WHOLE FALCO CONNECTION. «Matrina fuit SARA RUGGIERO» appears on TEN PAGES of the Arienzo parish baptism harvest, standing godmother to children of AT LEAST SIX FALCO HOUSEHOLDS: PASQUALE FALCO & CHIARA RIVETTI (generation four); GIUSEPPE FALCO & GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA of strada Costa; GIOACCHINO FALCO & VITTORIA CIMMINO; DOMENICO CRISCI & MARGARITA FALCO, on three separate pages; ANTONIO MORGILLO & ROSA FALCO — the founders' daughter; and VINCENZO FALCO & ANDREANA CRISCI, which is her OWN DAUGHTER. events.evidence:
**ANDREANA CRISCI'S MOTHER DELIVERED ARIENZO'S CHILDREN, AND THE REGISTER LETS HER SPEAK FOR THEM.**

«*Oggi che sono li **undici — 11** del mese di **Maggio** … mille ottocento **dieci**, ad ore **ventidue**, è **comparsa** avanti del Signor Sindaco di questa Università **la Signora SARA RUGGIERO** — di professione **OSTETRICE** — d'anni **QUARANTADUE** — … abitante nella strada **della CAMELLARA** — **La medesima** ha presentato un **bambino**, che ha dichiarato esser **nato da GRAZIA VIGLIOTTA d'anni VENTISEI**, domiciliata in detta Università, strada **ROSCIANO**, **e da IGNOTO GENITORE***».

**«E DA IGNOTO GENITORE» — father unknown.** Under the Napoleonic code the midwife declared the births no father would come forward for, and **the clerk wrote every verb in the feminine**: *è comparsa, la Signora, la medesima*. **This is the one kind of act in these registers where a woman stands alone before the Sindaco.**

**Forty-two in May 1810 puts her birth about 1768**, and the 1814 register gives a *levatrice* **Sara Ruggiero of forty-six** — the same year. **The identification rests on the street**: strada Camellara, where her husband Arcangelo Crisci is recorded two months earlier.

**AND IT LEAVES ONE THING UNCOMFORTABLE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WRITTEN DOWN.** If she was born in 1768, she bore **Carmela Crisci in January 1815 at about forty-seven**. *That is late but not impossible, and the alternative — two Sara Ruggiero on one street — is not better supported. Recorded as probable, with the difficulty stated.*

events.evidence:
**SHE WAS A MIDWIFE, AND THAT EXPLAINS THE TEN PARISH PAGES.** Act **29** of 1816: «*L'Anno mille ottocento sedici a' dì **VENTISETTE** del mese di **FEBRARO**, ad ore **DICIANNOVE**, avanti di noi **DANIELE SORICE Sindaco** … è comparsa **SARA RUGGIERO, di anni QUARANTACINQUE, di professione LEVATRICE, domiciliata in detto Comune, strada CAMELLARA**, ed ha dichiarato che il giorno sopraindicato ad ore **TREDICI** è nato nella casa di **FRANCESCA DIGLIO** … un **MASCHIO** che ci ha presentato … a cui si è dato il nome di **ANTONIO***».

**THE IDENTIFICATION, AND WHAT IT RESTS ON.** This archive already holds a **SARA RUGGIERO, forty-five, of strada CAMELLARA**, from the 1817 birth register, where she is «*sua moglie legittima*» of **ARCANGELO CRISCI** and bearing a son at forty-five. **Forty-five in February 1816 and forty-five in 1817**, on the same street, under the same name. **The two are the same woman**, and the repeated age is this office's ordinary habit rather than a difficulty. *No document says so in one sentence, and this is set down as an identification, not a quotation.*

**WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TRADE.** This archive has long recorded that «*Matrina fuit SARA RUGGIERO*» appears on **ten pages** of the Arienzo parish baptism harvest, standing godmother to children of **at least six Falco households** — Pasquale Falco & Chiara Rivetti, Giuseppe Falco & Gelsomina Vigliotta, Gioacchino Falco & Vittoria Cimmino, Domenico Crisci & Margarita Falco, Antonio Morgillo & Rosa Falco, and her own daughter's house. **It had no explanation for that reach.** **A LEVATRICE STANDS GODMOTHER TO THE CHILDREN SHE DELIVERS.** Her presence across six unrelated Falco households is her occupation, not a kinship — which removes an inference this archive had been careful never to draw and now need not.

**And she practised on the Falco's own street.** Strada Camellara is where Vincenzo Falco, Giuseppe Falco and Michelangelo Falco all lived. *Her successors in this register are **ROSA DELLA SELVA**, fifty-eight here and seventy-nine in 1830, and **CATERINA RUGGIERO** — whose surname is hers, and about whom nothing is claimed.*

*Found by reading the 1816 birth register at the combined band for work-list row 86.*

events.evidence:
«*e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE**, di professione **contadina** … **defunta***» — from her daughter's marriage act of 2 February 1845.

**PUBLISHED HERE AS «SANSONE» UNTIL 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND WITH IT THE CLAIM THAT THE SURNAME «HAD NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE AT ALL».** The letter is a long **ſ**, not a **z**, and the test is on the same leaf: **«Crescenzo», in the groom's own name, has a z** — a compact loop that drops below the line and has no ascender. **The letter in this surname rises above the x-height before it descends.** A z in this hand does not do that.

**So the surname was not new.** **ANGELO SANSONE**, contadino of **strada Camellara**, declares the death of Maria Falco, wife of Alfonso Diglio, on 25 April 1826 — and his surname is written in the same shape. **Three acts now agree: 1826, 1843 and 1845, all SANSONE.** Not claimed as kin.

---

**HER SURNAME IS SETTLED, FROM A REGISTER TWENTY-ONE YEARS OLDER THAN THE ONE THAT COULD NOT BE READ.** Her daughter's birth act — **Arienzo, Nati 1822, act 66** — writes it across a line break, «*la stessa è nata da **MARIA FELICE SAN=/SONE** sua moglie legittima, di anni **trentaquattro**, domiciliata con esso, e da **lui dichiarante***». **SAN, then SONE.** A word split at the syllable cannot be a «Sompone», and this filming separates it where the 1843 filming does not.

**Thirty-four in August 1822** puts her birth about 1788. She was dead before February 1845.

She is the woman the 1843 death act calls «*vedova*»'s husband's «*FELICIA SANSONE*» and this archive once published as **«Felicia Sompone»**.

events.evidence:
**DATED, AND HER PARENTS NAMED.** The 1845 dossier carries her death extract as well as her husband's; **the register was then opened at the act it copies**, and read at 3,200 pixels.

**Arienzo, Morti 1838, act 3, 10 January 1838**: «*avanti di noi **FILIPPO TROISI Sindaco** … del Comune di **Corpo d'Arienzo**, Distretto di **Caserta** … sono comparsi **SALVATORE SPOSITO**, di anni **quarantadue**, di professione contadino … domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, e **CESARE DIGLIO**, di anni **sessanta**, di professione contadino … domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, i quali han dichiarato, che nel giorno **dieci** del mese di **Gennajo** anno corrente, alle ore **otto**, è morta nella sua propria casa **MARIA FELICE SANSONE**, di anni **cinquantatre**, **moglie di GENNARO MORGILLO**, nata in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadina**, domiciliata ivi, figlia di **PASQUALE SANSONE defunto**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **MARTA LE CASARO defunta**, domiciliata ivi*».

**She died five and a half years before her husband**, in the house they shared on strada Camellara, and her daughter married an orphan's marriage seven years after that.

**Fifty-three in January 1838** puts her birth about 1785; her daughter's birth act of 1822 makes her thirty-four, which is 1788. *Three years apart, and the clerks guessed both.*

**THE SWEEP ROW FOR THIS ACT WAS WRONG IN FIVE FIELDS** — her age, her father's forename and both declarants' names. See the corrections page.

events.evidence:
«*…quali hanno dichiarato che a dì **diciannove** del mese corrente di **Febraro**, ad ore **ventuno**, **ANGELA ZIMBARDO**, **MOGLIE DI MATTEO CARFORA**, figlia delli furono **PASQUALE ZIMBARDO, ed ANTONIA SIMINO***». The declarant is «*parente della stessa defonta*».

**SHE IS A PROBLEM FOR A HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HOLDS, AND THE PROBLEM IS NOT SOLVED HERE.** The marriage act of **29 June 1828** makes **FRANCESCO CARFORA** of strada Signorindico «*figlio di **MATTEO CARFORA DEFUNTO** … e di **GRAZIA ZIMBARDO DEFUNTA***», and gives his age as **twenty-eight**, so he was born about **1800**.

**So a Matteo Carfora had a wife GRAZIA Zimbardo who bore a son about 1800, and a Matteo Carfora had a wife ANGELA Zimbardo who died in 1813.** Three readings fit and this archive cannot choose between them:

- **one man, two wives, both Zimbardo** — a widower marrying his late wife's sister was ordinary, and *Pasquale Zimbardo and Antonia Simino* would then be Angela's parents only;
- **one man, one wife, and one of the two acts has her forename wrong** — in which case Angela is Francesco Carfora's mother and he lost her at about thirteen;
- **two different Matteo Carfora**, which the 1828 act itself warns of by naming a *CARFORA MATTEO e CRISCI DIAMANTE* of Santa Maria a Vico.

**The 1828 word was re-read at full resolution on 22 September 2026 before this was written. It says GRAZIA.** So the disagreement is between two documents, not between a document and a bad reading. **This household is published as its own and is NOT merged with Francesco Carfora's.**
